abstract: Aquifers commonly exhibit depth-decaying hydraulic conductivity distributions, reflecting the effects of sediment compaction, cementation, and associated reductions in pore structure with depth. Analytical solutions for groundwater flow in such heterogeneous aquifers are often limited by the nonlinear dependence of transmissivity on hydraulic head. This study develops a novel analytical framework for groundwater flow in an unconfined strip-shaped aquifer with exponentially depth-varying hydraulic conductivity and non-uniform hydraulic heads prescribed along parallel stream boundaries. By introducing the Girinskii discharge potential, the governing nonlinear flow equation is transformed into a linear Poisson equation, enabling application of the superposition principle and Green’s function methodology. A closed-form solution is derived for the discharge potential by combining the well-induced response with the contributions of the stream boundaries, and hydraulic head is subsequently recovered through an explicit inverse transformation involving the Lambert W function. The analytical framework provides a direct representation of flow fields, stream functions, stagnation points, and capture-zone geometries under the combined effects of vertical heterogeneity, pumping, and spatially varying boundary conditions. The proposed formulation encompasses a number of previous analytical solutions as subsets. The steady analytical solution is verified against finite-element simulations, showing close agreement in the predicted hydraulic-head distributions. The formulation is further extended to transient groundwater flow driven by pumping, areal recharge and localized recharge from a circular basin, with close agreement obtained between the predicted temporal evolution of the resulting recharge mound and numerical results. Temporal evolution of stream depletion rates is analyzed under varying degrees of aquifer heterogeneity. The joint effects of the boundary-head slope ratio and hydraulic-conductivity decay exponent are shown to control the size, position, and asymmetry of the well capture zone. A first-order variance-propagation analysis quantifies the contribution of uncertain parameters to hydraulic-head uncertainty, revealing that the dominant uncertainty source changes from reference conductivity under weak heterogeneity to the conductivity-decay parameter under stronger heterogeneity. A parameter estimation procedure is further developed to estimate the vertical decay exponents from perturbed hydraulic-head observations and assess its sensitivity to observational uncertainty. The proposed analytical framework provides a general tool for investigating steady and transient flow, capture-zone delineation, and uncertainty propagation in vertically heterogeneous unconfined aquifer systems.

title: A regime-specialized mixture-of-experts framework with event-driven case memory for daily multi-step streamflow forecasting
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part B Author(s): Jiamu Chen, Jiahua Wei, Minglei Hou, Zhiming Zhang, Jinghao Zhang, Yanqing Shen
abstract: Accurate daily streamflow forecasting is crucial for flood risk monitoring and water resources operation, yet remains challenging due to regime nonstationarity and the scarcity of extreme-high-flow samples. A regime-specialized mixture-of-experts framework (RS-MoE) is proposed, integrating quantile-based regime partitioning, regime-specific experts, and a sparse gating router for streamflow forecasting. An optional event-driven case-memory module (RS-MoE-Mem) is further introduced as a post-routing residual-amplitude correction layer for tail-regime robustness. The framework is first evaluated on four representative stations in the Upper Yellow River for configuration selection and mechanism validation, and is subsequently transferred to 576 CAMELS-US basins for cross-region transferability validation. In the Upper Yellow River, RS-MoE and RS-MoE-Mem improve cross-station mean NSE from 0.860 to 0.863-0.867, raise high-flow NSE from 0.500 to 0.559-0.588 (+11.8% to +17.6%), and reduce high-flow RMSE from 0.064 to 0.059-0.057 (7.8%-10.9%). Lead-time decay is also alleviated, with day-7 NSE increasing from 0.780 to 0.787-0.791. Across 1,728 basin–family pairs, RS–MoE and RS–MoE-Mem achieve statistically significant gains (p ≤ 0.002), raising overall NSE from 0.044 to 0.285–0.295 and high–flow NSE from −0.226 to 0.024–0.070. Relative to RS–MoE, RS–MoE–Mem further improves high–flow NSE by 0.046, reduces high–flow RMSE by ∼0.002, and increases high–flow KGE by 0.039 (all paired differences p < 0.001). Across the three expert families, memory enhancement also reduces peak absolute bias by 0.67–1.21 percentage points and event-volume absolute bias by 1.05–2.10 percentage points. These results extend prior hydrological MoE applications. Attribution analysis and gating-frequency heatmaps reveal that RS-MoE gains tend to be larger in basins with strong streamflow variability, pronounced event-pulse behavior, and sufficient room for improvement, while the routing pattern remains stable and regime-consistent. These results support the transferability and configuration robustness of RS-MoE across regions and expert families.

title: Streamflow prediction in natural ungauged catchments using Temporal Fusion Transformers
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part B Author(s): Rafael Francisco, José Pedro Matos
abstract: Streamflow prediction is essential for water resources management. Classical hydrological models struggle with predictive accuracy and probabilistic representation in ungauged catchments. Recent advances in deep learning have demonstrated notable improvements in reproducing complex time series, such as streamflow, with the Temporal Fusion Transformer (TFT) emerging as a promising model. This study explores the potential of TFTs to predict daily streamflow in natural ungauged catchments in Portugal. Streamflow data from 53 catchments were collected from the national database, while meteorological inputs (precipitation and temperature) were derived from the ERA5-Land reanalysis dataset. Geomorphological descriptors for each catchment were also included. Results are reported on 46 catchments after screening from the initial set based on objective hydrometric and natural-flow criteria and show strong predictive performance and spatial generalization under ungauged conditions. In the test subsets, TFT models in ungauged conditions outperformed the individually calibrated hydrological model Hydrologiska Byråns Vattenbalansavdelning (HBV), securing an advantage in terms of median NSE (increased from 0.46 to 0.50), median KGE (increased from 0.44 to 0.48) and median CRPS (decreased, which is desired, from 5.51 to 3.70 L s − 1 km − 2 ). Model specialization substantially improved performance, reaching a median NSE = 0.62, a median KGE = 0.65, and the median CRPS decreased to 3.20 L s − 1 km − 2 , in selected test portions for this second task. Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) models were also evaluated as a data-driven benchmark, with TFTs achieving competitive performance under ungauged conditions. Additionally, retraining experiments highlight the model’s adaptability, showing that local data, even if limited in number, can be instrumental in further improving predictions. These findings support the application of deep learning in operational settings, such as flood and drought risk management, and water allocation strategies in catchments without comprehensive measurements.

title: Diffusion-Inversion-Net (DIN): an end-to-end direct probabilistic framework for characterizing hydraulic conductivities and quantifying uncertainty
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part B Author(s): Xun Zhang, Weijie Yang, Jiangjiang Zhang, Simin Jiang
abstract: We propose the Diffusion-Inversion-Net (DIN) framework for inverse modeling of groundwater flow and solute transport processes. DIN utilizes an offline-trained Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Model (DDPM) as a prior learner, which flexibly incorporates sparse, multi-source observational data, including hydraulic head, solute concentration, and hard conductivity data, through conditional injection mechanisms. These conditioning inputs subsequently guide the generative inversion process during sampling. After offline training, DIN leverages its probabilistic generative mechanism to directly produce ensembles of posterior parameter fields through repeated stochastic reverse denoising, without requiring online iterative data assimilation or repeated forward simulations for each inversion. Two representative synthetic prior settings, Gaussian and non-Gaussian, are investigated. The results demonstrate that DIN can produce multiple constraint-satisfying realizations under identical observational conditions, accurately estimate hydraulic-conductivity fields, and provide uncertainty diagnostics for the learned conditional ensemble. Additional comparisons with CUNet, CGAN, and ESMDA show that DIN achieves ensemble-mean RMSE values of 0.2500 and 2.385 and SSIM values of 0.9420 and 0.8810 in the representative Gaussian and non-Gaussian cases, respectively, while retaining its conditional sampling capability. The framework further provides an efficient end-to-end probabilistic inversion approach under the synthetic Gaussian and non-Gaussian settings considered in this study, as the major computational cost is amortized to the offline training stage and posterior hydraulic-conductivity samples can be generated without online iterative data assimilation. These results support the feasibility of end-to-end probabilistic groundwater inversion within the fixed synthetic configurations investigated here, with computational costs amortized through offline training. Generalization to different observation geometries, boundary and source conditions, noise models, or geological priors remains untested.

title: Morphology-intensity relationships and long-term evolution of extreme precipitation over China based on an adaptive sector scanning algorithm
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part B Author(s): Zhangrui Xie, Jiejun Huang, Ximing Chen, Yaqi Sun, Han Zhou
abstract: Understanding the spatial morphology of extreme precipitation is crucial for assessing hydrometeorological hazards. We developed an adaptive sector scanning algorithm within a semivariogram framework to characterize extreme precipitation across China using ERA5 daily precipitation data from 1950 to 2024. Extreme precipitation was identified using grid-specific 95th-percentile thresholds. Spatial Precipitation Extent (SPE) was defined as the area enclosed by eight corrected directional effective ranges, while the Anisotropy Ratio (AR) was defined as the ratio of the major to minor axes of a fitted ellipse. We examined the relationships among SPE, AR, precipitation intensity, and their long-term evolution. Results show that both SPE and mean precipitation intensity exhibit a pronounced southeast-to-northwest decreasing gradient across China. High AR values are primarily distributed along major mountain ranges, indicating a close spatial association between topography and the directional anisotropy of annual extreme precipitation. Mean precipitation intensity increases with SPE following a power-law relationship (R2 = 0.948, p < 0.05) but decreases with AR according to a power-law decay (R2 = 0.896, p < 0.05). From 1950 to 2024, SPE declined overall, while precipitation intensity decreased from the 1960 s to the early 1990 s and subsequently recovered in recent decades. Since the early 2000 s, the statistical dependence of precipitation intensity on SPE and AR has weakened. These findings advance understanding of the long-term evolution and spatial concentration of extreme precipitation and support the incorporation of spatial morphology into meteorological early warning and disaster risk reduction.

title: A recursive conditional generative adversarial network for multiphase flow prediction in anisotropic porous media under dynamic constraints
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part B Author(s): Tianyu Yang, Xiang Rao, Kang Wang, Shuhui Xu, Wentao Zhan, Zhong Chen
abstract: Permeability anisotropy and time-varying well controls govern oil-saturation evolution during waterflooding, but repeated high-fidelity simulation is computationally expensive. We propose a recurrent conditional generative adversarial network (R-CGAN) for rapid spatiotemporal prediction of oil-saturation fields under anisotropic permeability and dynamic injection-production controls. A permeability-guided feature-adaptation mechanism captures directional flow behavior, while spatial encodings of well locations, types, and time-varying rates drive recurrent state transitions together with the current reservoir state. Conditional temporal discrimination improves the spatial plausibility and temporal consistency of multistep predictions. A continuous-time refinement module combining continuous-time encoding with feature-wise linear modulation reconstructs intermediate states within each control period. Under an identical recurrent protocol, R-CGAN outperformed four baseline architectures, including the Fourier neural operator (FNO). Relative to FNO, the strongest baseline, it reduced mean absolute error and root mean square error by 9.5% and 9.1%, respectively. Over a 240-day recurrent forecast, structural similarity declined only from 0.9821 to 0.9781. At unsupervised within-period times, continuous-time refinement reduced mean absolute error and root mean square error by 31.8% and 35.4%, respectively, compared with linear interpolation. The model remained accurate for unseen anisotropy strengths, well configurations, well counts, and forecast horizons, and achieved an approximately 223.4-fold online inference speedup relative to finite-volume simulation. These results demonstrate an accurate and efficient surrogate for continuous-time reservoir-state prediction, supporting repeated-evaluation tasks such as history matching and production optimization.

title: Hydraulically constrained event-scale dynamic catchment delineation using multi-temporal backward tracking under design rainfall scenarios: a case study of urban underpass roads in Beijing
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part B Author(s): Qianting Chen, Yongwei Gong, Junru Zhang, Xin Dang, Honghong Shi
abstract: Urban underpass roads are typical low-lying hotspots prone to pluvial flooding; however, existing studies mostly rely on static catchment delineation and do not capture the temporal evolution of event-specific effective contributing areas during rainfall events. This study investigates three representative urban underpass roads within a 657.78 ha study area in Beijing. To address this limitation, this study proposes a multi-temporal backward-tracking algorithm integrating InfoWorks ICM simulation results with topographic data to delineate event-specific effective contributing areas under varying rainfall intensity, duration, and peak coefficient conditions. The framework was evaluated under 30 design rainfall scenarios with varying return periods, durations, and peak rainfall coefficients. Complementing conventional static delineation methods, the proposed framework reconstructs event-specific effective contributing areas using time-varying hydraulic states and prescribed backward-tracking criteria, enabling quantitative characterization of their variability across rainfall scenarios. Results reveal scenario-dependent spatial variability, while catchment boundaries exhibit outward expansion and increasing spatial reorganization under higher return period events. At the system scale, under the baseline delineation configuration, the total event-scale catchment area increased by 462.94 % from the 10- to 20-year return periods, showing a pronounced expansion across this interval. Rainfall intensity showed the strongest influence among the investigated rainfall characteristics on nonlinear contributing-area expansion, whereas longer rainfall duration and delayed peak timing primarily enhanced runoff contributions from distal upstream areas. This study develops an automated framework for reconstructing event-specific effective contributing areas and quantitatively characterizing their spatial evolution under different rainfall conditions, providing a methodological basis for potential runoff-contributing-area identification and event-specific flood-risk assessment in urban underpass roads.

title: Quantifying multidimensional drought risks under climate change: A deep learning-based downscaling and DDF curves approach
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part B Author(s): Xuan Xie, Guohe Huang, Yuke Li, Shuguang Wang, Yurui Fan
abstract: Reliable estimates of future drought characteristics and associated risks are essential for regional water resource planning under climate change. Traditional large-scale precipitation datasets and the derived drought indices, such as the Standardized Precipitation Index (SPI), suffer from limitations in spatial resolution and cannot directly represent actual precipitation deficits or associated water shortages. Moreover, separate analyses of drought duration, severity, and frequency often fail to capture the interdependence among these characteristics. To address these limitations, this study develops an integrated analytical framework that combines multi-criteria GCM selection, deep learning-based ensemble downscaling, and drought Duration-Deficit-Frequency (DDF) analysis. Future precipitation projections at the analyzed stations in the Upper Yangtze River Basin are first generated under four SSP scenarios through the proposed downscaling framework. The downscaled series are then used to construct DDF curves based on the best-fit probability distribution, jointly quantifying drought durations, cumulative precipitation deficits, and return periods. The results indicate that the occurrence of extreme droughts generally exceeds historical levels under future climate scenarios, although the magnitude of change varies substantially among the analyzed stations and across SSP scenarios. DDF analysis further reveals increased cumulative precipitation deficits, particularly for longer-duration drought events. Bootstrap analysis indicates that uncertainty in the DDF curves increases with drought duration and return period, while multilevel factorial analysis (MFA) identifies GCM ensemble configuration and downscaling methodology as the dominant sources of uncertainty. By linking drought-index-based event identification with physical precipitation-deficit quantification, the proposed framework provides a physically interpretable and uncertainty-aware approach for assessing station-specific drought characteristics and associated risks under alternative SSP scenarios.

title: Decoupled ammonia nitrogen and total nitrogen exports under hydroclimatic variability in an alpine headwater catchment of the central Qinghai-Tibet Plateau
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part B Author(s): Xueping Wang, Xiaolin Shui, Yujie Zhang, Xiaohong Zhao, Zhoufeng Wang, Bo Hu, Haixia Zhu
abstract: As the “Asian Water Tower” with a fragile alpine ecosystem, nitrogen loading in the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau (QTP) is critical to the water security of the downstream Yangtze River. This study elucidated the spatiotemporal dynamics and potential factors of nitrogen export in the Tongtian River through long-term monitoring (2015–2024) and seasonal sampling, coupled with Optimal Parameters-based Geographical Detector (OPGD) analysis. The results revealed a distinct temporal decoupling between ammonia nitrogen (NH3-N) and total nitrogen (TN). TN concentration and flux exhibited a persistent upward trend (p 0.05), whereas its flux exhibited a significant upward trend (p < 0.01), a signal captured only after controlling for intra-annual variability. TN concentrations were highest in the spring campaign (1.71 mg/L), while the NH3-N campaign mean was highest in summer (0.26 mg/L) and close to the autumn and winter means. OPGD identified cropland as the factor with the highest explanatory power for NH3-N concentration (q = 0.54) and pH as the primary explanatory factor for TN concentration (q = 0.53). Suspended sediment concentration had the highest explanatory power for NH3-N flux (q = 0.56), whereas TN flux was predominantly associated with pH and suspended sediment concentration (q = 0.74 and 0.71, p < 0.001). Interaction analysis further indicated joint associations of land-use, hydro-meteorological, and suspended sediment variables with temporal variability in nitrogen export. The contrasting nitrogen patterns may reflect differences in catchment inputs, hydrological transport, and temperature-dependent transformations. Therefore, management strategies must shift from passive concentration monitoring to actively decoupling anthropogenic practice from peak hydro-sedimentary windows.

title: Irrigation water abstraction as a hidden amplifier of river pollution: observation-based empirical evidence from a dual-river system in central China
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part B Author(s): Guoshuai Zhang, Peng Zhang, Min Xu, Yanxue Xu, Yue Zhao
abstract: Irrigation abstraction reduces dilution capacity for loads entering below an offtake. In China’s Yiluo River Basin, we quantified this loss using the Amplification Factor (AF), the ratio of no-diversion to residual discharge, computed from measured river and diversion discharges without hydrological modeling. AF equals a concentration ratio only for a fixed load entering below the offtake and not removed by diversion; it does not by itself estimate actual concentration change. Irrigation-season AF averaged 2.33 (Yi River) and 2.53 (Luo River), with single-day maxima of 12.6 and 11.9. Concentration responses were assessed using evidence not algebraically derived from AF. On irrigation-season dry days, the NH3-N coefficient was positive under all seven seasonal specifications (temperature-adjusted primary model: β = +0.115 per unit log(Qdiv + 1), p = 0.016) but weakened under calendar-based controls (p = 0.06–0.21), so we regard it as supportive rather than confirmatory evidence; residual seasonal confounding cannot be excluded. Absolute specific conductance was positively associated with abstraction (p = 0.0024–0.0042), whereas the downstream/upstream ratio was not significant (p = 0.119); these results are consistent with dilution-capacity loss but do not independently validate the mechanism. The Yi River, with concentrated abstraction, is least affected by known return-flow pathways; the Luo River is a composite multi-diversion system. Assumed gauging errors yielded AF uncertainty of ±11–12%, excluding structural and scenario uncertainty. Lagging diversion discharge by 1–3 days changed irrigation-season mean AF by less than 3%, whereas daily AF differed by more than 10% on 12–39% of days.

title: Climate change induced hydrological regime shifts in the transboundary Zarafshon River Basin in Central Asia
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part B Author(s): Sonu Khanal, Philip Kraaijenbrink, Faezeh Nick, Joel Fiddes, Arthur Lutz, Evan Miles, Esteban Garcia, Brecht Haeyer, Johannes Hunink, Walter Immerzeel
abstract: Mountain river basins in Central Asia are highly sensitive to climate-driven changes in snow and glacier melt, yet the magnitude and timing of the resulting hydrological regime shifts remain poorly quantified. To address this gap, we assess present and future hydrological shifts in the transboundary Zarafshon River Basin with the SPHY glacio-hydrological model. We improved the representation of snowmelt and snow infiltration, which redistributes water to delayed baseflow and improves winter and spring discharge. We calibrated the improved model against discharge observations, satellite-derived snow cover and glacier mass balance data through Monte Carlo optimization. Over 1991–2020, snowmelt dominates runoff (52.4%), followed by baseflow (23.3%) and rainfall-runoff (21.1%), whereas glacier melt contributes 3.2% but sustains late-summer low flows. Snow and glacier melt dominate the upstream hydrology, whereas rainfall-runoff and baseflow sustain the flow in the lower basin. Using downscaled ISIMIP3b climate scenarios, we project glacier volume to decline by ∼ 40% under SSP126 and ∼ 80% under SSP585 by 2100. Annual total runoff declines by less than 7% in all scenarios, because gains in rainfall-runoff and baseflow almost offset the melt loss. Peak total runoff declines by 22.6% under SSP585, and the annual peak discharge shifts earlier by 22–38 days. The hydrological regime shift from snowmelt to rainfall-runoff is more pronounced in the Fondarya than in the Matcha River system. These results indicate a shift from a snowmelt to a rainfall-runoff dominated hydrological regime. Such a shift would reduce summer water availability and increase irrigation stress, highlighting the need for adaptive management.

title: Phosphorus composition in urban estuarine sediments: similar spatial patterns, distinct seasonal drivers, transformation pathways and risks
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part B Author(s): Zhaoying Chen, Zhaokui Ni, Shuaishuai Zhou, Taotao Sun, Yue Wu, Yu Ma, Jixin Yang, Shuai Liu, Andrea Critto, Shengrui Wang
abstract: Estuaries are global biogeochemical hotspots threatened by phosphorus (P)-driven eutrophication. Although sediments serve as major P reservoirs, its molecular composition, influencing factors, transformation pathways, and environmental risks remain poorly understood. This study analyzed these aspects in the Shenzhen Estuary using 31P NMR, UV–Vis spectroscopy, EEM fluorescence, and microbial high-throughput sequencing. Results showed a consistent river-to-bay gradient, with the content of total P (TP), inorganic P (IP), Ortho–P, Mono–P (myo–IHP, scyllo–IHP, α–Gly, RNA–nmp), and Di–P (DNA–P) decreasing seaward, while the proportion of organic P (OP, 17.6 ± 7.3%) increased in both dry and wet periods. Despite similar spatial patterns, influencing factors, transformation pathways, and environmental risks differed markedly between seasons. Dry-period P components were primarily associated with microbial communities and organic matter (OM) properties, whereas wet-period patterns were closely related to OM properties and sources, as well as to microbial α-diversity. Spatially P transformation pathways were identified: river sediments favored OP mineralization (Mono–P/Di–P → Ortho–P), while bay sediments showed net assimilation (Ortho–P → Mono–P/Di–P) in the dry period; Ortho–P was converted to OP via biological uptake in the wet period. We developed a novel Phosphorus Environmental Risk Index (PERI) integrating P components and biotic/abiotic influencing factors. PERI values were significantly higher in river zones than bay regardless of season, and consistently higher in the wet period. These findings establish a framework for understanding sediment P dynamics and provide a risk–assessment tool for P management in estuaries.

title: Future exposure to dry and moist heat extremes linked to soil moisture regulation
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part B Author(s): Jingwei Zhou, Dragan Milošević, Adriaan J. Teuling
abstract: Extreme heatwaves pose escalating threats to ecosystems and human populations worldwide, yet comparative analyses of soil moisture impacts on both dry and moist heatwave types remain limited. Here, using multi-model climate simulations globally, we quantify how land–atmosphere interactions modulate dry versus moist heatwave intensification and consequent population exposure patterns. Unprecedented increases of both dry and moist heatwave magnitude are found across mid-latitude regions, with most regions already surpassing the 2 °C Paris Agreement threshold and certain regions exceeding 6 °C, relative to pre-industrial conditions. Dry heatwaves consistently exhibit greater intensification and trends than moist heatwaves. Soil moisture dynamics generally induce more changes in dry heatwaves relative to moist heatwaves. It is suggested that, northern parts of South America, Arabian Peninsula, and South Asia, are exposed to more severe dry and moist heatwaves in the future period (2040–2070) compared with other regions. Most places are experiencing increasing population exposure to heatwaves, with 30% more population in African regions exposed to severe moist heatwaves. Soil moisture amplifies population exposure in most places except in Arabian Peninsula. These findings demonstrate how region-specific land–atmosphere feedbacks modulate dry versus moist heatwave intensification, underscoring the necessity of incorporating such feedbacks to accurately quantify risks of two types of heatwaves and inform targeted adaptation strategies.

title: Biogeochemical controls on N 2 O emission factors across a river-estuary continuum: nonlinear nitrate dependence and an underrecognized role of phosphorus
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part B Author(s): Sibo Zhang, Lei Gu, Xinxiao Wu, Xiaokang Li, Chunming Li, Jie Zhang, Zhihao Xu, William H. McDowell, Xinghui Xia
abstract: The IPCC framework assigns the same default emission factor of 0.26% to the riverine and estuarine components of indirect N2O emissions, despite substantial biogeochemical variability within these aquatic systems. We examined EF5 along the Pearl River-estuary continuum during three seasonal sampling campaigns and evaluated its environmental predictors using machine learning, supplemented by winter N2O isotopocule and metagenomic analyses. Winter isotopocule-based estimates indicated that denitrification-related processes accounted for > 89% of N2O production. EF5, defined as the dissolved N2O-N:NO3 –-N concentration ratio, ranged from 0.02% to 0.38% (median 0.06%), and nitrate emerged as its leading predictor. EF5 declined sharply with increasing nitrate at low concentrations but more gradually at higher concentrations. At higher nitrate concentrations, increasing N2O concentration evidently weakened the EF5 decline expected from denominator coupling alone. This concentration dependence helps explain the greater predictive contribution of nitrate in estuarine waters, where nitrate concentrations were lower. TP and TN:TP were also important EF5 predictors, with the TN:TP ratio exceeding the Redfield molar ratio of 16:1 in 99.1% of observations. Higher TP was associated with lower predicted EF5 and positively correlated with the relative abundances of genes involved not only in denitrification but also in nitrate assimilation and DNRA, suggesting greater potential for nitrate utilization through pathways that do not directly produce N2O. The positive TN:TP-EF5 relationship in riverine waters may partly reflect wastewater-related N:P imbalance and dissolved N2O inputs. A global compilation comprising 3,560 riverine and 254 estuarine observations revealed broadly comparable median EF5 values (0.08% and 0.11%, respectively) between these two systems, both below the IPCC default, but river-estuary contrasts varied with latitude. These findings support EF5 parameterizations incorporating nitrate concentration dependence and phosphorus-related nutrient conditions.

title: Soil moisture sensor networks for advancing understanding of hillslope and catchment hydrology: a review
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part B Author(s): Yangkai Zhang, Erqing Wang, Yuhan Guo, Hu Liu, Jie Tian, Ying Zhao, Carlos R. Mello, Yan Liu, Li Guo
abstract: Soil moisture sensor networks (SMSNs) provide continuous, depth-resolved observations that help elucidate hydropedological processes: coupled soil–water interactions through which soil properties influence water storage, flow pathways, and redistribution across hillslopes and catchments. Because these processes vary across space, time, and depth, isolated measurements are often insufficient for mechanistic interpretation and model evaluation. This review synthesizes SMSN deployment strategies and applications across five domains: (1) soil water storage patterns; (2) soil water fluxes and runoff generation; (3) ecohydrological coupling; (4) land–atmosphere water and heat exchange; and (5) multi-source data fusion, assimilation, and validation. We compare four representative case groups: the Heihe Watershed Allied Telemetry Experimental Research (HiWATER) middle-reach oasis area in northwestern China; the Pailugou watershed in China’s Qilian Mountains; Terrestrial Environmental Observatories (TERENO) catchments and related sites in Germany and Italy; and the Shale Hills Critical Zone Observatory in the United States. These cases illustrate how environmental settings and network configurations shape process observability, cross-scale integration, and model evaluation. We examine limitations arising from sensor stability, installation disturbance, spatial representativeness, long-term operation, data quality, uncertainty, and the indirect nature of process inference. The synthesis links network design to observable process signatures and identifies priorities for integrating complementary observations. It provides guidance for designing SMSNs that support reliable interpretation of hillslope and catchment hydropedological processes.

title: Flow velocity drives divergent functional and structural responses in a rheophilic Yangtze fish: implications for aquatic ecosystem management
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part B Author(s): Waleed Afzal Naveed, Mian Adnan Kakakhel, Xiaotao Shi, Jiang Zewen
abstract: Altered flow regimes caused by dams and hydropower operations can modify hydraulic conditions experienced by riverine fishes, yet the biological consequences of graded water velocity across multiple levels of organisation remain poorly understood. This study investigated the responses of juvenile Coreius guichenoti to four water velocity regimes (control, low, medium, and high) during repeated exposure over seven days. Swimming performance, behaviour, oxidative status, innate immune responses, inflammatory cytokines, and white muscle histopathology were evaluated, and machine-learning models were used to assess integrated response patterns. Medium velocity increased critical swimming speed, antioxidant enzyme activities, lysozyme activity, and serum immunoglobulin M, whereas high velocity reduced swimming capacity and increased cortisol, lipid peroxidation, pro-inflammatory cytokine expression, and refuge-seeking behaviour. In contrast to these non-monotonic physiological responses, muscle pathology increased progressively with velocity. A random forest classifier achieved 90% cross-validated accuracy in distinguishing velocity treatments, while physiological biomarkers explained 36% of the variation in individual swimming performance. These findings demonstrate that altered hydraulic conditions can elicit divergent functional and structural responses in rheophilic fish, highlighting the need to incorporate biological response thresholds and hydraulic refugia into environmental flow assessment and management.

title: Sedimentary reorganization under sediment starvation and morphological restructuring in a human-modified mega-estuary
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part B Author(s): Dezheng Liu, Ziyun Xu, Ruiqi Chen, Sihao Mo, Liangwen Jia, Eunji Byun, Yan Miao, Haotian Wu
abstract: Estuaries worldwide are experiencing unprecedented anthropogenic pressures. However, the compound effects of sediment starvation and local morphological alterations on estuarine systems remain incompletely understood. The Lingdingyang Bay (LDB) of the Pearl River Estuary as a case study, this research integrates sedimentary records, long-term hydrological observations, and bathymetric data to reveal the estuarine response to multiple human stressors. Our findings indicate an abrupt and systemic shift in the estuarine hydrodynamic and sedimentary regime during the mid-1990 s. This shift was primarily driven by two concurrent factors: a ∼ 39% reduction in fluvial sediment supply due to upstream damming, which deprived the estuary of its natural sedimentary compensation, and high-intensity localized engineering (e.g., channel dredging and land reclamation). These morphological modifications leading to a persistent increase in the tidal range by over 30%. Driven by these combined impacts, the LDB underwent a source-sink reorganization, transitioning from a naturally efficient sediment sink to a human-regulated state characterized by internal erosion and localized deposition. The sustained increase in coarse-grained fractions and high-energy geochemical indicators in sedimentary records further reflects enhanced sediment reworking and bed-material winnowing. This study provides a observational framework for understanding how the coupled impacts of sediment starvation and localized morphological changes drive persistent shifts in highly modified mega-estuaries.

title: Long-horizon cascade reservoir scheduling with a multiscale constraint-consistent hybrid transformer
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part B Author(s): Changqing Meng, Chunzhe Wang, Yanke Zhang, Yuankun Wang, Chao Wang, Guoyong Zhang, Yongqiang Wang
abstract: Long-horizon cascade reservoir scheduling is challenging because annual release trajectories must satisfy hydraulic consistency and operating constraints across strongly coupled reservoirs, while repeated deterministic optimization is computationally expensive. This study develops a Multiscale Constraint-Consistent Hybrid Transformer (MCC-HT), in which hydraulic consistency is embedded during trajectory generation and reservoir-level operating requirements are further reconciled through an Iterative Cumulative Rebalancing (ICR) mechanism. The framework was evaluated for the lower Jinsha River–Three Gorges six-reservoir cascade using a 64-year ten-day inflow record (1959–2022) under a deterministic hindcast setting, with comparisons against the Progressive Optimality Algorithm (POA), Particle Swarm Optimization, and two ablation variants. Over the 2015–2022 test period, MCC-HT generated annual schedules that remained consistent with the prescribed operating requirements, while reducing the average runtime for full annual schedule generation from 664.55 s for POA to 2.79 s. Under this substantial computational reduction, MCC-HT approximated the annual generation achieved by POA, with a mean difference of +0.12% that varied with hydrological conditions across individual years. Ablation results further indicate that embedded constraint handling contributes more consistently across hydrological conditions, whereas the benefit of multiscale inflow representation is more condition-dependent. These results show that structural embedding of physical constraints can support efficient and physically admissible long-horizon cascade scheduling, providing a practical basis for repeated annual scenario evaluation in strongly coupled hydro-systems.

title: Constraint-driven generation of virtual urban drainage networks for refined urban inundation simulation
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part B Author(s): Zihao Zhang, Yan Gao, Quan Yuan, Xiaohan Li, Yuchao Jiang, Le Sun
abstract: Detailed drainage-network data are often unavailable in data-scarce cities, limiting refined urban inundation modeling. This study proposes a constraint-driven method for generating virtual urban drainage networks for one-dimensional and two-dimensional (1D–2D) coupled hydrodynamic simulation. The method extracts an equal-density network skeleton from urban roads, routes pipe elevations under minimum-cover and maximum-excavation-depth constraints, and assigns hierarchical pipe diameters using empirical quantiles of edge betweenness centrality. The framework was evaluated on Xiaohengqin Island, China, using SWMM–LISFLOOD-FP and an extreme rainfall event induced by Typhoon Yangliu in 2025. The generated network achieved a spatial topological matching F1 score of 0.8812 against the surveyed drainage network, and 87.41% of matched pipe segments had relative diameter errors within 50%. The proposed model also reproduced the distribution of 13 recorded inundation locations. Using the surveyed-network simulation as an independent hydrodynamic reference, the virtual-network simulation achieved a critical success index of 0.670 and an F1 score of 0.803 for inundation extent across 120,976 valid road-corridor cells. The RMSE and MAE of maximum water depth were 0.073 and 0.046 m, respectively, with a squared Pearson correlation coefficient ( R 2 ) of 0.811. At six locations with observed maximum depths, the RMSE was 2.15 cm and Pearson’s r was 0.981 ( R 2 = 0.962). Overall, the method provides an engineering-constrained drainage-network representation suitable for event-scale urban inundation modeling where detailed network data are unavailable.

title: From pollution-driven to process-regulated: A decade of ecological restoration reshapes CO 2 fluxes in a heavily polluted urban stream
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part B Author(s): Yingxue Pu, Xiaofeng Wang, Yuewei Zhang, Yixin He, Tingting Liu, Shuangshuang Liu, Jilong Wang, Honglin Chen, Yuan Zeng, Zuolin Xiao
abstract: Heavily polluted rivers are significant hotspots of CO2 emissions, yet how long-term ecological restoration alters these emissions and their biogeochemical drivers remain poorly understood. Here, we conducted a decade-long field investigation of CO2 concentrations and fluxes in a heavily polluted urban stream in Chongqing, China, spanning successive restoration periods: baseline polluted stage (2014), point-source wastewater interception stage (2018) and ecological restoration stage (2023). Integrating hydrochemical monitoring, machine-learning modeling, and a normalized mitigation-efficiency framework, we evaluated CO2 flux dynamics and underlying control mechanism shifts throughout long-term eco-restoration. Over the ten-year restoration period, dissolved CO2 concentrations and fluxes decreased by 76.0% and 72.4%, respectively, demonstrating substantial climate co-benefits alongside water-quality restoration. This reduction was primarily driven by substantial decreases in organic carbon and nutrient loads alongside improved dissolved oxygen and pH. Crucially, CO2 fluxes in this urban stream shifted from being driven by excessive organic carbon supply (carbon-overloaded regime in 2014) to pH and nitrogen constraints after wastewater interception (2018), and ultimately to phosphorus limitation and oxygen regulation following ecological restoration (2023). This result highlights that controlling mechanisms of urban stream CO2 emissions exhibit clear stage-dependent and shift from carbon-saturated, heterotrophic regime to nutrient-limited internal metabolism. Normalized mitigation-efficiency analyses further revealed that reductions in organic carbon and nitrogen yielded higher CO2 mitigation benefits per unit pollutant removed than phosphorus reduction. Although residual CO2 emissions remain higher than those in less disturbed rivers due to legacy effects from historical pollution, these findings demonstrate that restoration not only suppresses urban river CO2 emissions but also fundamentally restructures their biogeochemical controls from substrate-driven to process-regulated systems, providing a scientific basis for optimizing co-benefits of water quality and climate mitigation.

title: Hydrological forcing reshapes nitrogen partitioning under microplastic amendment in hyporheic zones
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part B Author(s): Shiqi Liu, Zhenhua Yan, Tao Zhang, Xi Chen, Lan Ma, Yuqiong Yang, Ping Lu, Saiyu Yuan, Guanghua Lu
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) are increasingly recognized as potential modifiers of nitrogen (N) cycling in aquatic sediments. Hyporheic zones (HZs), hotspots for riverine N transformation and important sinks for MPs, are exposed to dynamic hydrological forcing. However, how hydrological forcing structures N transformation responses in MP-amended HZs remains poorly understood. Here, we used field-collected sediments to simulate HZs and examined N transformation responses in sediments amended with conventional polyvinyl chloride (PVC) and biodegradable polylactic acid (PLA) MPs under contrasting drying-rewetting alternation (DWA) regimes and hydraulic retention time (HRT) levels. DWA enhanced sediment reoxygenation, weakened dissolved oxygen (DO) stratification, and altered putative nitrification-related taxa, enzyme-associated protein responses, and selected N-cycling functional genes in a polymer-specific manner. In PVC-amended HZs, DWA strengthened the coupling between nitrification-related responses and apparent nitrate reduction, whereas in PLA-amended HZs it promoted oxidative N transformation indicators but reduced apparent nitrate reduction, NO2 − accumulation, and NH4 + accumulation. Longer HRT reduced DO availability and generally increased apparent NO3 − reduction. In PVC-amended HZs, this was accompanied by greater NO2 − and NH4 + accumulation. In PLA-amended HZs, higher dissolved organic carbon (DOC) availability and sustained low-DO conditions coincided with greater apparent NO3 − reduction and stronger NO2 − and NH4 + accumulation. Multivariate analyses identified DO-centered associations under DWA and PVC-HRT, whereas DOC-centered associations emerged under PLA-HRT. These findings show that hydrological regime and polymer identity jointly structure N transformation responses in MP-amended HZs, with distinct patterns associated with oxygen availability, carbon availability, and nitrate-derived N partitioning.

title: INFO-LAX: an interpretable and uncertainty-aware framework for monthly rainfall erosivity estimation
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part B Author(s): Jinhui Yuan, Yuefeng Lu, Zhengqi Song, Liguo Dong, Miao Lu, Weijun Zhao, Zhixiang Lu, Kun Liu
abstract: Rainfall erosivity (R factor) is a dynamic climatic driver of soil erosion, yet monthly estimation is complicated by nonlinear daily rainfall aggregation, strong upper tail behavior, and the limited interpretability and uncertainty characterization of many data driven models. We developed INFO-LAX as an integrated application framework combining two LSTM-Attention encoders, a low weight XGBoost correction branch, and the Weighted Mean of Vectors optimizer. Daily NOAA/NCEI observations from 25 stations across five climate geomorphic regions of China were converted to monthly predictors and daily data derived R factors. Only observed records were used and were partitioned chronologically into training (1975–2008), validation (2009–2014), testing (2015–2020), and temporal holdout (2021–2024) periods. On the independent test set, INFO-LAX achieved R2 = 0.8842, MAE = 95.837, and RMSE = 251.728 MJ·mm·ha−1·h−1, ranking first among RF, GPR, GAM, TFT, and TCN. End-to-end grouped Shapley analysis attributed 55.8% of model contribution to precipitation, followed by dew point (20.5%) and temperature (20.4%). The 95% prediction interval achieved PICP values of 0.952 and 0.978 on the test and temporal holdout sets, respectively. For test Q95 events, Tail MAE was 529.466 MJ·mm·ha−1·h−1 and recall was 0.843, although the peak magnitude ratio of 0.763 indicated conservative estimation of the largest events. INFO-LAX advances monthly R-factor estimation by integrating nonlinear daily-to-monthly representation, model-wide attribution, upper-tail evaluation, and calibrated uncertainty, supporting reconstruction, gap filling, risk assessment, near-real-time updating, and meteorological forcing for future soil erosion digital twins.

title: Interpretable soil moisture drought forecasting using graph attention networks
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part B Author(s): Ye Tuo, Moritz Wirthensohn, Hongliang Ma, Francesco Avanzi
abstract: Accurate and interpretable soil moisture drought forecasting supports hydrological management. Capturing spatial and seasonal drought variability while interpreting learned dependencies remains challenging for data-driven models. This study assesses a domain-informed Graph Attention Network (GAT) to forecast soil moisture drought one-week-ahead by representing hydrological response units (HRUs) as a graph. A retrospective ensemble-based benchmark using 200 independently trained models evaluates predictive performance, spatiotemporal drought-pattern reproduction, and interpretability through feature importance and attention analyses. GAT achieves high F1 scores and a modest but spatially coherent improvement over an LSTM baseline, with the largest gains at lower elevations and reduced performance for both models in high-elevation headwaters. In full-record diagnostics, GAT better reproduces observed drought patterns, particularly in summer, with closer agreement in basin-wide drought frequency and reduced bias. Permutation-based feature importance identifies evaporative-demand variables and topographic features as important predictors with distinct spatial and temporal roles. Attention analyses show that HRU-graph connectivity shapes the dominant spatial attention pattern, while attention weights locally and seasonally reweight connected-source contributions in ways consistent with elevation-dependent input dynamics. A complementary assessment combines chronological train-validation-test separation with different soil moisture input configurations. GAT achieves highest F1 scores among the learned models, and soil moisture benefits the graph models more strongly than LSTM. However, none exceeds persistence in basin-level F1 during the withheld test period. These findings support GAT’s diagnostic value for examining reproducible spatiotemporal patterns in model behavior alongside predictive performance, while operational application requires further development and evaluation against persistence.

title: Improving hydrologic prediction and interpretability through physics-informed dual-output LSTM with water and energy balance constraints
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part B Author(s): Gopeshwar Sahu, Ashutosh Sharma
abstract: Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) has demonstrated strong predictive skill in hydrological modelling, but often lacks physical consistency and interpretability. The Mass-conserving LSTM (MC-LSTM) overcomes this limitation by enforcing water balance, yet the existing formulations remain restricted to single-variable prediction and simplified representation of hydrological fluxes. This study proposes a Physics-Informed Dual-Output LSTM (PIDuaL) that simultaneously predicts streamflow and evapotranspiration (ET) through a modified mass-balance structure. Three constrained variants are further developed by enforcing water balance, energy balance, and combined water and energy balance within the PIDuaL framework. For fair benchmark comparison, a purely data-driven Dual-LSTM is also implemented. Across 149 human-influenced watersheds in India, LSTM and Dual-LSTM show lower streamflow skill, with a median Nash-Sutcliffe efficiency (NSE) of 0.58, whereas MC-LSTM and PIDuaL improve performance to a median NSE of 0.67. Performance gains are most pronounced in hydrologically challenging conditions, including semi-arid and highly human-influenced watersheds, where purely data-driven models struggle. PIDuaL substantially reduces bias, and its constrained variants exhibit the largest improvement in low-flow simulation, accompanied by stronger correlation with baseflow-governing attributes, indicating physically meaningful recession dynamics. Although ET performance is slightly reduced relative to the purely data-driven Dual-LSTM, all physics-informed models maintain satisfactory skill, with median NSE values of at least 0.69 and correlation coefficients of 0.89 or higher. Importantly, PIDuaL internal states exhibit strong correspondence with independent soil moisture and GRACE-based storage anomalies, demonstrating enhanced interpretability. Overall, the results demonstrate that the proposed physics-informed dual-output framework improves predictive accuracy under hydrologically challenging conditions while enhancing physical consistency and model interpretability.

title: Climate-driven shift from glacial to pluvial groundwater contributions in a central Nepal Himalayan catchment
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part B Author(s): Caroline Aubry-Wake, Philip Kraaijenbrink, Walter Immerzeel
abstract: Mountain river systems integrate water from rainfall, seasonal snowmelt, and glacier melt, yet most hydrological models mix these sources with flow pathways, limiting the ability to diagnose how climate-driven changes propagate through surface and subsurface stores. Here we extend the SPHY model with a source-explicit groundwater framework that preserves the climatic origin of water through subsurface storage, allowing groundwater recharge and discharge to be attributed to rainfall, seasonal snowmelt, and glacier melt. The model is evaluated against observations from 2014 to 2024 in the glacierized Langshisha Basin in the Nepal Himalaya and subsequently forced with bias-corrected ISIMIP3b climate projections under three SSP scenarios through 2099. Across all scenarios, annual discharge changes modestly (−10 to − 24% by 2099), but its composition shifts almost completely. Glacier melt, which currently supplies ∼ 41% of streamflow, declines to 13–16% by late century, and glacier-derived groundwater falls from ∼ 18% to 6–7%. Rainfall becomes the dominant water source, increasing from ∼ 31% today to 65–74% in 2090–2099. Despite this major shift in water sources, total groundwater discharge remains comparatively stable because declining glacier-derived recharge is increasingly replaced by rainfall-derived recharge. Under strong warming (SSP5-8.5), the basin shifts from a melt-supported July peak to an autumn, rainfall-dominated regime. By preserving source identity through subsurface storage and discharge, the framework reveals a transition from glacier-supported to rainfall-supported groundwater that is obscured when groundwater is represented solely as baseflow, providing a clearer diagnosis of how mountain water supplies respond to climate change.

title: Molecular compositions and hydrological features govern dissolved organic phosphorus transport and transformation in rivers across different climate zones
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part B Author(s): Peipei Zhang, Qibiao Yu, Fenfang Wang, Jianing Wang, Dongsheng Wang, Weijin Yan, Dingjiang Chen
abstract: Dissolved organic phosphorus (DOP) is a potentially bioavailable component of riverine phosphorus export, yet the molecular controls on its uptake and their coupling with hydrological transport remain poorly constrained. Here, we integrated Fourier-transform ion cyclotron resonance mass spectrometry, incubations, and nutrient-spiraling metrics across heterogeneous rivers and estuaries spanning five river basins of eastern China. DOP accounted for 5.79–86.6% (mean: 31.6% ± 13.2%) of total phosphorus, with concentrations and molecular composition varying with river size and land use. DOP concentrations decreased from headwater streams to mainstems and rose with agricultural and urban land proportions; forest rivers were relatively enriched in highly unsaturated compounds, whereas agricultural and urban rivers were enriched in labile peptides and CHOP-class compounds. We developed a molecular lability index (LI-DOP) integrating H/C, O/C, and molecular mass. LI-DOP explained 60% of the observed variation in uptake velocity (Vf, 0.19–0.79 m d-1) and was retained in the optimal model of riverine turnover rate (k, 0.02–0.28 d-1) together with discharge and DOP concentration. These quantitative relationships indicate that DOP processing reflects molecular composition in conjunction with hydrological and chemical conditions and cannot be adequately characterized by DOP concentration alone. Moreover, DOP conversion potentially contributed 9.61–40.2% (20.9 ± 8.26%) of dissolved inorganic phosphorus at river scales. These estimates suggest in-river DOP conversion may constitute an important internal source of bioavailable phosphorus, while DOP escaping conversion may be exported downstream and support phosphorus availability in estuaries. These findings support incorporating DOP molecular composition and transformation into river-estuary phosphorus assessments.

title: Improving actual evapotranspiration change attribution in Yellow River Basin water conservation area using an observation-constrained two-step framework
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part A Author(s): Shaohui Chen
abstract: Attributing actual evapotranspiration (ET) changes (ETCs) in complex basins remains challenging due to correlated drivers and heterogeneous responses. This study develops a dynamic observation-constrained two-step framework to quantify the contributions of 13 drivers to ETCs in the Yellow River Basin water conservation area (YRB WCA) during 2000–2019. First, Bayesian model fusion integrates five ET products under in situ observation constraints, with spatially and temporally varying weights predicted by random forest using satellite-derived surface conditions. Second, eigen-transformation constructs an orthogonal regression basis from standardized predictors, reducing redundancy among retained components. Across five sites, leave-one-year-out cross-validation yields a pooled root mean square error (RMSE) of 17.13 mm·month−1 and a pooled coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.7216, which is comparable to the best-performing individual products. By dynamically integrating the complementary performance strengths of multiple ET products, the framework reduces reliance on any single product, thereby providing spatially complete ET estimates for regional ETC attribution. Attribution results show that soil moisture, fractional vegetation cover, albedo, and precipitation are dominant factors, with regional mean absolute contributions (RMCs) of 11–14.8%, followed by leaf area index, wind speed, Lwnet and Swnet as moderate regulators, with RMCs of 6.7–9.6%, whereas temperature variables, specific humidity, and pressure act as secondary influencers, with RMCs < 6%. Driver contributions exhibit pronounced spatial heterogeneity and bidirectionality across YRB WCA, reflecting the combined effects of estimated sensitivities and driver trends.

title: Short-term forecasting from GRACE data via dynamic mode decomposition with sequential update
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part A Author(s): V. Ciriello, G. Libero, D.M. Tartakovsky
abstract: Dynamical systems theory is often used for short-term forecasting of hydrologic processes, because it preserves physical interpretability while remaining computationally efficient. One of its tools, dynamic mode decomposition (DMD), provides a modal representation of high-dimensional systems capable of capturing dominant spatiotemporal dynamics in observed data. We investigate the ability of xDMD, a DMD variant that allows for inhomogeneous dynamics, to predict short-term anomalies in basin-averaged total water storage across 15 major river basins worldwide. We compare global and basin-scale training strategies and evaluate the impact of sequential retraining frequency. Our results demonstrate that globally trained models with sequential updating on average outperform basin-scale approaches, indicating that spatial coherence provides a more stable and representative modal basis for temporal extrapolation. Periodic retraining is essential to accommodate gradual evolution of the temporal coefficients and to maintain the robust forecast capacity for update intervals of up to six months. Extension of the retraining interval to annual updates degrades the performance, suggesting the emergence of non-autonomous behavior in some systems and linking the prediction horizon of the xDMD-based forecast to the drift time scale of the temporal coefficients of each basin. A benchmark against recurrent LSTM-GRU networks confirms markedly smaller systematic biases at a fraction of the computational cost. A sliding-window spectral diagnostic confirms that the non-autonomous behavior is almost entirely confined to the temporal coefficients of a nearly time-invariant spatial basis, and provides a transferable, a-priori criterion for selecting the model-updating strategy for generic spatiotemporal signals.

title: High-frequency monitoring and reconstruction of lake water temperature with meteorological observations
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part A Author(s): Hanxiao Yuan, Songtao Ai, Changhong Hu, Runchuan Ouyang, Shoukat Ali Shah, Xinde Chu, Qiuhua Tang, Wolfgang Rack, Christo Pimpirev
abstract: Lakes, as vital components of land water systems, play crucial roles in local climate regulation and ecological functions. Water temperature is a key indicator of lake thermal dynamics and climate sensitivity, while its high-frequency variations and coupling mechanisms with meteorological drivers remain insufficiently understood, especially under extreme weather conditions. To bridge this gap, we conducted a detailed investigation of Qinghai Lake using high-resolution (1 h interval) observations of water temperature and meteorological variables from October 2023 to October 2024. We developed a comprehensive analytical framework incorporating statistical analysis, wavelet time–frequency decomposition, anomaly detection, and deep learning-based reconstruction. The results reveal a strong nonlinear relationship between water and air temperature, as demonstrated by RAPS trend analysis and S-curve regression (R2 = 0.82). Wavelet coherence analysis indicates robust coupling at diurnal and synoptic timescales, with a distinct temporal lag in the lake’s thermal response to atmospheric forcing. Anomaly detection further highlights the critical role of strong wind and precipitation in driving abrupt water temperature shifts. To improve reconstruction performance, we propose a novel PCA-GRU-MA model, which integrates Principal Component Analysis (PCA), Gated Recurrent Units (GRU), and Multi-Head Attention mechanisms (MA). Model validation demonstrates superior accuracy compared to seven benchmark models (RMSE = 1.55 °C, MAE = 1.15 °C, NSE = 0.94), underscoring its capacity to capture thermal anomalies and effectiveness in reconstructing hourly water temperature. This study advances the understanding of high-resolution lake thermal dynamics and offers a methodological foundation for lake ecosystem management, climate change adaptation, and early-warning systems.

title: Simultaneous Bayesian quantification and decomposition of structural, parameter, and forcing uncertainty in hydrologic models: A blended model approach
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part A Author(s): Rezgar Arabzadeh, James Craig, Bryan Tolson, Jonathan Romero-Cuellar, Robert Chlumsky
abstract: Disentangling the contributions of structural, parametric, and forcing uncertainty to hydrological model predictions remains a long-standing challenge. This study proposes a unified Bayesian framework that jointly quantifies and temporally decomposes these three uncertainty sources in streamflow prediction. The blended model structure of Mai et al. (2020) reformulates structural uncertainty as an equivalent parameter uncertainty through continuously weighted process algorithms, enabling simultaneous Bayesian inference over all three sources using the No-U-Turn Sampler (NUTS). A multivariate analysis of variance (MANOVA) then partitions total predictive variance for each Julian calendar day, yielding a time-varying uncertainty budget across the hydrological year. Applied to 12 MOPEX catchments (1948–2004), the framework achieves CRPS skill scores (relative to a climatological benchmark) of 0.84–0.92, Kling–Gupta Efficiency (KGE) values of approximately 0.63–0.85, and 95% prediction interval coverage of 0.84–0.96. Parameter uncertainty is the largest source at 11 of the 12 catchments (median ∼55%), followed by forcing (∼25%) and structural (∼20%) contributions. Forcing uncertainty peaks during winter–spring high-flow periods and is positively correlated with forest cover fraction (r = 0.50) and elevation, while structural uncertainty is amplified during summer–fall low-flow recession when competing baseflow algorithms diverge most strongly. These results reveal that parameter uncertainty dominates at nearly every site, implying that additional streamflow observations yield greater uncertainty reduction than equivalent investment in improved forcing data or model structural refinement. The temporally resolved uncertainty decomposition further demonstrates that uncertainty envelopes in real-time streamflow forecasting should be time-varying rather than static: structural uncertainty triples during low-flow seasons while forcing uncertainty shifts markedly between summer convective and winter frontal regimes, each requiring different mitigation strategies.

title: Global spatiotemporal dynamics and population exposure of extreme precipitation intensity-frequency combination types (1961–2020)
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part A Author(s): Zilong Zhang, Zhaosheng Wang, Jiang Zhang, Cuijuan Liao, Jiameng Chen, Min Chen, Yuanyuan Huang
abstract: Extreme precipitation (EP) under global warming poses growing risks, yet intensity and frequency of EP are often analyzed separately, limiting the understanding of their co-evolution. Using ERA5-Land daily precipitation data for 1961–2020, this study proposes a K-means clustering framework that jointly classifies EP into nine intensity–frequency combination types and analyzes the transition patterns of EP across two climatological periods, 1961–1990 and 1991–2020. The results reveal a predominant shift toward higher EP frequency globally, with the coverage of the low-intensity and low-frequency (LL) type decreasing markedly while the low-intensity and middle-frequency (LM) and low-intensity and high-frequency (LH) types expanding across the two periods. Around 56% of the land area experienced a change in the dominant EP intensity–frequency combination type, exhibiting an asymmetry in the evolution of intensity and frequency. Specifically, 76.11% and 11.86% of these transitions were driven primarily by single changes in frequency and intensity, respectively, whereas only 7.30% involved same-direction changes in both frequency and intensity. Overlaying the EP classification with GHS-POP population data for 1991–2020 shows that medium- and high-density population regions are more exposed to the LM type and have a lower share of the less hazardous LL type. Regions where elevated EP hazard potential coincides with higher population exposure, particularly South Asia and Southeast Asia, have been identified as critical EP hotspots. These findings highlight the necessity of integrating intensity and frequency dimensions into EP characterization and hazard assessment, providing a basis for region-specific climate adaptation and disaster-risk mitigation planning.

title: Reconciling flood control and hydropower objectives through optimized spatially-explicit capacity equivalency of cascade reservoirs
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part A Author(s): Di Zhu, Shuo Ouyang, Wei Guo, Yanlai Zhou, Kanglin Lin, Sheng Sheng, Hua Chen, Chong-Yu Xu, Fi-John Chang
abstract: Flood control capacity (FCC) is generally reserved for flood safety during high flow seasons. Such operational priority often constrains reservoir performance by reducing hydropower generation and increasing water spillage. However, the rapid expansion of cascade reservoir systems has revealed complementary characteristics in FCC. This complementarity allows for its strategic reallocation among reservoirs to enhance overall system efficiency. This study proposes a novel joint hydropower operation framework based on the concept of equivalent FCC. The framework integrates three synergistic modules including an equivalent coefficient module, a hydropower optimization operation module, and a multicriteria evaluation module. In an application to seven cascade reservoirs in China’s Yalong River Basin, the framework established a key finding: the equivalent coefficient between the Lianghekou (LHK) reservoir and its downstream reservoirs influenced by the FCC replacement and safety flow thresholds at downstream flood control points, varies with flood regional composition and design flood magnitude. The minimum FCC equivalent coefficient is 0.67, which is adopted as a conservative basis for FCC reallocation. Reallocating FCC toward the head reservoir increases cascade hydropower generation by up to 5.8 billion kWh. This increase represents a 5.6% improvement over the conventional operation scheme. This study provides a transferable framework for improving hydropower efficiency, flood prevention, and sustainable water–energy management under diverse hydrological regimes.

title: Building a data-driven conceptual model of the hydrological functioning of the Taita Hills tropical water tower system in Kenya
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part A Author(s): Michel R. Frem, Tibor Y. Stigter, Boris M. van Breukelen, Gretchen M. Gettel, Graham P.W. Jewitt, Benson Mwakachola
abstract: Tropical natural water towers regulate downstream freshwater resources, yet their hydro(geo)logical functioning remains poorly understood. This study integrates multi-year (2022-2025), multi-season hydroclimatic and tracer observations to build a data-driven conceptual model of a tropical metamorphic water tower at Taita Hills in Kenya. The collected dataset enabled rainfall partitioning, baseflow separation, multiple-method recharge estimations, hydrochemical and tritium analyses, and various spatial and multivariable analyses. Results show that the highland subcatchments, representing 43% of the catchment area, account for 87% of total discharge. Actual recharge is approximately twice as high in the highlands as in lower subcatchments. At the subcatchment scale, recharge ratios in more forested and elevated subcatchments (25% of rainfall) are about 1.5 times higher than in thicket-dominated subcatchments. The perennial behavior of most springs and streams, and the high baseflow contribution, indicate an important groundwater-buffering capacity. Evidence suggests that structural geology influences subsurface flow between subcatchments and baseflow in the streams. Spatial variations in lateral subsurface flow, higher specific discharge, and higher spring density in the south point towards cross-subcatchment transfers facilitated by lineaments. Hydrochemical and isotope analyses indicate increasing mineralization and (yearly to decadal) residence times from highlands to lowlands. These results indicate highland-lowland connectivity and show that the Taita Hills function as a groundwater-dominated water tower, where highlands are the main precipitation input zones, storage capacity is large, and preferential flow pathways sustain downstream and dry-season flows. More broadly, these findings reinforce the need to account for subsurface processes when assessing the hydrology of water towers.

title: Advancing satellite remote sensing from open water mapping to water type classification and hydrographic characterization: Application to the endorheic Tibetan Plateau
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part A Author(s): Yiyang Zhang, Kang Yang, Xiaodong Yi, Xiaoyu Guo, Yuxin Zhu, Yuhan Wang
abstract: While satellite-derived waterbody products can map global open water extent and dynamics with good accuracy, integrating water type classification with continuous river networks remains a challenge. Here, we introduce a Topology-aware Water Type Classification (TaWTC) method for classifying the 30 m resolution Global Surface Water (GSW) mask in the endorheic Tibetan Plateau (TP), a representative study area with diverse water types, namely river networks, isolated lakes, pathway lakes, and terminal lakes. This method delineates continuous river networks and isolated lakes by incorporating the water-landscape interaction knowledge, identifies pathway and terminal lakes using two auxiliary datasets, and applies filtering thresholds to ensure product quality. We generate an annual 30 m water type product for 2014–2021, and characterize river network hydrography in detail: (1) the water area in the endorheic TP ranges from 32,268.5 to 35,722.4 km2 during the mean annual river discharge period from 2014 to 2021, comprising 757–935 lakes (>1 km2) and 160–180 river networks; (2) terminal lakes consistently expand, whereas other water types fluctuate annually; (3) low-order (1–3, ∼150 m wide) rivers comprise 67 ± 3% of the network’s length, whereas high-order (4–5, ∼300 m wide) rivers comprise 64 ± 4% of the river area; (4) compared with two existing datasets, our product captures approximately 1.6 times more river length and 1.7 times greater river area, offering improved river width estimates (RMSE: 34.7 m vs. 58.2–89.7 m); (5) our continuous river networks enable hydraulic geometry analysis along longitudinal profiles and evaluation of slope and drainage area impacts on river width. Taken together, our method advances current 30 m open water mapping by providing a more complete, accurate, and continuous water type product, and thereby supports enhanced hydrographic understanding of rivers and lakes.

title: An automated adaptative framework for weather data interpolation
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part A Author(s): Cédric Magain, Guillaume Renard, Philippe Orban, Aurore Degré, Jeroen Meersmans, Caroline De Clerck, Serge Brouyère, Joost Wellens
abstract: Spatially continuous estimates of reference evapotranspiration and rainfall are crucial for environmental management applications. However, their estimation often relies on weather station measurements characterized by incomplete temporal records. Spatial interpolation methods (SIMs) address this issue but are variable and data-specific, making their selection challenging due to dynamic, unharmonized networks and missing data. Advances in computing capabilities enable automation of selection routines, allowing development of automatic SIMs selection process. Several authors proposed employing combined metrics to optimize model selection. Accordingly, this paper developed a new composite metric (CM), based on random and systematic error, integrated into an automated process, called JWgrid (Judicious Widget for Geospatial Robust Interpolation Design or JW), to identify optimal interpolation methods across various contexts. Using Leave-One-Out Cross-Validation (LOOCV), the SIM with the lowest CM value is selected from popular interpolation techniques. The methodology was assessed on weather station networks in Luxembourg, evaluating rainfall and reference evapotranspiration related variables. Results showed low error values with SIM selection frequencies being variable dependent. The methodology’s robustness was assessed by (1) reducing data to 25, 50, and 75% of the original network size, (2) using synthetic datasets with varying data variability, network configurations, and presence or absence of an external drift and (3) applying to a mountainous study area. Network density minimally affected overall accuracy, though SIM selection frequencies varied with no universally preferable method. In synthetic tests and the mountainous area, the JW methodology performed at least equally to the best single method by selecting the most appropriate method at every timestep. Those results highlight the proposed methodology’s advantages, producing reliable gridded datasets across diverse climatic conditions. The approach enables users with limited SIMs experience to easily generate gridded data, providing an effective solution for spatial interpolation challenges in environmental applications.

title: Analytic outlet-state identification in a pathway-age neural transport operator enables cross-domain streamflow forecasting in human-affected basins
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 681, Part A Author(s): Xue Li, Li Wang, Jian Sha
abstract: Neural streamflow forecasts often leave initial water storage unconstrained. We introduce outlet-gauged pathway-age transport (OGPAT), the first neural hydrological operator in which contemporaneous outlet discharge analytically identifies the extensive coordinate of a learned mass-bearing catchment state. Learned normalized pathway-age composition w i and release functional h i define m i = Q t w i / ∑ j h j w j , the unique state on the ray of w satisfying ∑ i h i m i = Q t . This parameter-free map guarantees exact issue-time flux consistency, finite nonnegative storage, and a zero state at zero flow. The state and forecast rainfall enter one nonnegative causal ledger whose outlet marginal gives the complete 1–18 h forecast. Inputs comprise current discharge, 27 basin attributes, and 24-h antecedent and 18-h issued weather from 2025. OGPAT was fitted once on 578,390 issues from 224 minimally disturbed United States basins and tested without target-basin fitting on 1,355,521 issues from 173 human-affected non-reference basins in nine ecoregions. Against same-input Transformer and long short-term memory (LSTM), pooled overall root mean squared error (RMSE), high-flow RMSE and peak-magnitude mean absolute error (MAE) fell by 4.03–7.02%, 3.51–5.44% and 29.01–38.13%, respectively; peak timing improved by 1.34–1.96 h. Basin 35th-percentile skills remained positive; station-block 95% intervals for overall RMSE skill excluded zero against both controls. Against the original capacity-matched non-gauged transport parent, overall/high-flow RMSE and peak-MAE fell by 7.96%/6.94%/35.77%. Against the paired free-radial parent with matched active parameters and training, RMSE and peak-MAE reductions remained 7.33–9.08% and 30.86–33.94%.
