More broadly, this study provides a framework for interpreting strongly negative δ98Mo signatures in other organic-rich marine environments characterized by fluctuating redoxclines, weakly sulfidic conditions, and active Mn/Fe cycling.

title: Silicon isotope fractionation during non-stoichiometric dissolution of wollastonite: Insights into dissolution reaction mechanisms
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 434 Author(s): Cameron Wood, Anna L. Harrison, Jacques Schott, Franck Poitrasson, Jon K. Golla, Jean-Michel Brazier, Vasileios Mavromatis
abstract: Silicate weathering exerts a major control on element cycles including the carbon cycle, whereby dissolution of silicates on the continents removes CO2 from the atmosphere in the form of alkalinity. The process of silicate weathering has also gained attention recently as a potential strategy for mitigation of climate change if the rates of dissolution can be accelerated. In the present study we show that wollastonite (CaSiO3) dissolution rate and stoichiometry is pH-dependent, with faster rates at acidic pH and preferential release of Ca relative to Si at acidic pH but much slower at alkaline pH with slight enrichment of the fluid in Si relative to Ca. The substantial fractionation of Si isotopes occurring during dissolution at acidic pH (Δ30Sisolid-fluid (≥0.85‰) is consistent with the formation of a SiO2 altered layer via the preferential release of Ca vs Si followed by the progressive condensation of Q2 wollastonite SiO4 units into Q3 and Q4 units, but it contradicts the formation of a silica layer induced by wollastonite stoichiometric dissolution followed by amorphous silica precipitation. In contrast, at basic pH, the fluid is somewhat enriched in 30Si, consistent with fractionation during adsorption of Si oxyanions at the surface of possibly precipitated calcite. Ca isotope fractionation, in contrast, is negligible under most conditions, implying calcite precipitation, if present, occurred near to equilibrium. An important implication of the experimental results is that isotope fractionation can occur during net silicate dissolution. Therefore, Si isotopes, and their combination with the isotopes of other major elements, provide an opportunity to evaluate dissolution mechanisms.

title: Green rust controls dissolved iron during transformation to magnetite: provisional solubility products of chloride and sulfate green rust
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 434 Author(s): Neil L. MacPherson, Logan Swaren, Leslie J. Robbins, Manuel Schad, James M. Byrne, Andreas Kappler, Kurt O. Konhauser, Daniel S. Alessi
abstract: Green rusts (GR) are a group of reactive mixed-valent FeII/FeIII hydroxide minerals that play an important role in geochemical systems. Yet, the formation kinetics and environmental implications of the transformation process and products remain poorly constrained. In this study, batch solubility experiments were conducted on fully characterized chloride-rich [GR(Cl)] and sulfate-rich [GR(SO4)] green rust varieties to determine their provisional solubility products ( K sp ′ ). While GR is a metastable phase that transforms into magnetite (Fe3O4) over the course of days, the kinetics of this transformation are slow enough to make the K sp ′ valuable in predicting equilibrium aqueous iron concentrations. Solubility experiments of GR(Cl) and GR(SO4) were performed at circumneutral pH (7.6 – 8.6), two different ionic strengths (IS) representing low IS or ‘freshwater’ (ultrapure water) and high IS or ‘seawater’ (0.56 M NaCl), and at three aging time intervals: 0, 2, and 7 days. X-ray diffraction (XRD) and 57Fe Mössbauer spectroscopy analyses demonstrated progressive transformation of GR to magnetite during this time interval. Solubility experiments yielded average K ′ sp values for GR at each of the three age intervals. Variations between the average K ′ sp as a function of age were statistically insignificant, thus the resulting average K ′ sp values for each GR age interval were combined to produce an overall mean log K ′ sp . The overall mean log K ′ sp ( C l ) values in low and high IS are −75.07 ± 1.39 and −76.22 ± 0.42, respectively, while the overall mean log K ′ sp ( SO 4 ) values in low and high IS are −119.72 ± 1.03 and −126.60 ± 1.07, respectively. Chemical speciation modeling of the concomitant dissolution of GR and magnetite demonstrated that dissolved Fe concentrations were almost entirely controlled by GR dissolution rather than magnetite, demonstrating that GR can dominate aqueous Fe concentrations even in the presence of magnetite.

title: Trace-element signatures in magnetite induced by iron-reducing bacteria
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 434 Author(s): Xiaohua Han, James M. Byrne, Andreas Kappler, Wei Lin, Yongxin Pan
abstract: Biogenic magnetite nanoparticles produced by microorganisms are ubiquitous in modern environments and likely abundant in ancient sediments such as banded iron formations and paleosols. While magnetotactic bacteria (MTB) synthesize intracellular magnetite with distinctive morphological, chemical, and magnetic biosignatures, dissimilatory Fe(III)-reducing bacteria (DIRB) generate extracellular magnetite that is nanoscale, aggregated, and often superparamagnetic, complicating its distinction from abiotic counterparts. To resolve this challenge, we systematically compared magnetite synthesized through abiotic Fe2+ aq-induced ferrihydrite transformation and biogenic transformation mediated by the DIRB Shewanella oneidensis MR-1. Ferrihydrite substrates were co-precipitated with 21 trace elements at concentrations of 0, 10, and 20 ppm to evaluate the combined effects of formation pathway and trace-element availability on magnetite particle size, Fe valence state, and trace-element partitioning. Transmission electron microscopy results showed that biogenic magnetite was consistently smaller than abiotic magnetite, with increasing trace-element concentrations further reducing particle size in both systems. Notably, trace elements induced opposite redox trends: abiotic magnetite became progressively oxidized due to substitution-driven Fe2+ oxidation, whereas biogenic magnetite became more reduced as microbially mediated Fe(III) reduction was enhanced. Inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) analyses demonstrated distinct trace-element partitioning patterns: abiotic magnetite preferentially incorporated Mg, whereas the biotic solid aggregates were consistently enriched in Co and Cd, regardless of initial trace-element concentrations or post-synthesis washing treatments. Because the biotic solid aggregates contained both magnetite and bacterial biomass, their elemental compositions reflect both mineral and biological pools. Accordingly, our objective is to identify pathway-dependent trace element signatures of biogenic and abiotic magnetite formation rather than to quantify elemental incorporation into a pure magnetite lattice. The observed differences may represent the combined effects of trace-element substitution in the magnetite lattice and biologically mediated processes. Comparison with magnetite produced by MTB further highlights substantial interspecies differences in trace-element partitioning, reflecting how the degree of biological control shapes biomineralization. Collectively, the coupled signatures of particle size, Fe valence distribution, and trace-element partitioning establish a coherent geochemical framework for distinguishing abiotic and biogenic magnetite. These results provide new constraints for identifying extracellular microbial magnetite in modern and ancient sedimentary records, with implications for paleoenvironmental reconstruction and astrobiological exploration.

title: Anaerobic oxidation of methane coupled to manganese oxide reduction by ANME–2a in brackish coastal sediments
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 434 Author(s): Robin Klomp, Thomas J. van Asselt, Evalien Baas, Thilo Behrends, Tom Berben, Reinier A. Egas, Marit R. van Erk, Niels A.G.M. van Helmond, Peter A.G. ter Horst, Isabel M.L. Rigutto, Thomas Röckman, Anna J. Wallenius, Olga M. Żygadłowska, Wytze K. Lenstra, Mike S.M. Jetten, Caroline P. Slomp
abstract: Methane (CH4) is a powerful greenhouse gas, and its emission from coastal systems is critically dependent on the balance between methanogenesis and CH4 removal. Anaerobic oxidation of CH4 (AOM) coupled to sulfate reduction is a key pathway, but the role of alternative electron acceptors, such as manganese (Mn) oxides, and the underlying microbial physiology remain elusive. Here, we examine the potential for Mn–driven AOM (Mn–AOM) in brackish coastal sediments at two sites in the Bothnian Sea. The overlapping presence of CH4, Mn oxides, dissolved Mn, and anaerobic methane–oxidizing archaea (ANME) of the clade ANME–2a in sediment zones at the two sites points towards potential for Mn–AOM. Laboratory incubations of sediment from these zones using 13C–labelled CH4 revealed stimulation of AOM upon addition of the Mn oxides birnessite and pyrolusite at one of the two sites. X–ray absorption spectroscopy of the sediment confirmed reductive dissolution of the added Mn oxides during the incubations. A role for cryptic sulfur cycling could be excluded since the addition of molybdate, an inhibitor for sulfate reduction, did not affect the Mn–AOM activity. In all incubations where AOM was stimulated by Mn oxides, members of ANME–2a were the only methanotrophs and increased in relative abundance compared to the start and control. Metagenomic analysis revealed that the ANME–2a genome encoded for all genes involved in the reverse methanogenesis pathway, and eleven multi–heme c–type cytochromes (MHCs), which could mediate extracellular electron transfer. Several MHCs of the ANME–2a were similar to MHCs of freshwater metal–reducing ANME–2d, suggesting similar mechanisms for metal–driven AOM across ANME clades. We conclude that ANME–2a can couple Mn oxide reduction to CH4 oxidation in brackish coastal sediments. Our results highlight that this process needs to be considered when studying CH4 dynamics in coastal systems.

title: Pressure-dependence of viscosity and structure of nepheline melts: implications for mobility of alkaline silicate melts under continental rifts
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 434 Author(s): Qi Chen, Bin Zhao, Aaron Wolfgang Ashley, Young Jay Ryu, Tony Yu, Yanbin Wang
abstract: Primitive nephelinitic magmas are among the most silica-undersaturated alkaline melts generated in continental rifts. However, high-pressure viscosity and structural constraints for their nepheline-rich component remain sparse. Within the Na-aluminosilicate system, nepheline is the silica-poor endmember required to evaluate how pressure, H2O, and silica influence melt rheology along the nepheline-jadeite-albite join. Here, we report in situ falling-sphere viscosity measurements on nepheline melts with 0.2 and 3 wt% H2O at 0.6–7 GPa and ≤ 1980 K. We also perform in situ X-ray scattering measurements on nepheline and nepheline + silica melts under similar conditions to constrain their structures. Our results show that nepheline melt viscosity decreases strongly from ∼0.6 to 5 GPa and then increases slightly at higher pressures. Increasing H2O from ∼0.2 to 3 wt% lowers the melt viscosity by ∼0.2–0.4 log units, corresponding to a reduction by a factor of ∼1.6–2.5, over comparable pressure–temperature conditions. X-ray scattering shows no resolvable pressure-dependent shift in the position of the first-neighbor T-O peak (T = Si + Al), whereas the first sharp diffraction peak (FSDP) shifts to higher Q values with pressure for both nepheline and nepheline + silica melts. This provides direct evidence for the reorganization of intermediate-range structure. Nepheline melt shows a smaller pressure-induced FSDP shift than nepheline + silica and literature jadeite melts, broadly paralleling its weaker viscosity reduction relative to jadeite and albite melts. Pressure-induced changes in Al and possibly Si coordination may also contribute to the weaker viscosity reduction. We apply our constraints to a primitive nephelinitic melt analog for the Labait volcano (Tanzania). We find that ≤ 3 wt% H2O increases both melt mobility and calculated percolation velocity by up to a factor of ∼50 relative to the dry case. These results indicate that volatile enrichment can be crucial to promote extraction of deep nephelinitic melts beneath continental rifts.

title: Calcium isotope systematics during multistage seafloor alteration of abyssal peridotites: insights from the Gakkel Ridge
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 434 Author(s): Jia-Wei Xiong, Chuan-Zhou Liu, Yin-Zheng Lin, Yang Xu
abstract: Calcium is readily mobilized and redistributed during seafloor alteration of abyssal peridotites, yet the associated isotope effects of serpentinization and carbonation are difficult to distinguish from inherited magmatic signatures. Here we combine thermodynamic modelling and whole-rock geochemistry with selective leaching experiments to disentangle these contributions in a petrographically classified suite of Gakkel Ridge peridotites. Thermodynamic melting calculations coupled with internally consistent mineral–melt fractionation factors provide a reference frame for both Ca contents and isotope compositions. Relatively fresh peridotites have δ 44/40Ca values of 0.88–0.94‰, slightly below the predicted residual values, consistent with minor carbonate addition and/or prior melt–rock interaction. In contrast, serpentinized peridotites lacking visible carbonate generally record substantial Ca loss and span a wide δ 44/40Ca range of 0.59–1.19‰. Calculations of selective orthopyroxene and clinopyroxene consumption yield distinct isotope trajectories depending on the evolving Ca contributions of the two pyroxenes and the adopted mineral–fluid fractionation factors. None of the results reproduces the lowest measured values, which likely reflect inherited magmatic signatures and/or unmodelled kinetic effects. In carbonated samples, carbonate-rich leachates account for ∼ 59–100% of whole-rock Ca, with δ 44/40Ca values down to − 0.11‰ in aragonite-dominated fractions and up to 1.43‰ in calcite-dominated fractions. Carbonate addition can thus dominate the whole-rock isotope budget, with the direction of the shift set by the dominant polymorph. These results collectively show that altered oceanic mantle is highly heterogeneous in Ca isotope composition, and that carbonated oceanic mantle spans both light and heavy signatures. This pre-subduction heterogeneity should be considered when interpreting Ca isotope evidence for recycled carbonate in the deep Earth.

title: Trace element distribution in coarse-grained Ca-Al-rich inclusions by femtosecond LA-ICP-MS: Implications for U-Pb chronology
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 434 Author(s): Merel E. Onderwater, Elishevah M.M.E. van Kooten, Glenn J. MacPherson, Alexander N. Krot, Martin Bizzarro
abstract: Calcium-aluminium-rich inclusions (CAIs) in chondritic meteorites are the first solids that formed in the Solar System, as established by U-Pb chronology. After initial condensation, coarse-grained CAIs (Compact Type A, Type B, Type C) experienced melting, resulting in igneous partitioning and spatial redistribution of trace elements among constituent minerals. Understanding these distributions is essential for identifying trace-element host phases and interpreting U-Pb ages. Rare earth elements (REEs) and the actinides Th and U are particularly informative tracers, yet actinide behavior in coarse-grained CAIs remains poorly constrained. Further, the decay of short-lived 247Cm to 235U (t1/2 = 15.6 Myr) complicates U-Pb age determination of bulk CAIs, but its impact at the mineral scale remains elusive. Here, we present major- and trace-element distribution maps of six coarse-grained CAIs mainly composed of melilite, Al,Ti-pyroxene, anorthite and spinel (±forsterite) from CV3 (Vigarano-type) chondrites acquired by femtosecond laser ablation ICP-MS. In CAIs lacking perovskite or hibonite, our results show that Al,Ti-pyroxene is the dominant host of U, Th, and most REEs, with strong enrichments observed toward pyroxene grain edges, whereas light REEs reside in melilite. Trace-element zonation reflects igneous fractional crystallization and is overprinted by melt evaporation, which caused depletion of the most volatile REEs (Yb, Eu, Ce) and U in CAI outer regions and rims. Using Nd and Th distribution maps as proxies for Cm, we model the effects of 247Cm-235U decay on mineral-scale U isotopic compositions. Variable Cm-U partitioning among coexisting minerals is predicted to generate resolvable inter-mineral 235U/238U variations, with the largest excesses in melilite. These variations can produce apparent U-Pb age offsets of ∼0.1–1.0 Myr when U isotopic compositions and radiogenic Pb are derived from isotopically distinct mineral reservoirs, but generally remain small (< 0.15 Myr) when using bulk U isotopic compositions. Our results demonstrate that fractional crystallization and melt evaporation exert a primary control on U distribution and isotope systematics in igneous CAIs and provide new constraints on the interpretation and robustness of high-precision U-Pb chronology of the earliest Solar System solids.

title: Molecular mechanisms of cadmium isotope fractionations during adsorption onto todorokite
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 434 Author(s): Hui Yin, Xinran Yan, Kideok D. Kwon, Chuanwei Zhu, Wentao Wang, Juhyeok Kim, Wei Li, Jingyuan Ma, Jiangshan Li, Ping Wang, Mingxia Wang, Guohong Qiu, Peng Cai, Hanjie Wen
abstract: Todorokite (Tdr), a tectomanganate with a 3 × 3 tunnel structure, controls the adsorption behavior and isotope fractionation of Cd2+ in marine and terrestrial environments. However, the underlying mechanisms of these processes remain poorly constrained. Here, we elucidate how ionic strength governs Cd isotope fractionation during adsorption onto Tdr by integrating batch adsorption experiments, Cd K-edge extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) spectroscopy, density functional theory (DFT) calculations, and classical molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. The adsorption density of Cd2+ onto Tdr gradually increases with pH, but decreases greatly with increasing ionic strength from 0.1 M to 0.72 M NaNO3. Cd2+ adsorption preferentially enriches lighter Cd isotopes in the solid phase relative to the aqueous solution. This fractionation is linked to distortions in Cd2+ coordination environments upon adsorption, as revealed by EXAFS and DFT. Increasing ionic strength reduces the magnitude of Cd isotope fractionation (Δ114/110Cdsolid‑solution) from −0.46 ± 0.05‰ to −0.26 ± 0.07‰, which closely correlates with a shift in Cd2+ binding configurations from tunnel-center sites to corner sites, as captured by classical MD simulations. At low ionic strength, Cd2+ forms a mixture of outer-sphere complexes in tunnel centers and inner-sphere complexes at edge and corner sites. Elevated ionic strength promotes partial dehydration of Tdr tunnels and enhances inner-sphere complexation at corner sites, thereby dampening isotope fractionation. These findings resolve the adsorption-induced Cd2+ isotope fractionation mechanisms and identify ionic strength as a key control on Cd2+ partitioning and isotopic signatures during interactions with tectomanganate minerals in the environment.

title: Stable cerium (Ce) isotope fractionation during sorption onto common iron oxides and implications for Ce redox proxies
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 434 Author(s): Weiming Ding, Wei Ren, Yanyi Yang, Tingying Xu, Xin-Yuan Zheng
abstract: Stable cerium (Ce) isotopes (142Ce/140Ce) have recently emerged as a promising proxy for redox changes in modern and ancient environments. However, robust interpretation of Ce isotope data from natural samples is hampered by the lack of constraints on Ce isotope fractionation during sorption of aqueous Ce onto iron oxides – ubiquitous minerals that strongly influence the Ce cycle in nature. Here we report results from a series of controlled laboratory experiments designed to quantify stable Ce isotope fractionation during sorption of aqueous Ce(III) onto four common iron (oxyhydr)oxides, including ferrihydrite, goethite, hematite, and magnetite. Complementary synchrotron-based X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) analyses were employed to assess Ce valence states on mineral surfaces, while a series of isotope exchange experiments using an enriched 142Ce tracer were conducted to constrain Ce isotope exchange kinetics and the mechanism underlying the observed fractionation. XANES analyses show no detectable Ce(III) oxidation during sorption onto ferrihydrite, goethite, or magnetite, but nearly complete oxidation of Ce(III) to Ce(IV) on hematite. The observed oxidation of Ce(III) on hematite surfaces demonstrates that Fe oxides can contribute to Ce redox transformations, complicating interpretations of Ce valence states alone as redox indicators. The 142Ce-tracer experiments provide unambiguous evidence for rapid Ce isotope exchange between dissolved and sorbed Ce, regardless of Ce valence state on Fe oxide surfaces, with near-complete Ce isotope exchange typically achieved within 2 days. These results indicate that isotopic equilibrium may be attained rapidly during Ce sorption onto Fe oxides. Heavy Ce isotopes are preferentially retained in the aqueous phase, and the inferred equilibrium fractionation factors between aqueous and sorbed Ce (Δ142Ceaq–sorbed) increase in the order: hematite (0.071‰) ≈ goethite (0.077‰) < magnetite (0.118‰) < ferrihydrite (0.174‰). The magnitude of the observed fractionation does not correlate with Ce oxidation on mineral surfaces, suggesting that changes in Ce valence state are not the only control on stable Ce isotope fractionation. Instead, the fractionation appears to be closely linked to the Ce sorption affinity of oxide minerals, with greater affinity corresponding to larger fractionation, indicating an important mineralogical control on equilibrium Ce isotope fractionation during sorption. Together with previously quantified Ce isotope fractionation during sorption onto manganese oxides, this work provides a framework for interpreting δ142Ce variations in Fe- and Mn-oxide-bearing sediments, particularly those formed in aqueous environments with low Ce concentrations. Although further study is needed to fully constrain the effects of solution chemistry and post-depositional alteration, the mineral-specific Ce isotope fractionation identified here provide first-order constraints for interpreting Ce isotope variations in Precambrian banded iron formations (BIFs). A simple mass-balance model predicts that the onset of Mn oxidation on the early Earth can generate greater δ142Ce variability in seawater and coeval BIFs than Fe-oxide sorption alone. A closed-system diagenetic model further indicates that primary Ce isotope signatures preserved in BIFs are relatively robust against complete reset by later fluid alteration. These results highlight the potential of stable Ce isotopes to trace the emergence of Mn oxidation in Earth’s early oceans.

title: Recycling of juvenile arc crust in an ancient convergent margin revealed by Hg isotopes
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 434 Author(s): Han Qi, Jun-Hong Zhao, Runsheng Yin, Anbo Luo
abstract: Recycling of newly formed arc crust at convergent margins is critical to the long-term balance between growth and destruction of the continental crust. However, identifying this process in ancient convergent systems remains challenging because direct geological evidence is rarely preserved. Here, we measure Hg stable isotopes and Nd–Hf radiogenic isotopes in subduction-related igneous rocks from the Neoproterozoic (870–730 Ma) active continental margin of the Yangtze Block in South China to investigate the recycling of juvenile arc crust. Both mafic rocks and granitoids exhibit variable whole-rock Δ199Hg values that largely overlap the depleted-mantle range, ranging from −0.13‰ to +0.15‰ (mean = −0.04 ± 0.15‰, 2SD) and −0.18‰ to +0.11‰ (mean = −0.05 ± 0.14‰, 2SD), respectively, suggesting variable contributions from mantle-, marine-, and terrestrial-derived Hg. Samples with negative Δ199Hg signatures show variable but mostly positive whole-rock εNd (−3.4 to +6.4) and positive zircon εHf (+1.8 to +14.7), and all samples with Δ199Hg below the depleted mantle range (< −0.10‰) have positive εNd values (+0.3 to +3.1). These combined isotopic characteristics indicate that terrigenous sediments formed by weathering and erosion of juvenile arc crust and carrying terrestrial-derived Hg were recycled into the mantle source of arc magmas. Such recycling was likely achieved through subduction of arc-derived trench sediments and/or tectonic erosion of forearc materials. The results of this work suggest that recycling of newly formed arc crust in convergent margins may have been an overlooked means of crustal destruction throughout Earth’s history.

title: Multi-site Li diffusion and coupling to Cr, REE, and P in garnet: Experimental data and implications for interpreting diffusion profiles in natural systems
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 434 Author(s): E.M. Bloch, A. Devoir, O. Müntener, R. Hervig, J.J. Barnes, M.J. Kohn
abstract: We present diffusion experiments on almandine and spessartine garnet conducted at 700–900 °C and 1 atm under Ni–NiO fO2 buffering, designed to evaluate the role of coupled substitution and defect chemistry in controlling Li mobility. Experiments employing source powders doped with Li and either REE or P demonstrate that Li diffusion varies systematically with the identity of the coupled species. In REE-doped systems, Li profiles evolve over the same length scale as REEs and yield diffusivities consistent with established REE diffusion rates, indicating that Li transport is limited by the slower trivalent cation flux. In contrast, undoped Li-out diffusion experiments produce substantially longer Li profiles over identical timescales, reflecting faster transport. Comparison with published inversions of multielement diffusion in natural garnets reveals no clear inconsistency between those natural datasets and experimentally derived slow REE diffusivities, supporting application of the Li–REE results to natural systems. Lithium–Phosphorus experiments yield extremely short P diffusion profiles, consistent with a much slower Li mechanism involving P on the tetrahedral site. Additional experiments reveal fast Li transport associated with multi-site diffusion behavior and with processes linked to Cr redistribution. Across all experiments, effective Li diffusivity varies by at least three orders of magnitude as a function of experimental conditions and substitution mechanisms. These results demonstrate that Li diffusion in garnet cannot be described by a single Arrhenius relationship but instead reflects a spectrum of coupled and multi-site diffusion mechanisms. The dataset presented here likely captures only a subset of the mechanisms active in natural systems and Li diffusivity may span an even broader range than we observe here. Consequently, quantitative interpretation of Li diffusion in natural garnets requires consideration of multiple diffusion mechanisms, potentially including processes not yet characterized, and should be approached with appropriate caution.

title: Sedimentary and redox controls on pyrite sulfur isotopes in oxic–suboxic continental shelf sediments
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 434 Author(s): Xin Chang, Tiegang Li, Zhifang Xiong, Chengguo Guan, Yu Gu, Houjie Wang, Guangchao Zhuang, Xiting Liu
abstract: Pyrite links sedimentary processes with the biogeochemical sulfur cycle and is widely used for reconstructing past redox and depositional environments. However, the controls on pyrite formation and its sulfur isotopic composition (δ34Spyr) in dynamic continental shelf settings, particularly under fluctuating oxic–suboxic conditions, remain poorly constrained. Here we investigate a late Pleistocene–Holocene sedimentary succession from the mud wedge off the Shandong Peninsula (Yellow Sea), which provides a high-resolution archive of glacial–interglacial environmental change, to resolve the relationship between δ34Spyr and shelf sedimentary evolution. We combine sulfur isotope measurements with redox-sensitive trace metals (U and Mo) and previously published sedimentological and geochemical data. Bulk δ34Spyr shows systematic variability associated with several depositional and diagenetic factors. First, δ34Spyr covaries with sedimentation rate, total organic carbon content, and water depth, indicating an important influence of depositional dynamics on pyrite formation and apparent isotopic fractionation. Second, more oxidizing conditions during the Holocene sea-level highstand coincide with generally higher δ34Spyr values, consistent with redox-related changes in sulfur burial. Third, localized sulfur cycling possibly related to anaerobic oxidation of methane may have contributed to elevated δ34Spyr in discrete intervals through isotopic mixing. These results indicate that bulk pyrite sulfur isotopes in oxic–suboxic continental shelf sediments primarily record sedimentary evolution and local diagenetic sulfur cycling, while redox-related variations in sulfur burial may further influence their stratigraphic pattern. This study provides a well-constrained example of δ34Spyr behavior in a non-euxinic shelf environment and emphasizes that depositional and early diagenetic processes must be explicitly considered when applying pyrite sulfur isotopes to paleoenvironmental reconstructions.

title: Synergistic effects of montmorillonite and microbial consortia on Cr(VI) reduction
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 434 Author(s): Yi Zhou, Guocheng Lv, Yunpu Zhao, Xiaotong Yang, Meng Liu, Xuelian Yu, Hongli Chen, Xiaoyan Li, Libing Liao
abstract: Cr(VI) contamination poses a serious threat to ecosystems and human health, making bioremediation strategies that leverage mineral–microbe interactions one of the most critical remediation approaches. Here, we systematically describe the synergistic role of montmorillonite (Mnt) and an indigenous microbial consortium in driving Cr(VI) transformation under simulated groundwater conditions. In batch experiments, abiotic systems with Mnt or sterilized biomass showed negligible or limited Cr(VI) removal, whereas the Mnt–microbe system achieved nearly complete Cr(VI) removal in Cycle 1 and maintained consistently high removal efficiencies over three consecutive redox cycles. RT-qPCR analysis revealed an adaptive strategy whereby the chromate efflux transporter gene chrA was upregulated in the late stage while the intracellular reductase gene yieF remained continuously expressed, concurrent with a strong enrichment of Gammaproteobacteria (from 11.35% to 89.90–96.35%) within Mnt-provided microhabitats. Advanced spectroscopy (XRD, XPS, EXAFS) and microscopy, together with a quantitative Cr mass balance, demonstrate that the main reduction product is Cr(III), which is retained through three pathways: (i) retention of Cr(III) compounds on solid surfaces, (ii) interlayer fixation of Cr(III) within Mnt, and (iii) coprecipitation of Cr(III) with Fe(oxyhydr)oxides. These results highlight a combined mechanism whereby Mnt acts as a chemical buffer, structural host, and ecological scaffold, providing a robust, field-relevant strategy for in situ remediation of Cr(VI)-contaminated aquifers and soils.

title: Mercury isotopes in coral skeletons as proxies for marine Hg cycling: assessing fidelity and fractionation during biomineralization
description: Publication date: 15 November 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 433 Author(s): Fei Cao, Yongquan Zhang, Ruoyu Sun, Larissa Schneider, Songjing Li, Rui Zhang, Pengfei Li, Wang Zheng, Jiubin Chen, Yi Liu
abstract: Stable mercury (Hg) isotopes provide powerful tools for tracing marine Hg sources and transformations. However, suitable geological archives that record long-term changes in seawater Hg isotopes remain scarce, limiting reconstructions of past marine Hg cycling. Here, we evaluate the potential of coral skeletons as archives of seawater Hg isotope compositions and assess the mechanisms controlling Hg incorporation during coral calcification. We systematically investigate the effectiveness and isotopic impacts of chemical cleaning protocols designed to isolate aragonite-bound Hg in coral skeletons. Sequential leaching and oxidative soaking experiments demonstrate that a substantial fraction of Hg in untreated coral skeletons is associated with non-aragonitic phases, primarily organic matter, and can be efficiently removed by optimized oxidative cleaning. These treatments result in large decreases in Hg concentrations and systematic changes in mass-dependent fractionation (MDF; δ202Hg), while mass-independent fractionation (MIF; Δ199Hg and Δ200Hg) signatures remain invariant. This indicates that cleaning selectively affects MDF without altering source-diagnostic MIF signals. Applying the optimized cleaning protocol, we analyze Hg concentrations and isotope compositions in coral skeletons collected from nearshore and offshore environments in the South China Sea. Coral skeletons preserve distinct regional differences in Hg MIF, which are consistent with published regional seawater values, reflecting contrasting contributions from atmospheric and terrestrial Hg sources. In contrast, δ202Hg values are consistently more negative than seawater by approximately 1 ‰, indicating systematic MDF during skeletal incorporation, likely driven by biologically mediated kinetic effects associated with calcification. Our results suggest that coral skeletons generally preserve seawater Hg MIF signatures while exhibiting predictable MDF during biomineralization. These findings establish coral skeletons as promising archives for reconstructing long-term changes in marine Hg cycling in response to natural variability and anthropogenic perturbations.

title: Nickel isotope fractionation by EDTA complexation
description: Publication date: 15 November 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 433 Author(s): Yen-Po Lin, Chih-Chiang Hsieh, Shotaro Takano, Kuo-Fang Huang, Tung-Yuan Ho
abstract: The marine biogeochemical cycling of nickel (Ni) has recently emerged as an important research topic, with studies suggesting that Ni isotopes may serve as a proxy for tracing marine nitrogen fixation. Field studies in low-to-mid latitude surface waters typically report nutrient-type dissolved Ni patterns alongside enriched Ni isotopic signatures, indicating a biological preference for lighter isotopes. However, a laboratory culture study utilizing the organic chelator EDTA (ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid) to regulate metal bioavailability has found relatively heavy Ni isotopes in phytoplankton cells. Ni in both natural seawater and culture media is predominantly complexed by organic ligands, whereas phytoplankton primarily take up non-EDTA-bound Ni. This raises the question of whether the discrepancy between field observations and laboratory results arises from abiotic fractionation induced by EDTA complexation. In this study, we first developed an anion-exchange chromatography method to effectively separate and quantitatively recover non-EDTA-bound Ni ions and organic Ni-EDTA complexes (Ni(EDTA)2−). Through optimization of analytical conditions, we achieved complete separation with total recoveries of 100 ± 4%. While separation efficiency slightly decreased at pH 5 due to partial breakthrough of Ni-EDTA from the resin, optimal separation was achieved under neutral to alkaline conditions (pH 7 and 9), where non-EDTA-bound and EDTA-bound Ni were stably partitioned. Isotopic analysis revealed that Ni(EDTA)2− is significantly enriched in light isotopes, leaving the residual non-EDTA-bound pool isotopically heavy. The measured isotopic fractionation, Δ60Ni(Ni(EDTA)2−–Ni2+) = −1.65 ± 0.27‰, defines the isotopic offset between EDTA-bound and non-EDTA-bound Ni species under neutral to alkaline conditions and agrees with theoretical predictions based on coordination environment and zero-point energy effects. The abiotic fractionation induced by EDTA chelation is substantial and may potentially mask and confound biological isotope signatures. Our study provides a critical methodological foundation and a necessary correction framework for laboratory trace metal incubation studies, enabling more accurate interpretation of Ni isotope fractionation in EDTA-amended, environmentally controlled experiments. Such a large isotopic fractionation induced by EDTA complexation also suggests that isotopic fractionation may occur between organically complexed and inorganic Ni species in natural seawater.

title: Molybdenum redistribution and extreme isotope fractionation in a Barremian weathering profile revealed by scientific drilling
description: Publication date: 15 November 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 433 Author(s): Qin Lin, Philip A.E. Pogge von Strandmann, Ming-Dao Sun, Peng-Li He, Le Zhang, Man Li, Yi-Jun Xiong, Jin-Long Ma, Jie Li, Yi-Gang Xu
abstract: Molybdenum (Mo) redistribution and isotope fractionation during continental weathering provide an important link in the biogeochemical cycles in Earth’s history, but their preservation in ancient weathering systems remains poorly constrained. Complete palaeo-weathering profiles are rarely recovered without overprinting by modern weathering. Here, we investigate Mo mobility and isotope behavior in the YSDP-1 scientific-drilling core from the Chaoyang Basin, Northeast China. The continuous core intersects a ∼ 17 m-thick Barremian palaeo-weathering profile preserved between two andesite flows, which records a downward gradation from calcrete to saprolite. Relative to the fresh andesite, the calcrete is Mo-depleted and shows limited Mo isotope fractionation. In contrast, through the gradational transition into saprolite, whole-rock Mo concentrations increase and the δ98Mo values decrease significantly to a minimum of −3.36‰. In-situ analyses show that Mo is concentrated mainly in saprolite-hosted pyrite, and pyrite separates yield lighter δ98Mo values of −3.43 to −3.66‰. Together with Fe speciation and S content variations, the results indicate depth-focused sequestration of isotopically light Mo at a subsurface Fe–S reduction front in a redox-stratified weathering system. Such profiles may act as isotopic filters, substantially altering exported Mo isotope signatures with little change in Mo concentrations or fluxes, with implications for marine and lacustrine records and low-oxygen weathering on early Earth and Mars.

title: Apatite in Chang’e-6 mare basalts reveals a heterogeneous distribution of chlorine in the Moon
description: Publication date: 15 November 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 433 Author(s): Sen Hu, Mengfan Qiu, Linxi Li, Hejiu Hui, Jialong Hao, Huicun He, Yubing Gao, Liang Gao, Zhan Zhou, Mahesh Anand, Wei Yang, Yangting Lin, Xian-Hua Li, Fu-Yuan Wu
abstract: Chlorine (Cl) serves as a crucial volatile element, providing insight into the magmatic processes and volatile inventory of the Moon. The lunar rocks have notably elevated Cl isotopic compositions; however, no information is available about the Cl and its isotopes on the farside. Here, we report a petrographic, chemical, and Cl isotopic study of apatite in the Chang’e-6 (CE6) mare basalt collected from the South Pole–Aitken (SPA) basin. CE6 mare apatite was measured to have a Cl abundance of 0.04–3.36 wt%. We estimated a Cl abundance of ∼0.6 μg g−1 for the CE6 mantle source, slightly higher than that (0.26–0.32 μg g−1) estimated from Apollo low-titanium mare basalts and lower than that (∼1.3 μg g−1) of Chang’e-5 low-titanium mare basalt. Cl abundances in the mantle source of low-titanium mare basalts exhibit a positive correlation towards the crystallization ages, highlighting a heterogeneous distribution of chlorine in the lunar mantle. The measured chlorine isotopic compositions (δ37Cl, 14.5 ± 2.0‰ to 27.2 ± 2.2‰) are mostly higher than that of nearside mare basalts (0–20‰). CE6 mare apatite shows a positive correlation between Cl abundances and Cl isotopic compositions, comparable with the trend defined by the low-titanium mare apatite collected from the nearside hemisphere. We infer that the high δ37Cl values of CE6 mare apatite were associated with magmatic fractionation of Cl coupled with an elevated chlorine isotopes in the mantle source, favoring the model that the massive formation impact event of SPA would have imprinted the chlorine isotopic compositions in the underlying mantle rocks.

title: Archaeal lipid hydrogen isotope fractionation reveals carbon and energy metabolism in seep ecosystems
description: Publication date: 15 November 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 433 Author(s): Jiachen Fan, Hongxiang Guan, Zeji Wang, Xiaoyan Xu, Xiaoming Miao, Qi Li, Huaichun Wu, Sanzhong Li, Nengyou Wu
abstract: The hydrogen isotope composition (δ2H) of lipid biomarkers from aquatic and terrestrial organisms is a key paleohydrological proxy. However, the biogeochemical controls on the δ2H of archaeal lipids remain poorly understood. Here, we analyzed δ2H values of archaeal lipids from seep carbonates collected at two seep sites: Haima, South China Sea, and AC818, Gulf of Mexico. The hydrogen isotope fractionation (ε2H) between anaerobic methanotrophic archaea (ANME)-derived isoprenoids and porewater ranges from −227‰ to −205‰ (interquartile range). Across all existing data from seep carbonates and sediments, ε2H values average −218 ± 23‰, which indicates mixotrophic physiology based on the reported values for autotrophs (−252 ± 39‰) and heterotrophs (−203 ± 24‰). This pattern is consistent with the lifestyle of ANME, which aggregate with sulfate-reducing bacteria and consume methane, a metabolic mode fundamentally different from that of axenic cultures of non-ANME archaea. Based on our data and those from pure cultures, we suggest that archaeal ε2H is primarily controlled by carbon metabolic mode (autotrophic vs. heterotrophic) rather than respiratory mode (aerobic vs. anaerobic), and more fundamentally, by cellular bioenergetic status. This interpretation is quantitatively evidenced by its universal negative correlation with metabolic energy yield (ΔG/n), reflecting control of cellular bioenergetic status that integrates both energy yield and demand. ANME-1 lipids show relatively negative ε2H (−233 ± 29‰) and positive ε13C (−53 ± 9‰) compared to ANME-2 (−211 ± 21‰ and −62 ± 6‰, respectively), which is consistent with a divergence in carbon source utilization: ANME-1 may rely more on autotrophic CO2 fixation, whereas ANME-2 adopts a more mixotrophic strategy with greater dependence on methane. Collectively, our findings suggest that archaeal lipid ε2H has the potential to serve as a proxy for cellular bioenergetic status, complementing δ13C-based reconstructions of carbon metabolism, and providing a promising framework for deciphering archaeal bioenergetics in modern and ancient ecosystems.

title: Salinity-driven controls on arsenic mobility in naturally coated sands: multi-mineral sorption, kinetic limitations, and metal-facilitated transport
description: Publication date: 15 November 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 433 Author(s): Lucien Stolze, Massimo Rolle
abstract: Arsenic mobility in groundwater is sensitive to hydrodynamic and hydrochemical perturbations, yet the coupled mechanisms controlling arsenic transport in natural sands remain poorly constrained. This study uses a series of column experiments, combined with chemical extractions, surface microscopy, and reactive transport modeling, to explore how transient pore-water chemistry and co-existing mineral surfaces in sandy porous media control arsenate transport under oxic conditions. The detailed experimental investigation and the quantitative model-based interpretation, coupling surface complexation reactions with kinetic mass transfer limitations, allowed us to identify three concurrent hydrogeochemical processes governing As partitioning and transport: (i) an increase in salinity mobilizes aluminum, which complexes with arsenate in the pore water and facilitates its transport; (ii) background cations exchange with protons on the silica surface, lowering the pore water pH and promoting protonation of the metal oxide coatings, which increases As sorption onto these coatings; (iii) major ions adsorb as outer-sphere complexes on the oxide coatings, modifying the surface charge and thereby the binding of arsenate, which is enhanced at circumneutral pH. The first mechanism favors arsenic mobility while the latter two promote its retention, producing a biphasic breakthrough under saline perturbation. Furthermore, kinetic mass-transfer limitations significantly favor As elution and indicate that equilibrium, complete mixing assumptions can substantially overestimate the true retention capacity of an aquifer. Our findings show that these coupled mechanisms have important implications for As mobility in natural porous media under transient hydrochemical conditions and need to be simultaneously considered.

title: Accessory mineral control on δ 88/86 Sr variation during granitic magma evolution and implications for tracing fluid-melt interaction
description: Publication date: 15 November 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 433 Author(s): Nian-Qin Zhang, Yi-Xiang Chen, Kun Zhou, Xu-Qi Chen, Fang Huang
abstract: The formation and differentiation of granitic magmas play a fundamental role in the growth and evolution of continental crust, as well as in the formation of metal ore deposits. Stable Sr isotopes show great potential for tracing fluid-melt interaction during the extensive evolution of granitic magmas. However, the effect of mineral crystallization on stable Sr isotope variation in such magmas remains poorly constrained. To address this issue, we report the stable Sr isotope composition (δ 88/86Sr) of syn-exhumation granites from the Sulu ultrahigh-pressure metamorphic belt. The granites exhibit a wide range of δ 88/86Sr values (−0.63‰ to +0.53‰), mostly lower than those of the mantle and upper continental crust. Petrological observations and whole-rock geochemical compositions suggest that such variations cannot be explained by post-magmatic alteration or assimilation of country rocks. In addition, thermodynamic modeling shows that partial melting of granitic gneiss produces only a slight decrease in δ 88/86Sr values of ca. 0.13‰. Although feldspar crystallization can induce significant stable Sr isotope fractionation, the opposing effects of plagioclase and K-feldspar largely offset each other and cannot explain the observed values. Furthermore, trace element ratios (Zr/Hf, K/Rb, and Nb/Ta) provide no evidence for extensive fluid-melt interaction. Instead, mineral-separate analyses show that apatite has substantially higher δ 88/86Sr values than those of the corresponding whole rocks, whereas titanite and epidote-group minerals show smaller and more variable heavy isotope offsets. The stable Sr isotope variations in the granites correlate with geochemical proxies of accessory mineral fractionation, such as P2O5, TiO2, Nb/Zr, and LREEs, suggesting that the crystallization of such Sr-rich minerals is the dominant factor driving δ 88/86Sr values to as low as −0.63‰. Therefore, fractional crystallization of accessory minerals is proposed to be the primary mechanism for generating light Sr isotopic compositions in the Sulu syn-exhumation granites. These results underscore the pivotal role of accessory minerals in the geochemical evolution of granitic magmas and demonstrate the sensitivity of stable Sr isotopes as tracers of accessory mineral behavior during crustal differentiation. While stable Sr isotopes have great potential for tracing fluid-melt interaction, caution should be exercised because only samples with δ 88/86Sr values lower than ca. −0.6‰ can be more reliably ascribed to such a process. Moreover, by combining Sr-Ba-Fe isotope systematics, we can decode a progressive crystallization sequence from feldspar and mica crystallization to late-stage precipitation of Fe-Ti oxides and Sr-rich accessory minerals during granitic magma evolution.

title: Sulfur isotope fractionation during metal–silicate equilibration and implications for Earth’s mantle
description: Publication date: 15 November 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 433 Author(s): Lucas Calvo, Jabrane Labidi, Anat Shahar, Edith Kubik, Julien Siebert
abstract: Sulfur (S), a moderately siderophile and volatile element, may have been delivered to Earth during the planet’s main stage of accretion. Alternatively, it may have been supplied by the late veneer, after the core was fully segregated from the mantle. Mid-ocean ridge basalts present a systematic depletion in the heavier S isotope, 34S, relative to chondrites. This has been suggested to reflect isotopic fractionation during core–mantle differentiation or during evaporative loss from Earth’s magma ocean. Two studies have estimated the metal–silicate S isotope fractionation but yielded conflicting results. Laboratory experiments suggest that equilibrium fractionation favors the heavy 34S in metal during metal–silicate equilibria. However, the magnitude of the 34S/32S fractionation between metal and silicate appears too small to explain the composition of mid-ocean ridge basalts. In contrast, ab-initio calculations predict fractionation in the opposite direction, with a much smaller magnitude. Here, we present a series of experiments conducted with the triple-isotope technique. This approach allows for a robust determination of sulfur isotope fractionation between metal and silicate. We also report a set of conventional time-series experiments with variable starting isotopic compositions, and compare the results from both approaches. The reported results confirm that metal–silicate equilibration produces significant 34S-depletion in silicates, with a magnitude of 0.65 ± 0.28‰ at 1673 K, in agreement with previous experimental work. This fractionation is parametrized as a function of temperature to account for Earth’s mantle composition following 1000 ∗ ln α M e t . - S i l . ≈ a / T 2 = 1.819 ± 0.784 × 10 6 K - 2 . This fractionation can explain most depleted mantle estimates; however, additional processes such as the effect of high-pressure equilibrium, sulfide–melt equilibria, or long-term mantle recycling may contribute to the observed Earth’s mantle regional variations.

title: Solubility of tholins in hexane, acetonitrile, and acrylonitrile: Implications for Titan’s lakes
description: Publication date: 15 November 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 433 Author(s): Yohann Layssac, Troy L. Williams, Rohana Liyanage, Jackson O. Lay, Vincent F. Chevrier
abstract: Aerosols formed in the atmosphere of Titan sediment and accumulate on the surface where they may interact with the liquid hydrocarbons and organics composing the lakes and seas. In this study, Titan tholins made from nitrogen and methane (95/5) exposed to a cold plasma discharge have been mixed with acetonitrile, acrylonitrile, hexane and a saturated solution of acetonitrile in hexane, under an inert atmosphere at room temperature. The liquid phase has been monitored through time (days to weeks) using gas chromatography coupled to mass spectrometry. Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy has been used to characterize tholins before and after solubilization events, in both the near and mid infrared regions. Infrared spectra do not show differences induced by the interaction of tholins with the liquid phases used in this work. Gas chromatograms indicate that many organics are extracted from our tholins in acetonitrile, with the characterization of nitriles, amines and other nitrogen bearing molecules. Among the three other solvents tested, only acrylonitrile shows limited solubilization of organics from tholins, but no structure could be identified. Pure hexane fails to solubilize any organics detectable in our conditions, as expected by its nonpolar nature. Despite the high solubility of our tholins in acetonitrile, no organics are solubilized when this molecule is saturated in hexane. The positive results obtained with polar solvents (acetonitrile and acrylonitrile) and the negative results obtained with nonpolar liquid phases (hexane with or without acetonitrile) are consistent with previous studies. However, these studies also showed that the composition of tholins is highly dependent on the conditions used for their synthesis, which cannot capture the complexity of Titan’s atmosphere where many processes co-exist. This suggests that Titan haze could contain a rich reservoir of organics that, given the geological timescales available, would make the presence of dissolved organics in the lakes and seas a real possibility.

title: Impact-induced formation of low-Ca pyroxene in a partially melted troctolitic clast from the Chang’e-5 lunar regolith
description: Publication date: 15 November 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 433 Author(s): Yang Bai, Zhuang Guo, Yuqi Qian, Shichuan Sun, Jingru Ma, Kangjun Huang, Li-Hui Chen, Yunpeng Dong, Simon A.T. Redfern, Charles K. Shearer, Guochun Zhao
abstract: The composition of the lunar deep interior remains debated, as remote sensing observations indicate that impact-excavated materials from within and around large basins contain both olivine and low-Ca pyroxene (LCP). Here we show a partially melted exotic troctolitic clast from Chang’e-5 lunar soils that records impact-induced mineral transformations. The exotic clast consists of forsteritic olivine grains with magnesium-rich rims and pyroxene crystals embedded in a feldspathic glassy matrix. Pyroxene crystals occur as elongated aggregates, with dendritic crystallites growing along the grain edges. The elongated pyroxene crystals show distinct zoning, with Fe-enriched, low-Ca cores and Al-enriched, high-Ca rims, while the dendritic crystallites are compositionally identical to the rims. Elemental mass-balance considerations suggest that impact-induced melting and recrystallization of olivine and anorthite generated the observed LCP–Al-rich high-Ca pyroxene (HCP) assemblage, with Si released during anorthite transformation compensating for the substantial Si consumption during LCP formation. These observations indicate that the LCP formed through impact-induced partial melting of an olivine-rich troctolite under rapid cooling conditions, rather than being a primary phase excavated from the lunar deep interior. Our findings demonstrate that LCP signatures observed around large impact basins, e.g., Imbrium and South Pole-Aitken basins, may originate from impact-modified olivine-rich lithologies, rather than being directly excavated from the deep interior. These results raise the possibility that such transformations may be a widespread process associated with large-scale impacts on the Moon and have important implications for the interpretation of remote sensing data and constraints on the composition of the lunar interior.

title: Quantitative constraints on fluid-induced extreme oxygen isotope fractionation from crystal–fluid interactions in highly evolved granite–pegmatite systems
description: Publication date: 15 November 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 433 Author(s): Zhen-Hua Wang, Chang-Zhi Wu, Ru-Xiong Lei, Xiang-Long Luo, Matthew J. Brzozowski
abstract: The mechanisms of rare metal mineralization within highly evolved granite–pegmatite systems remain a topic of debate, particularly regarding the role of magmatic–hydrothermal processes in rare metal enrichment. While hydrothermal fluids play a critical role in transporting rare metals in some mineralizing systems, their transport effectiveness varies significantly depending on their origin and physicochemical properties. The highly evolved F–Rb-rich Baishitouquan (BST) pluton is a representative rare metal granite–pegmatite system in NW China. It exhibits a progressive lithological transition from amazonite-free granite in the lower lithological zones (LLZ) to amazonite-rich granite and pegmatite veins in the middle lithological zones (MLZ) to amazonite-poor granite in the upper lithological zone (ULZ), which formed as a result of the magmatic–hydrothermal evolution of a single granitic melt. Accordingly, this pluton provides a unique opportunity to investigate the mechanisms of rare metal mineralization through quantitatively constraining the origin and physicochemical properties of fluids, and by evaluating how these fluids drive geochemical fractionation during magmatic–hydrothermal evolution. This is accomplished here by characterizing the δ18O values of microtexturally and chemically heterogeneous domains in zircon and quartz from the different lithological zones of the BST pluton. Magmatic zircon domains (Zrn-I; δ18OZrn-I = 5.88–7.39‰) have δ18O values that reflect that of the parental granitic melt. In contract, quartz phenocrysts (δ18OQtz = 8.71–10.97‰) and hydrothermal zircon domains (Zrn-II and Zrn-III; δ18OZrn-II = 6.67–12.18‰; δ18OZrn-III = 15.03–20.69‰) exhibit systematically elevated δ18O values. Quartz record syn-magmatic hydrothermal perturbations, whereas hydrothermal zircon domains reflect post-magmatic crystal-fluid interactions and progressive isotopic re-equilibration. The transition from magmatic to hydrothermal conditions is constrained between the oxygen isotope closure temperatures of the Zrn-I domain (∼698 °C) and quartz (∼527 °C). The fluid evolution trajectory is reconstructed from zircon–fluid oxygen isotope fractionation relationships, in which Zrn-I defines the initial isotopic state of the fluid in equilibrium with the magma, whereas Zrn-II and -III record progressive isotopic re-equilibration with evolving hydrothermal fluids during cooling. Modeling results demonstrate that fluid-induced geochemical fractionation during fluid evolution generates pronounced intra-crystal heterogeneity in both oxygen isotopes and trace elements. The quantitatively reconstructed δ18Ofluid–temperature trajectory of the hydrothermal fluids that exsolved from the BST granitic magmas demonstrates that their internal evolution, driven by progressive cooling and crystal–fluid interactions, is sufficient to trigger extreme oxygen isotope fractionation and pegmatite formation without requiring an influx of externally derived fluids.

title: Diagenetic pathways and preservation of bulk and amino acid δ 15 N in bivalve shell organic matter across the Holocene to the Pliocene
description: Publication date: 15 November 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 433 Author(s): Qian Huang, Kirsty E.H. Penkman, Ellie Nelson, Daniel Vigelius, Thomas Tütken, Lukas Fröhlich, Bernd R. Schöne
abstract: Nitrogen isotope (δ15N) records preserved in mollusc shells have strong potential to reconstruct changes in nitrogen sources, transformations and transport in the ocean beyond instrumental observations. This is because mollusc shells can be precisely dated and often preserve highly temporally resolved records. In addition to bulk nitrogen isotope analysis, compound-specific nitrogen isotope analysis of amino acids (CSIA-AA) further enables the separation of biogeochemical processes from the trophic effects. However, the extent to which bulk and amino acid-specific δ15N are preserved in shell-bound organic matter in (sub-)fossil materials over the multi-millennial to multi-million-year timescales remains poorly understood. Furthermore, intra-crystalline organic matter (intra-OM), which is encapsulated inside calcium carbonate biomineral units, has not been systematically evaluated for its ability to preserve original isotopic signals relative to total shell organic matter (total-OM). Here, we investigate the effects of diagenesis on bulk and amino acid-specific nitrogen isotope compositions in the shell-bound organic matter (both intra-OM and total-OM) of the long-lived bivalve Arctica islandica, a well-established geochemical archive in the North Atlantic. We analysed live-collected and sub-fossil shells spanning the Holocene from the northern North Sea and fossil specimens from several Crag formations in East Anglia, UK, dating to Plio-Pleistocene. Using spectroscopic, chemical, and isotopic approaches, we assessed the preservation of the biomineral structure, shell organic chemistry and nitrogen isotope compositions in bulk shell organic matter (δ15NBulk) and their amino acids (δ15NAA). Only minimal modifications of the original aragonitic shell mineralogy were detected as indicated by low (<5 %) calcite content in all specimens analysed from the different studied time periods (Plio-Pleistocene, Early or Mid-Holocene, Late Holocene and Modern). Then we identified a diagenetic trajectory in which inter-crystalline organic matter was progressively lost through open-system interactions during taphonomy, reflected by declining nitrogen content and convergence of amino acid compositions between total-OM and intra-OM. In contrast, intra-OM remained physically protected within the biomineral matrix and retained nitrogen over ca. 2–3 million years, despite internal molecular reorganisation including peptide hydrolysis and selective loss of labile amino acids (e.g., serine and threonine). Given lack of net nitrogen loss, intra-OM showed robust preservation of δ15NBulk. However, while δ15NAA of intra-OM in Holocene shells retained patterns consistent with limited diagenetic alteration, CSIA-AA δ15N patterns in Plio-Pleistocene shells deviated from the Holocene pattern, even within intra-OM, with changes in the relative isotope spacing among amino acids associated with degradation. These findings provide mechanistic insight linking organic matter preservation and nitrogen isotope preservation in molluscs shell biomineral archives and highlight intra-OM as a promising substrate for reconstructing past marine nitrogen cycling within certain diagenetic limits.

title: Time-resolved Mo isotopes track source evolution from recycled slab components to a coherent OIB-type mantle source
description: Publication date: 15 November 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 433 Author(s): Dongjing Xu, Xiu-Zheng Zhang, Yue Qi, Jie Li, Bing Chen, Pei-Na Guo, Tao Du, Qiang Wang
abstract: Subduction returns surface lithologies to the mantle and helps generate enriched domains sampled by ocean-island basalts (OIB). Many studies identify recycled components in OIB sources, but few resolve how these components mature into coherent, melt-fertile mantle domains. We examine this transition using Miocene and late Middle Pleistocene alkaline lavas that record temporally distinct sampling of a regional slab-modified asthenosphere above stagnant Tethyan slab material in southeastern Yunnan. New major- and trace-element, Sr–Nd–Pb and Mo isotope data for ca. 0.25–0.22 Ma Pingbian basanites are compared with published ca. 13–11 Ma Maguan basalts. The Pingbian lavas form a compact, silica-undersaturated, high-Nb suite. Relative to Maguan, Pingbian has narrower ranges of source-sensitive trace-element ratios and Sr–Nd–Pb isotope compositions and a clearer enriched mantle 1 (EM1)-like signature, characterized by low 206Pb/204Pb and 143Nd/144Nd and intermediate 87Sr/86Sr. These features define a more focused melt-producing domain, whereas δ 98/95Mo spans −0.41‰ to +0.04‰. Integrated δ 98/95Mo–Ce/Mo, trace-element and Sr–Nd–Pb relationships are consistent with similar recycled component classes in both suites but different effective weighting, with weaker expression of eclogitized oceanic crust and sediment-derived material and stronger expression of hydrated slab mantle in Pingbian. The resolved Mo isotope excursions indicate that component-scale heterogeneity persisted within this focused source. We define OIB-source maturation as source focusing and component reweighting within an inherited recycled slab inventory, rather than replacement by a new reservoir. More broadly, this paired record suggests that EM1-like OIB-type sources above stagnant slabs can develop through such reorganization, while Mo isotopes may retain component-level memory despite the narrowing of trace-element and Sr–Nd–Pb signatures.

title: Boron isotope fractionation in siliceous hot spring sinters: Geochemical implications for biosignatures
description: Publication date: 15 November 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 433 Author(s): Eizo Nakamura, Chie Sakaguchi, Katsura Kobayashi, Nghiem Van Dao, Elena Kalinina, Hidehisa Tsuchida, Steven W. Ruff, Luke Steller, Martin Van Kranendonk, Ayrton Hamilton, Kathleen Campbell
abstract: Siliceous hot spring sinters preserve coupled mineralogical, geochemical, and isotopic signatures generated during microbial silicification and therefore represent valuable archives of biosignature formation. However, the mechanistic criteria for distinguishing biologically influenced silicification from abiotic silica precipitation remain poorly constrained. Here we present paired boron-isotope and comprehensive multi-element datasets (up to 57 elements) for opaline silica sinters and coexisting waters from four hydrothermal systems spanning a wide range of physicochemical conditions (pH 2–8; 30–98 °C): the Taupo Volcanic Zone (New Zealand), Misasa (Japan), Puga (India), and El Tatio (Chile). Hydrothermal waters exhibit a relatively restricted range of δ11B values (≈ −5 to − 1‰, except Puga at ≈ −13‰), whereas associated silica sinters display much larger isotopic variability (≈ −10 to − 40‰), with in situ secondary ion mass spectrometry (SIMS) analyses revealing microscale domains with values as low as − 50‰. Strongly negative δ11B values are systematically associated with boron enrichment (up to > 10,000 ppm), laminated microbial fabrics, and enrichments of multivalent and high-field-strength (HFS) cations. Stepwise leaching experiments and SIMS observations indicate that the measured boron-isotope signatures predominantly preserve primary depositional characteristics despite minor localized evaporative modification. To explain these coupled observations, we propose an EPS microenvironmental reactor model in which microbial activity within EPS-rich microenvironments generates localized physicochemical conditions distinct from those of bulk fluids. Within these microenvironments, local pH gradients associated with microbial activity promote the formation of tetrahedral borate, while EPS-associated multivalent and HFS cations facilitate boron retention during early opal-A polymerization. Progressive silica precipitation preferentially immobilizes isotopically light boron, producing strongly negative δ11B values together with characteristic multi-element enrichments. The model provides a mechanistic framework linking microbial activity, aqueous boron speciation, element partitioning, and silica precipitation, thereby accounting for the observed hierarchy of boron-isotope fractionation across geothermal systems spanning acidic to alkaline conditions. These findings indicate that opaline silica exhibiting δ11B ≤ − 20‰, together with boron enrichment, HFS-cation enrichment, and stromatolitic microfabrics, provides a powerful and testable geochemical criterion for biologically influenced silicification. Such negative δ11B values extend far beyond those of primary silicate reservoirs and, when coupled with complementary elemental and microstructural evidence, are consistent with biologically influenced boron sequestration during silica precipitation. The consistency of this signature across chemically diverse hydrothermal environments, together with its potential preservation in Paleoarchean hydrothermal deposits, suggests that boron isotopes offer a valuable tool for evaluating biosignatures in ancient terrestrial hydrothermal systems and silica-bearing environments, including Mars.

title: Impact-induced submicroscopic metallic iron particles identified in “dusty olivine” from brecciated lunar meteorite Bechar 012
description: Publication date: 15 November 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 433 Author(s): Yutong Ma, Zhuang Guo, Aicheng Zhang, Jingjing Niu, Shan Qin
abstract: Nanophase iron particles are ubiquitous in lunar soils and are largely attributed to space weathering; however, no nanophase iron particles formed in lunar crystalline minerals via impact events have been reported. Their growth, migration, spatial distribution, and interactions with host minerals under impact remain poorly understood. Here, we report the discovery of impact-induced dusty olivine clasts (containing nanoscale to submicron iron metal particles) in the lunar breccia meteorite Bechar 012. These clasts encapsulate a comprehensive record of iron particle formation and distribution within their crystalline host. Their well-preserved state provides a clear snapshot of the microscopic mineral processes often obscured in more heavily processed soils or breccias, making Bechar 012 an ideal natural sample for study. Crystallographic orientation analysis suggests that these dusty olivine grains undergo plastic deformation, with iron metal particles concentrated within the deformed regions, indicating a correlation between deformation microstructures and iron metal particle formation. We propose a three-step model for the formation of dusty olivine and the iron metal particles therein: (1) impact-induced plastic deformation of olivine; (2) sub-solidus olivine decomposition (Fe2SiO4 = 2Fe + SiO + 3/2O2) within partially amorphous zones, leading to the nucleation of nanosized iron metal particles, with SiO and O2 diffusing away through disordered pathways (e.g., partially amorphous zones, dislocations and pores) in the deformed olivine; and (3) capture of particles by migrating dislocations, followed by aggregation and oriented attachment (OA)-driven growth along the olivine lattice at dislocations and subgrain boundaries, resulting in the formation of submicron-sized iron metal particles. These processes indicate an equilibrium shock pressure below 16 GPa, with temperatures between 1000 °C and 1650 °C. These results confirm the pivotal role of impact-induced olivine deformation in facilitating the formation, migration, and growth of iron metal particles and highlight the significance of OA in their coarsening. The discovery of impact-induced iron metal particles in the lunar meteorite indicates that these particles can be broadly formed within crystalline minerals, rather than being limited to the amorphous rims of lunar regolith minerals and glassy impactites, while also offering a potential explanation for the lunar magnetic anomalies.

title: Behavior of major to trace elements, volatiles, and metals during basaltic arc magma differentiation: a slow-cooling experimental study at 1.5, 1.0, 0.7, and 0.4 GPa
description: Publication date: 15 November 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 433 Author(s): Jia Chang, Andreas Audétat
abstract: High-pressure differentiation of arc basaltic magmas in compressive arc settings is commonly invoked to generate high-Sr/Y magmas associated with porphyry Cu deposits, but why such magmas are particularly fertile remains debated. To address this question, we conducted slow-cooling crystallization experiments on a volatile- and metal-doped natural arc basalt at 1.5, 1.0, 0.7, and 0.4 GPa. The starting material contained geologically realistic volatile and metal contents, including 3.5 wt% H2O, 0.4 wt% CO2, 2200 µg/g S, and 1000 µg/g Cl. Samples were homogenized at 1250 °C, slowly cooled to target temperatures, and then quenched. Most runs used single-crystal zircon liners to minimize Fe, S, and metal loss to Pt95Rh05 capsules. In all pressure series, minerals crystallized in the sequence olivine → pyroxenes → amphibole → ±plagioclase, with early olivine and pyroxenes partly replaced by amphibole during cooling. These textures resemble those in deep-crustal arc cumulates. Comparison between experimental residual melts and global arc magma suites suggests that recurrent recharge and mixing of primitive mafic melts with variably evolved melts are common during the formation of intermediate to felsic arc magmas. At pressures ≥0.7 GPa, abundant amphibole crystallization and suppressed plagioclase crystallization generated residual melts with high Sr/Y ratios and moderately depleted HREE signatures. Despite relatively oxidizing conditions and sulfide–anhydrite coexistence in some runs [ΔFMQ = +2.4 (±0.4)], all pressure series reached sulfide saturation early, at ≤54 wt% melt SiO2. Sulfide saturation depleted the residual melts in S and likely also in Cu, Au, and Ag, whereas Mo, Pb, and Zn were less affected. Neither S nor ore-forming metals were preferentially enriched in the high-pressure residual melts. CO2 promoted early exsolution of CO2-rich fluids, which became progressively more H2O-rich during differentiation. At melt SiO2 contents ≥65 wt%, increasing fluid/melt ratios led to depletion of Cl, Mo, Pb, and Zn in the residual melts. Higher pressure delayed fluid saturation, reduced the amount of exsolved fluid, produced more CO2-rich fluids, and allowed melts at a given SiO2 content to retain more H2O and CO2. Nevertheless, high-pressure melts did not become enriched in Cl or metals relative to lower-pressure melts, probably because these elements partitioned more strongly into fluids at higher pressure. We conclude that high-Sr/Y magmas produced by high-pressure differentiation are distinguished mainly by high H2O contents, rather than by unusually high S, Cl, Cu, or other ore-metal contents. Their fertility is therefore more likely controlled by high magmatic H2O contents, which may promote deep magma storage in transitional mid- to upper-crustal reservoirs and focused fluid release through porphyry fingers.

title: Source evolution controls the molybdenum isotope composition of Archean continental crust
description: Publication date: 15 November 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 433 Author(s): Eric D. Vandenburg, Oliver Nebel, Laura M. Spencer, Marc-Alban Millet, R. Hugh Smithies, Peter A. Cawood, Alexandra Churchus, Wenli Liang, Emilie Bruand, Jean-François Moyen, Alex McCoy-West, Priyardarshi Chowdhury
abstract: Earth’s continental crust is its most chemically evolved and diverse reservoir. Numerous studies have investigated its stable metal isotope character to understand its formation and secular evolution. Molybdenum (Mo) isotopes are useful tracers of petrogenetic processes in Phanerozoic igneous rocks, but Archean granitoids, which make up much of Earth’s early continental crust, remain poorly characterized. Here, we report high-precision whole-rock Mo isotope data for 28 Archean granitoids from Australia’s Pilbara and Yilgarn cratons, with crystallization ages from 3.52 to 2.63 Ga. The samples cover a spectrum of magmatic series, including tonalite-trondhjemite-granodiorite (TTG), TTG hybrid, sanukitoid, potassic, and potassic hybrid magmas. After assessing the effects of alteration, crustal contamination, and fluid exsolution, we interpret the observed δ 98/95Mo range of −0.93 to +0.25‰ as primarily reflecting magmatic source characteristics. TTG and TTG hybrid granitoids, together with samples derived from unenriched meta-mafic or mantle-like sources, have mean and median δ 98/95Mo values close to, or slightly higher than, chondrite and depleted MORB mantle (DMM). In contrast, potassic, potassic hybrid, and sanukitoid series granitoids, as well as samples derived from enriched meta-mafic or felsic crustal sources, extend to lower, sub-mantle δ 98/95Mo values. Elemental proxy relationships, major- and trace-element modeling, and phase-equilibrium constraints indicate that source composition and residual mineralogy during partial melting primarily control Mo isotope variability in these rocks. In crustally-derived granitoids, lower δ 98/95Mo values are associated with more mature source compositions and with changes in the abundance and composition of residual feldspar. Amphibole, garnet, and biotite may also have subordinate effects. These relationships suggest that Mo isotopes track the progressive reworking of Archean crust. Juvenile crust-derived TTG magmatism is characterized by near- to suprachondritic δ 98/95Mo, whereas later sanukitoid and potassic granitoid magmatism, linked respectively to mantle metasomatism and reworking of TTG-dominated gray gneiss, shifts toward lower δ 98/95Mo values. The observed trends imply that intracrustal reworking alone can push continental averages to sub-mantle values, with ramifications for mass-balance models. Although TTGs are generally suprachondritic, their δ 98/95Mo values are not high enough to easily support models requiring large volumes of Hadean to Paleoarchean continental extraction from a chondritic mantle to offset the subchondritic Mo isotope composition inferred for the depleted mantle from Archean komatiites. The strong Mo isotope contrast between continental crust and upper mantle may therefore have developed after 2.6 Ga, once crustal recycling became more extensive.

title: Nitrous oxide cycling and isotopic overprinting in lake basins with contrasting mixing regimes
description: Publication date: 15 November 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 433 Author(s): Teresa Einzmann, Moritz F. Lehmann, Annie Bourbonnais, Jakob Zopfi, Fabio Lepori, Claudia Frey
abstract: Nitrous oxide (N2O) is a potent greenhouse gas and ozone-destroying substance, and lakes contribute variably to its atmospheric budget. We investigated the seasonal variability of N2O cycling in two contrasting basins of Lake Lugano, Switzerland: the meromictic North Basin (NB) and the holomictic South Basin (SB). Over one full seasonal cycle, we measured N2O concentration and site-specific isotopomer compositions to assess spatio-temporal dynamics. Both basins showed near-neutral N2O exchange with the atmosphere, without clear seasonal patterns of N2O emission versus uptake (average air–water exchange flux of 0.04 ± 0.3 µmol m−2 d−1). Keeling-plot analysis indicated a nitrification-driven N2O source in the oxic water column in both basins, as inferred from its position-specific isotopic nitrogen composition. In the anoxic water column in the North Basin, N2O was persistently depleted, whereas in the deep South Basin N2O consumption was observed only during late-stage stratification.
