Solid-melt reactions markedly altered the composition of the incoming komatiite melt, with basaltic komatiite and komatiitic basalt formed at lower temperatures and modified high-Mg komatiites at higher temperatures. The melts exhibit the very wide range of MgO/SiO2 seen in ultramafic lavas in Archaean greenstone belts. Consideration of rare earth element and Hf partitioning suggests that assimilation of protocratonic ancient harzburgite into invading komatiite will be much more strongly seen in radiogenic Hf than Nd (or Ce) isotope ratios. Although both the original solid (harzburgite) and the incoming melt (komatiite) are ultramafic, their chemical contrast is sufficient to drive metasomatic reaction, likely partly due to the presence of a percolating melt. The reactions require higher temperatures than attained in the post-Archaean mantle, explaining both the sharp demise of komatiites after 2.5 Ga and the highly refractory nature of Archaean harzburgites and dunites. Ancient proto-cratonic mantle is one plausible candidate harbouring radiogenic signatures of Hadean silicate differentiation. The reason why these signatures are most commonly found in Archaean mafic and ultramafic igneous rocks may relate to the secular drop in maximum plume temperature, which has compromised the capacity of younger melts to sample this reservoir via assimilation

title: Spatial association between atmospheric cadmium deposition and farmland soil cadmium in a karst mining region
description: Publication date: Available online 5 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials Author(s): Hanbing Liu, Shihao Wang, Huading Shi, Xinliang Xu
abstract: Atmospheric Cd deposition supplies ongoing inputs to farmland, but its relationship with soil Cd varies across environmental settings. We examined this relationship using annualized deposition at 78 monitoring sites, 1,400 farmland topsoil samples, and enterprise locations in a karst Pb–Zn mining region of southwestern China. Deposition ranged from 0.604 to 21.6gha⁻¹ yr⁻¹. Higher deposition coincided with higher soil Cd around monitoring sites, with rank correlations of 0.278–0.335 after removing broad spatial trends. Spatial-bootstrap intervals for the unadjusted correlations excluded zero at 5km under both regional partitions, whereas support at 2 and 3km depended on the partition. Quantile regression using cross-validation-selected deposition estimates and adjustment for soil properties, precipitation, and enterprise density identified a positive association at the conditional 90th percentile of soil Cd (coefficient, 0.604mgkg⁻¹ per g ha⁻¹ yr⁻¹; Bonferroni-adjusted interval, 0.044–1.237). The Q90 association also remained positive when nearest-enterprise distance replaced enterprise density. These findings show that current atmospheric loading overlaps elevated farmland soil Cd, with the most consistent adjusted evidence in the upper conditional distribution. Joint deposition monitoring and soil surveys can help prioritize investigations of ongoing inputs and farmland contamination.

title: Facet-dependent As(V) adsorption behavior on goethite: Molecular-scale coordination mechanisms and surface reactivity
description: Publication date: Available online 5 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials Author(s): Xiaofei Li, Miao Wang, Dian Chen, Cong Fan, Xiaolian Wu, Yanping Bao, Xiaohu Jin, Qian Yao, Xueding Jiang, Hailong Wang
abstract: Goethite is a major arsenic scavenger in natural waters, sediments, and soils, yet facet-dependent As(V) coordination remains poorly characterized. We studied As(V) adsorption on two well-defined goethite morphologies: plate-like GA (higher (021)/(110) ratio) and rod-like GB (lower (021)/(110) ratio), both dominated by the (110) facet. Results showed GA exhibits a ~1.5-fold higher As(V) adsorption capacity (5.69 vs. 3.73 µmol/m2) and a ~3.6-fold higher rate constant than GB (1.34 vs. 0.37 m2/(μmol·min). Area-normalized QCM-D revealed ~1.1-fold faster As(V) deposition on GA, indicating higher loading and faster kinetics on the (021)-enriched GA. At 0.8mM As(V), pH5.0, in-situ ATR-FTIR, supported by EXAFS and DFT, indicates bidentate inner-sphere complexes dominate on both goethites, with a minor monodentate fraction detectable on GA but not on GB, reflecting different (021)/(110) facet ratios. DFT confirmed the (021) facet has a higher density of singly-coordinated hydroxyl groups and more negative adsorption energies for bidentate and monodentate As(V) complexes (−1.97 to −1.39eV) than the (110) facet (−1.09 to −0.86eV), explaining its coordination versatility and higher reactivity. Overall, As(V) adsorption is strongly facet-dependent; enhancing (021) exposure is a promising strategy for tailoring goethite adsorbents, and findings provide a molecular-scale foundation for predicting As(V) mobility in oxic environments.

title: Depth-associated molecular differentiation of sediment dissolved organic matter shapes contrasting complexation responses of Cu and Cd in drinking water reservoirs
description: Publication date: Available online 5 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials Author(s): Jiafeng Zhang, Kexuan Zhang, Jingqi Yu, Saiyu Shang, Shilei Zhou
abstract: Water depth represents an important physical gradient across reservoir systems and is associated with systematic differences in sediment dissolved organic matter (SDOM) composition and its interactions with heavy metals (HMs). In drinking water reservoirs of North China, deep reservoirs (DR) showed higher Cd and Cu concentrations and higher potential ecological risk index (RI) than shallow reservoirs (SR). SDOM in both reservoir types was dominated by humic-like components. SR showed slightly higher biological index (BIX; 0.93 ± 0.13) and significantly higher Y fluorescence index (YFI; 1.25 ± 0.30), together with enrichment of protein-like molecules and molecules with higher molecular activity. In contrast, DR exhibited a higher proportion of humic-like components (69.93%), greater molecular diversity and a tendency toward a more unsaturated molecular composition. Fluorescence quenching showed that Cu2+ interacted with all four components C1–C4 (LogK a = 3.177–4.239), with an overall fluorescence-response sequence of tryptophan-like > humic-like > tyrosine-like, indicating a broad, multi-component response. In comparison, Cd2+-induced fluorescence response was mainly concentrated in C4, which exhibited a higher apparent LogK a for Cd2+ (4.818 ± 0.559) than for Cu2+ (3.748 ± 0.229). Overall, reservoirs with contrasting depth regimes exhibited systematic differences in SDOM source characteristics, molecular activity, and component structure, accompanied by distinct fluorescence-response patterns of Cu2+ and Cd2+. These findings indicate that SDOM compositional and metal-interaction characteristics provide complementary information to total metal concentrations and conventional sediment risk indices for characterizing sediment metal–organic interaction environments.

title: Seasonal variation in the spatial distribution, community assembly, and associated factors of antibiotic resistance genes in tropical drinking water reservoirs of Hainan, China
description: Publication date: Available online 4 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials Author(s): Luoxian Huang, Bo Chen, Xiaojin Liu, Zhiqiang Guo, Guoqianhui Zhang, Jingyu Li, Qiongyao Fu
abstract: Antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) have been widely investigated in temperate and subtropical reservoirs but remain poorly understood in tropical drinking-water reservoirs. We sampled four drinking-water reservoirs in Hainan during both winter and summer, integrating physicochemical, heavy-metal, and metagenomic data to investigate the diversity, spatiotemporal patterns, and assembly of ARGs, mobile genetic elements (MGEs), and microbial communities. ARG composition and community structure differed significantly by season and reservoir. Contig-based analysis identified ARG–MGE arrangements in diverse putative hosts; sul1 and qacEdelta1 co-occurred with integrases and transposases, demonstrating MGE co-localization. Null-model analysis indicated reservoir-specific ARG assembly in winter but predominantly stochastic assembly in summer, whereas microbial community assembly was deterministic in both seasons. Mantel and Spearman analyses showed seasonal variation in ARG relationships: stronger correlations with environmental factors in winter and more positive correlations with MGEs in summer. Summer co-occurrence networks were larger and more connected, with more positive ARG–MGE–microbial genus associations. Partial least squares path modeling (PLS-PM) showed positive MGE–ARG associations in both seasons, whereas microbial community composition was negatively associated with ARGs only in winter. These results characterize seasonal ARG variation and its associations with microbial communities and MGEs in tropical reservoirs, providing a baseline for monitoring regional drinking-water sources.

title: Uranium and arsenic partitioning and redox speciation among iron mineral assemblages along a Ningyo-toge mill tailings pond sediment core: Localized U(VI) reduction in siderite-bearing domains
description: Publication date: Available online 4 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials Author(s): Kohei Tokunaga, Yoshio Takahashi, Satoshi Mitsunobu, Yusuke Watanabe, Norito Takesue, Ayu Takemoto, Naofumi Kozai
abstract: Understanding the long-term mobility and retention of U and As in Fe-rich mine-impacted sediments requires resolving the relationship between Fe mineral assemblages and the partitioning and redox speciation of U and As. We investigated a 1m core from the Ningyo-toge mill tailings pond, Japan, using geochemical profiles, bulk and micro-XRF-XAFS, sequential extraction, and adsorption experiments. The shallow layer (0-40cm) was dominated by ferrihydrite, with an increasing contribution of goethite with depth, and retained U and As predominantly as U(VI) and As(V). The middle layer (40-60cm) contained goethite, hematite, magnetite, Fe(II)-bearing phyllosilicates, and minor pyrite and siderite, and showed the highest proportions of U(IV) and As(III). Below 60cm, goethite, hematite, magnetite, Fe(III)-bearing phyllosilicates, and minor siderite were present, while U(VI) and As(V) again became predominant. The 40-60cm layer showed the highest porewater U and As concentrations, suggesting that reductive transformation and dissolution of Fe(III) (hydr)oxides may have contributed to their release. Adsorption experiments showed mineral-specific U and As partitioning, with siderite showing the greatest U(VI) reduction under experimental conditions. Micro-XRF-XAFS revealed localized partial U(VI) reduction in siderite-bearing domains within ferrihydrite-rich shallow sediment under oxidizing conditions. These findings highlight the importance of Fe mineral assemblages and particle-scale heterogeneity in evaluating the long-term retention and mobility of U and As in Fe-rich tailings sediments.

title: Simultaneous cesium desorption and surfactant degradation from montmorillonite by coupled capacitive deionization–electro-oxidation
description: Publication date: Available online 4 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials Author(s): Jiaxin Hu, Sebastian Gonzalez Ramirez, Huagui Zhang, Jae W. Lee, Timothy N. Hunter, David Harbottle
abstract: Remediation of cesium-contaminated clay minerals is difficult because Cs+ is strongly retained within collapsed interlayer spaces. Cationic surfactants can promote Cs+ release, but residual surfactant creates a secondary pollution risk requiring post-treatment. Here, a coupled capacitive deionization–electro-oxidation (CDI-EO) system using a boron-doped diamond (BDD) anode and activated carbon cathode was developed for one-step Cs+ desorption and in situ surfactant degradation from Cs-saturated montmorillonite (0.95mmolg-1, 85% of cation exchange capacity, CEC). Electrochemical degradation of dodecyltrimethylammonium bromide (DTAB) was first optimised in a static electrolytic cell, reaching ~96% degradation at 150mAcm-2 after 12h for a DTAB loading of 0.5 × CEC. These conditions (150mAcm-2, 0.4M Na2SO4, pH 7) were then applied in a recirculating flow-by CDI cell at 20mLmin-1. Within 6h, DTAB degradation reached 84–89% and Cs+ desorption up to ~89%, with maximum Cs+ release within 1h due to surfactant-induced interlayer expansion and electric-field-driven ion extraction. XRD showed interlayer contraction to 1.22–1.25nm after treatment, confirming effective surfactant removal from the clay structure. Over five consecutive cycles, Cs+ desorption remained ~70% and surfactant degradation exceeded 80%, demonstrating sustained treatment performance. Electrical energy consumption was 129–140 kWh kg-1 clay for the dilute laboratory batches studied, and the electrosorption capacity of the unmodified AC cathode is identified as the bottleneck for net Cs⁺ capture. The integrated CDI-EO process therefore provides a simplified single-step route for radionuclide-contaminated clay remediation, simultaneously combining decontamination and surfactant removal while avoiding a separate post-treatment stage for disposal.

title: Pangolin scales as a potential retrospective biomonitoring matrix for environmental and rescue-associated chemical exposures in endangered wildlife
description: Publication date: Available online 4 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials Author(s): Lu-Chi Lin, Nick Ching-Min Sun, Yu-Min Tzou, Sichao Wang, Hou-Feng Li, Shiou-Ruei Lin, Shan-An Chan, Hsiao-Ying Yang, Cheng-Hua Liu, Ya-Hui Chuang
abstract: Pangolins are among the world's most trafficked and endangered mammals, yet their exposure to emerging organic contaminants (EOCs) remains largely uncharacterized. Their keratinous scales represent an untapped matrix for potentially non-invasive biomonitoring. This study developed and validated a modified QuEChERS-based extraction coupled with liquid chromatography–quadrupole time-of-flight mass spectrometry (LC-QTOF/MS) for suspect screening and targeted quantification of EOCs in pangolin scales. The workflow was applied to scales collected from 18 deceased wild Formosan pangolins (Manis pentadactyla pentadactyla) with and without documented rescue histories. A total of 57 EOCs spanning six chemical classes were tentatively identified, reflecting environmental contamination and rescue-associated pharmaceutical exposure. Eight EOCs were further selected and confirmed as targets. The method achieved recoveries of 70–120%, relative standard deviations ≤20%, and method detection limits ranging from 0.1 to 2.0µgkg−1. Target EOC concentrations spanned nearly four orders of magnitude, from 0.84µgkg−1 (isoxaflutole) to 15,400µgkg−1 (enrofloxacin). Compositional and quantitative EOC patterns showed substantial inter-individual variation and rescue-associated pharmaceutical signatures. This study provides the first report of multiple EOC residues in pangolin scales, supporting their further evaluation as a potential retrospective biomonitoring matrix for wildlife conservation across the family Manidae.

title: Characterizing Crop-Differentiated Hazardous Pollutant Emissions from Residue Open Buring: An Integrated Multi-Source Satellite and Phenological Metrics Coupling Approach
description: Publication date: Available online 4 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials Author(s): Ying Zhou, Caixu Yang, Wanting Zhang, Jianlei Lang, Wenhan Zhang, Wenyue Zhang, Dongsheng Chen, Shuiyuan Cheng
abstract: Crop residue open burning (CROB) is a significant global source of hazardous air pollutants, posing acute and chronic health risks and transboundary pollution episodes. Current remote sensing-based emission estimates generally overlook crop-type differences and apply uniform combustion parameters, limiting the characterization of crop-specific combustion and emission heterogeneity. To address this gap, we developed a crop-specific emission estimation framework by integrating multi-source satellite-derived fire radiative power (FRP) data with crop distribution and phenological information to characterize crop-specific variations in combustion characteristics and emission spatiotemporal patterns. The results showed that different crop residues exhibited distinct combustion characteristics. Specifically, the maximum burning duration for wheat residue (9h) was shorter than that for rice and corn (13h), while rice and corn residues showed faster FRP growth and reached their peak FRP earlier during combustion. These differences indicate that crop residues exhibit distinct FRP temporal evolution patterns, underscoring the necessity of adopting mathematical distribution models and combustion parameters that can characterize crop-specific burning behaviors. In terms of emissions, corn residue burning dominated CROB emissions, contributing 43.0%-67.3% of various pollutants, and its PM2.5 emission per unit residue yield (emission intensity) was 1.3-1.5 times higher than those of rice and wheat. Substantial regional heterogeneity was observed; for the same crop, PM2.5 emission intensity varied by up to 16 times across different regions. This study provides a methodological framework for crop-specific CROB emission estimation and develops a high-resolution, crop-specific emission inventory, offering essential data support for air quality modeling, health risk assessment, and targeted CROB management.

title: Mechanisms of organic pollutant removal and residual carbon evolution from pharmaceutical waste salts via molten bubble-enhanced oxidation
description: Publication date: Available online 4 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials Author(s): Wuyang Xiao, Yuxian Wang, Xian Li, Xiaodong Chen, Pin Liu, Jinjun Guo, Congbin Jiang, Zehua Li, Hongyun Hu, Guangqian Luo, Hong Yao
abstract: Pharmaceutical waste salts (PWS) pose severe environmental risks. High-temperature melting coupled with oxidizing gas bubbling shows great potential for organic pollutant removal. However, the underlying transformation mechanisms and evolutionary behavior of residual carbonaceous species remain unclear, hindering process optimization. To fill this gap, this study investigates carbon partitioning among gas, tar, water‑soluble and water-insoluble solid fractions during molten bubble-enhanced oxidation (MBEO) of PWS by a self-constructed reactor. MBEO reduces the TOC in treated salts to 19.6mg/kg with 99.5% removal efficiency at 1000 ℃ within 20min. Elevated temperatures accelerate organic pollutant removal while exacerbating incomplete oxidation. Residual organic carbonaceous species consist of water-insoluble amorphous carbon, water-soluble humic-like, tyrosine-like, and tryptophan-like substances. As the reaction proceeds Partial water‑insoluble fractions convert into water-soluble fractions. Residual amorphous carbon undergoes a two‑stage structural evolution. Polycondensation and aromatization dominate to drive rapidly structural ordering in the initial stage, followed by framework rearrangement enabling further slow ordering. Meanwhile, continuous cleavage and oxidation of weak organic bonds within amorphous carbon detach partial organic species, which are transformed into water-soluble humic‑like and tyrosine‑like substances. This study clarifies organic carbon transformation during molten oxidation, providing mechanistic insights for PWS purification and guidance for optimization MBEO technology.

title: Associations of Ambient Fine Particulate Matter Exposure with Metal and Metalloid Concentrations in Follicular Fluid
description: Publication date: Available online 4 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials Author(s): Qingqing Tao, Yujie Zhou, Tian Tian, Rui Yang, Fei Kong, Qin Li, Rong Li, Jie Qiao
abstract: Ambient fine particulate matter (PM2.5) contains metals and metalloids, but whether long-term exposure is associated with element concentrations in human follicular fluid remains unclear. Here, we examined this association in a cross-sectional study of 198 women undergoing assisted reproductive technology. Twelve-month residential PM2.5 exposure before oocyte retrieval was modeled at 1-km resolution, and 14 elements were measured in follicular fluid. Multivariable linear regression models estimated percentage changes and 95% confidence intervals (CIs), with false discovery rate (FDR) correction. An interquartile-range increase in PM2.5 was associated with higher follicular-fluid concentrations of chromium [22.10% (95% CI: 9.59%, 36.04%)], lead [23.15% (95% CI: 1.27%, 49.76%)], cadmium [22.81% (95% CI: 8.95%, 38.44%)], arsenic [29.25% (95% CI: 8.13%, 54.49%)], germanium [15.72% (95% CI: 4.42%, 28.25%)], and lithium [25.84% (95% CI: 9.65%, 44.43%)]. Associations with five elements remained statistically significant after FDR correction, whereas the association with lead did not. This study links ambient PM2.5 exposure to measured element concentrations in human follicular fluid, providing evidence from the ovarian microenvironment. Prospective studies should evaluate whether these elements mediate associations between PM2.5 exposure and ovarian function or assisted-reproduction outcomes. Integrating personal exposure monitoring and source apportionment could clarify exposure pathways and inform reproductive health risk assessment.

title: Corrigendum to “Fermi-level pinning and internal electric field engineering in S-scheme titanium dioxide/bismuth molybdate for fast mineralization of gaseous formaldehyde” [J Hazard Mater 514 (2026) 142655]

title: When co-occurrence becomes risk: a SOURCE–FATE–DOSE–EFFECT–DECISION framework for microplastic-PFAS interactions, food-chain transfer, and dietary safety
description: Publication date: Available online 4 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials Author(s): Ankur Biswas, Anuj Sharma, Sindhu Varshini Bai
abstract: Microplastics and per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) co-occur across wastewater, landfill leachate, sediments, agricultural soils, stormwater, aquatic food webs, and food-contact systems, yet their risks are often assessed separately. We synthesize quantitative evidence showing that PFAS sorption and release from microplastics depend on polymer identity, PFAS chain length, particle size, field conditioning, and matrix chemistry. Reported patterns include chain-length-dependent sorption, field enrichment on environmentally conditioned particles, greater PFOS sorption by smaller polyethylene particles, and 76.8–77.6% PFOS release from polyethylene microplastics under simulated fish digestive conditions. We propose a SOURCE–FATE–DOSE–EFFECT–DECISION (SFDED) framework that classifies microplastics as sinks, vectors, secondary sources, or co-stressors according to role-specific evidence requirements and extends these roles to farm-to-fork pathways. The framework distinguishes co-occurrence, bioaccessibility, absorbed internal dose, and biological effect, and links research goals to the minimum measurements needed to support each claim. Applying this framework identifies seven priority gaps: human gut-fluid desorption, mammalian internal dosimetry, mixture toxicity in human-relevant systems, dietary PFAS exposure estimation, food-related microplastic standards, treatment removal of particle-bound PFAS, and systematic synthesis across a broader primary-study base. Together, this approach provides a transparent basis for interpreting microplastic–PFAS interactions and prioritizing evidence needed for food-safety assessment, monitoring, treatment decisions, and risk management.

title: Bridging HRMS spectra and anti-Staphylococcus aureus activity by machine learning for prioritization of putative antibacterial contaminants in wastewater
description: Publication date: Available online 4 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials Author(s): Shuyang Feng, Shuran Li, Xiaoping Shi, Ming Ying, Minxin Ji, Jingya Lou, Xu Yan, Gang Wu, Xu-Xiang Zhang
abstract: Antibacterial contaminants are an increasing environmental and public health concern, yet prioritizing compounds with potential antibacterial activity in wastewater remains challenging. We developed machine learning models linking MS/MS-derived probabilistic fingerprints to activity against Staphylococcus aureus, enabling activity-guided prioritization before structural elucidation. Among 36 machine learning and deep learning configurations across different algorithms and fingerprint representations, MLP_PubChem and XGBoost_PubChem achieved the highest observed test F1 scores in positive- and negative-ion modes, respectively (0.48 and 0.42; AUROC, 0.84 for both). SHAP analysis examined feature contributions in positive-ion RF_Both and negative-ion XGBoost_PubChem. For wastewater screening, positive-ion MLP_Both (test F1, 0.475; AUROC, 0.847) and negative-ion XGBoost_PubChem prioritized 89 of 3,797 successfully scored features, reducing the immediate follow-up list by 97.66%. Database searches yielded 39 candidate annotations for structural investigation. Retrospective screening identified MS/MS matches to prioritized candidate features in public wastewater datasets from multiple geographical regions. A web application is available at https://huggingface.co/spaces/dgfhdu/P-A to support candidate screening. By focusing structural elucidation on features with predicted anti-S. aureus activity, this workflow supports non-targeted screening guided by biological activity.

title: Polystyrene Nanoplastic Exposure Exacerbates Epileptic Vulnerability in SCN1A Mutation Models
description: Publication date: Available online 3 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials Author(s): Jeong Hyeon Jo, Sung Bum Park, Won Hoon Jung, Jangjae Lee, Seong Soon Kim, Woorin Seo, Jeonghui Im, Kyoung Jin Choi, Byumseok Koh, Hye Jin Nam, Myung Ae Bae, Sung-Hee Cho, Ki Young Kim
abstract: Micro- and nanoplastics are pervasive contaminants detected in human tissues that cross the blood–brain barrier to induce neuroinflammation, apoptosis, and neurotoxicity. Here, we examined whether polystyrene nanoplastic (PS-NP) exposure alters seizure susceptibility in SCN1A +/− cerebral organoids and Scn1a +/− mice, modeling the severe genetic epilepsy Dravet syndrome. At equal mass concentrations, 50nm PS-NPs penetrated organoids more deeply and upregulated inflammatory and neurotoxic gene expression more robustly than 100nm particles, inducing apoptotic activation and significant DNA fragmentation. Exposure disrupted steroid homeostasis—causing genotype-dependent cortisol elevations—and perturbed neurotransmitter systems in SCN1A-deficient models via reduced GABA and glutamate, accompanied by decreased GAD2 and increased VGLUT2 expression. In vivo, exposed Scn1a +/− mice exhibited hyperactivity and reached Racine stages 3 to 5 more rapidly under thermal induction, demonstrating a reduced seizure threshold. Pharmacological inhibition of 11β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 1 reversed this hyperactivity but failed to restore the seizure threshold. Together, these findings indicate that PS-NP exposure exacerbates seizure vulnerability in genetically susceptible backgrounds, accompanied by marked neurochemical, endocrine, and apoptotic disruptions. These results support a 'second-hit' model wherein environmental nanoplastics act as external triggers in genetic epilepsy, underscoring the vital need to incorporate gene–environment interactions into neurotoxicological risk assessments.

title: Arsenite channel aquaporin PvNIP2;1 drives arsenic transport and sequestration in hyperaccumulator Pteris vittata
description: Publication date: Available online 3 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials Author(s): Dan Sun, Wenjing Tian, Xiang Zhang, Tian Qiu, Huiyu Shao, Yanzhao Bi, Huayuan Feng, Yetao Tang, Lena Q. Ma, Yue Cao, Rongliang Qiu
abstract: Phytoremediation of arsenic (As)-contaminated soil is critical for mitigating soil contamination and protecting food safety. The first-known As-hyperaccumulator Pteris vittata effectively takes up As from contaminated soil. However, the molecular mechanisms behind its efficient AsIII accumulation are unclear. Among the eight aquaporin PvNIP members identified in P. vittata, AsIII channel PvNIP2;1 exhibits high AsIII permeability and has a typical F−A−A−R selectivity filter with a predicted pore diameter of 5.9Å, based on AlphaFold modeling of its 3D structure. Expression of PvNIP2;1 in yeast mutant ∆acr3 confirmed its role in AsIII transport but not its chemical-analog silicon, unlike its homolog OsLsi1 in rice. In transgenic Arabidopsis thaliana, PvNIP2;1 enhanced shoot As accumulation by 292% under AsIII treatment and by 75% in As-contaminated soil. The 118% higher expression of PvNIP2;1 in the fronds than roots, and being localized on the plasma membrane of frond epidermal cells implicate its role for AsIII influx into frond cells, essential for efficient As accumulation in P. vittata fronds. Additionally, coupling PvNIP2;1 expression with limited AsV reduction further increased shoot As accumulation by 106% in A. thaliana. Our results reveal an unreported aquaporin with AsIII permeability critical for As hyperaccumulation in P. vittata and provide a key molecular component for engineering more complete As accumulation pathways for phytoremediation.

title: Environmental Media–Based Microbial Source Tracking Enables Source Identification of Antimicrobial Resistance in Urban Rivers
description: Publication date: Available online 3 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials Author(s): Muhammad Adnan Sabar, Than Van Huy, Yoshinori Sugie, Hiroyuki Wada, Bo Zhao, Norihisa Matsuura, Masaru Ihara, Toru Watanabe, Hiroaki Tanaka, Ryo Honda
abstract: Urban rivers receiving treated wastewater remain hotspots for antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs), yet quantitative source attribution remains challenging. Conventional microbial source tracking (MST) cannot distinguish ARG contributions from treated effluent, untreated sewage, and environmental reservoirs such as sediments. Here, we developed an environmental media-based MST (EM-MST) framework integrating source-enriched microbial markers to quantify ARG sources in an urban river impacted by two wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) and combined sewer overflow (CSO). From fifteen screened markers, NOB-16S (effluent-enriched nitrite-oxidizing bacteria), dsrA (sediment-enriched sulfate-reducing bacteria), and crAssphage (sewage-associated) were selected using qPCR validation and multivariate analysis. Combined with shotgun metagenomic profiling of 676 ARGs and a non-negative least squares mixing model, these markers enabled source attribution. During dry weather, WWTP effluent accounted for the largest source proportion (81.5–93.1%), with efflux pump, sulfonamide, macrolide, and aminoglycoside ARGs. During the sampled CSO event, untreated sewage accounted for 91%–100% of the estimated source contribution, delivering β-lactam, macrolide–lincosamide–streptogramin, and tetracycline ARGs associated with gut microbiota. River sediments showed greater resistome similarity to WWTP effluent, consistent with an effluent-associated ARG reservoir, while the estimated sediment contribution remained minor (3.0 ± 5.3%). The EM-MST enables quantitative differentiation of ARG sources in wastewater-impacted urban rivers.

title: Behavior of radionuclides in high temperature combustion processes: A radiological hazard?
description: Publication date: Available online 3 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials Author(s): Juan C. Mora, Fco. Javier Guillen, A. Salas
abstract: High temperature combustion processes, such as combustion of fossil fuels or biomass for energy production, tobacco smoking, organic waste incineration, or wildfire events in forests, are governed by the same physical, chemical, and thermal mechanisms that control the partitioning, enrichment, migration, volatilization, and condensation of radionuclides, either anthropogenic or naturally occurring, which may pose a significant radiological hazard to the environment and to human health. A review was carried out up to the end of 2025, using a PRISMA-style workflow. In this review, those combustion scenarios are presented within a common mechanistic framework to better understand the behavior of primordial and anthropogenic radionuclides under these conditions. Modeling and empirical results under controlled conditions show that radionuclide volatility drives the different activity concentrations when comparing heavy bottom ashes, lighter fly ashes, and flue gases (smoke). Enrichment factors can vary by orders of magnitude depending on temperature profiles, redox conditions, chlorine, sulfur and calcium content, and particle size distributions. Radioisotopes of volatile elements and compounds, such as C 137 s under chlorine-rich atmosphere conditions, or P 210 o, or P 210 b exhibit preferential condensation on fine particulate matter ( < 2.5 μ m), whereas refractory elements and compounds, including isotopes of uranium, thorium, plutonium, or americium, concentrate in heavier fractions. In particular, C 137 s, P 210 o and P 210 b can show enrichment factors of up to 1000 times in fine particles due to vapour and condensation mechanisms, following an inverse correlation between radioactivity and particle diameter. This fact is relevant as the inhalation of submicron particles ( < 1 μ m) may constitute one of the primary exposure pathways, and thus a radiological hazard, with combined-exposure implications with other co-contaminants, like heavy metals or organic toxics, which are often present in the gases of combustion processes. A structured synthesis was developed, highlighting where this framework is applicable, and providing advice on future research on radionuclide speciation in high-temperature, ultrafine-particle characterisation, weathering of aged ash, small and dispersed combustion sources, and the effect of modern ultra-low-emission retrofits and biomass co-firing on radionuclide partitioning.

title: Coupled PFAS defluorination and fluoride immobilization in sewage sludge via calcium-mediated alkaline hydrothermal treatment: the role of sludge-derived hydroxyapatite
description: Publication date: Available online 3 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials Author(s): Renjie Chen, Shijie Yuan, Bin Dong, Zuxin Xu
abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in wastewater accumulate in sewage sludge (SS) and may enter soils through land application. This study investigates Ca-mediated alkaline hydrothermal treatment (AHT-Ca) for coupled PFAS defluorination with fluoride immobilization, with hydroxyapatite (HAP) formed from endogenous sludge phosphorus contributing to enhanced defluorination. At 240 °C, AHT-Ca achieved an apparent defluorination efficiency of 84.3% for extractable organic fluorine (EOF). Concurrently, 90.2% of the released fluoride was immobilized in mineral phases, predominantly as CaF₂. Model-compound experiments with sludge-derived HAP synthesized at different pH values suggested a key role for surface nucleophilic reactivity in HAP-mediated defluorination during alkaline hydrothermal treatment (AHT). Higher synthesis pH increased the density of strong Lewis basic sites on HAP, particularly Ca-[O2-]-Ca sites, with defluorination efficiencies reaching 97.4% for PFOA and 73.7% for PFOS at 240 °C. In situ spectroscopy and density functional theory (DFT) calculations provided insight into the interfacial defluorination mechanism on sludge-derived HAP, in which Ca-associated Lewis acidic sites facilitated PFAS enrichment, whereas strong oxygen-containing Lewis basic sites (Ca-[O2-]-Ca) promoted nucleophilic C-F bond activation. These findings demonstrate the potential of regulating sludge-derived mineral formation and surface reactivity to couple defluorination with fluoride immobilization, offering a viable strategy for mitigating sludge PFAS pollution.

title: Engineering the electronic structure of LaCoO 3 nanofibers via Cu doping for efficient electrocatalytic ammonia synthesis
description: Publication date: Available online 2 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials Author(s): Bingyan Shi, Mingze Xia, Siqi Zhang, Cheng Fan, Shengji Tian, Chade Lv, Xiaofeng Lu
abstract: Electrocatalytic nitrate reduction reaction (NO3RR) to ammonia is a promising alternative to the Haber-Bosch process, but suffers from slow kinetics, complex mechanism, and competing reactions. In this work, B-site Cu-doped LaCoO3 (ABO3-type) perovskite nanofibers (NFs) are successfully fabricated through a high-voltage electrospinning-calcination technique for NO3RR. The optimized 5% Cu-LaCoO3 NFs catalyst exhibits an outstanding Faradaic efficiency (FE) amounting to 98.7 ± 0.5% under –0.483V vs. RHE. An NH3 generation rate of 27.6 ± 0.6mgcm⁻2 h⁻1 is recorded at –0.683V vs. RHE, significantly exceeding that of pristine LaCoO3 NFs. Moreover, when employed as the cathode in an assembled aqueous cell, the catalyst delivers a peak power density of 5.58mWcm⁻2 and shows reasonable long-term charge-discharge stability. Through physicochemical analyses and density functional theory (DFT) computations, it is demonstrated that substituting Cu at the B‑site of LaCoO3 enhances orbital mixing between Cu 3d and O 2p states, tunes the adsorption behavior of Co, and modifies the electronic configuration of LaCoO3, thereby lowering the activation barrier for NO3RR. This work presents an innovative strategy for designing advanced electrocatalysts capable of both NH3 electrosynthesis and power generation, offering a promising route toward sustainable energy conversion.

title: Editing of SpNRAMP3 , SpCAX3 , and SpHMA3 differentially affects cadmium concentrations and growth responses in Sedum plumbizincicola
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Xiaotong Wu, Yixin Zhang, Yanlan Mo, Huan Liu, Longhua Wu, Hongxu Ren, Yaping Zhang, Wenzhong Xu
abstract: Sedum plumbizincicola is a Cd/Zn hyperaccumulator with exceptional Cd tolerance and shoot accumulation capacity. Here, bioinformatic analysis, subcellular localization, heterologous expression in yeast, and CRISPR/Cas9-mediated genome editing were combined to characterize the role of SpNRAMP3 in Cd homeostasis and tissue Cd allocation and its functional relationships with SpCAX3 and SpHMA3. SpNRAMP3 encodes a protein with 11 predicted transmembrane domains and shows a localization pattern consistent with tonoplast association; it is expressed in roots, stems and leaves and displays Cd-responsive expression. Heterologous expression of SpNRAMP3 in yeast increased cellular Cd accumulation and conferred Cd hypersensitivity. Two independent SpNRAMP3-edited lines showed greater Cd sensitivity and lower Cd concentrations in young leaves, supporting a role for SpNRAMP3 in Cd homeostasis, growth response, and tissue Cd allocation. Heterologous expression of SpCAX3 also altered cellular Cd accumulation and Cd sensitivity in yeast. Compared with the wild type, the spnramp3spcax3 double-edited lines showed 72.5–79.8% lower Cd concentrations in young leaves and reduced relative growth inhibition under Cd stress, whereas the spnramp3sphma3 lines showed 28.2–58.6% lower Cd concentrations in young leaves but substantially greater growth inhibition. These results suggest that SpHMA3 primarily mediates vacuolar Cd sequestration, whereas SpNRAMP3 and SpCAX3 may contribute to Cd homeostasis and tissue Cd allocation through distinct but functionally connected processes. These proteins may act together to support Cd hyperaccumulation and hypertolerance in S. plumbizincicola. This study provides a framework for understanding Cd homeostasis and tissue Cd allocation in hyperaccumulator plants and identifies candidate targets for genome-editing-based improvement of phytoremediation.

title: Seasonal hydrological regulation influences the spatiotemporal dynamics of dissolved organic matter and heavy metals in cascade reservoirs
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Ju Gao, Chunhui Li, Xiong Zhou, Yujun Yi, Xuan Wang, Qiang Liu
abstract: Cascade reservoirs have drastically altered natural hydrological cycles and material transport in rivers, yet their effects on pollutant migration remain unclear. Here, we present an attribution analysis framework based on field sampling to elucidate the spatiotemporal dynamics, association pathways, and influencing factors of dissolved organic matter (DOM) and heavy metals in the upper Yellow River cascade reservoirs. The results indicate that cascade reservoirs exert pronounced seasonal hydrological regulation on DOM and heavy metals. During wet-season impoundment, hydrochemical conditions may promote the shift of DOM from terrestrial humic-like to autochthonous protein-like dominance, with lower heavy metal concentrations. During the dry season, DOM transformation may be suppressed, with humic-like DOM dominant and heavy metal concentrations higher than in the wet season, while outflow concentrations remain lower than inflow despite increased total flux. Hydrochemical and DOM variables jointly explain 58% of heavy metal variation, with DOM-related variables contributing 67.78% of explained variation; hydrochemical factors may mainly be associated with heavy metals indirectly through DOM. Seasonal reservoir regulation and tributary recharge along the cascade contribute to longitudinal fluctuations in DOM and heavy metal distributions. Understanding the transport and influence mechanisms of DOM and heavy metals is critical for watershed water security and pollution control.

title: Carbon–iron co-enrichment on rice rhizoplane is associated with Fe plaque crystallization and persistent Cd immobilization: A five-year field study
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Fanyi Kong, Zhao-Feng Yuan, Zhiqiang Wang, Hanzhong Jia, Zhiping Yang, Qiang Zhang, Minggang Xu, Shenggao Lu
abstract: Cadmium (Cd) contamination in paddy soils threatens rice safety, yet the longevity of amendment-based immobilization remains uncertain. Here, a five-year field experiment investigated Cd migration across the soil–root–rice continuum after a single application of lime or oyster shell powder (OS). Both amendments reduced brown-rice Cd in the first year, but only OS maintained the effect; after five years, grain Cd remained at 0.11 mg kg⁻¹ , below the food-safety limit of 0.20 mg kg⁻¹ and lower than the control (0.23 mg kg⁻¹) and lime treatment (0.20 mg kg⁻¹). Sequential extraction and cross-niche metagenomic analyses revealed pronounced carbon–iron (C–Fe) co-enrichment at the rhizoplane under OS treatment. OS increased operationally defined poorly crystalline Fe-associated fractions and extractable organic C, accompanied by greater Cd partitioning within rhizoplane Fe-associated pools. Metagenomic analyses further revealed enrichment of carbohydrate-active enzyme families and Cd-resistance-associated genes at the OS rhizoplane. These findings indicate that persistent rhizoplane C–Fe associations are associated with enhanced Cd retention at the root–soil interface and may contribute to the long-term performance of oyster shell amendment under field conditions.

title: Analysis and prediction of tissue-specific bioconcentration factors of organophosphate esters in silver salmon ( Oncorhynchus kisutch ) using machine learning
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Xiaofang Che, Hongliang Jia, Zijun Xiao, Zhaowei Wang, Wen-Jun Hong, Song Cui, Zhe Lin, Yi-Fan Li, Dan Xu
abstract: Organophosphate esters (OPEs), widely used flame retardants, are ubiquitous aquatic contaminants that pose significant risks to ecological and public health. The bioconcentration factor (BCF) is a key metric for assessing the ecological risks of OPE bioconcentration. Here, we quantified the bioconcentration of 10 OPEs across 11 biological matrices (10 solid tissues and serum) in silver salmon via in vivo exposure. Adipose tissue exhibited the highest average BCF, with moderate levels in the intestine, liver, kidney, and brain, and comparatively lower accumulation in the remaining tissues. To explain and predict tissue-specific accumulation, we developed mixed and structure-only models using thirteen machine learning algorithms. The optimal eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) mixed model achieved high predictive accuracy (R2 test = 0.882, RMSE = 0.250) and captured nonlinear patterns. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis identified tissue lipid content, liver clearance rate, and water content as the primary determinants of bioconcentration, followed by the molecular descriptor BCUT2D_MWLOW. This model revealed that tissue physiological properties are important factors for OPE bioconcentration. Feature interaction analysis further revealed synergies between lipid content and BCUT2D_MWLOW. This study offers mechanistic insights into OPE tissue distribution and a modeling framework for refined risk assessment.

title: Microplastics in a large Brazilian bay: Multispecies bivalve approach reveals an association with population density
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Thaiza Maria Avelino Soares, Victor Vasques Ribeiro, Ana Cecília Rizzatti de Albergaria-Barbosa, Raimara S. Gomes, Andreia N. Fernandes, Ítalo Braga Castro
abstract: Microplastic contamination is pervasive across aquatic ecosystems, including protected coastal environments. Todos os Santos Bay, the second-largest bay in Brazil, encompasses 1385 km² within a multiple-use marine protected area and supports over three million inhabitants, major port activities, petrochemical industries, mangrove forests, and coral reefs. Here, we assessed microplastic contamination using three filter-feeding bivalve species as sentinels, and evaluated its associations with population density, human modification, socioeconomic deprivation, and distance to river discharges using Crassostrea sp., the only species sampled at all 16 sites. A total of 834 microplastics were detected, with average concentrations of 3.21, 2.88, and 2.36 particles g-1 in clams, oysters, and mussels, respectively. These concentrations exceeded the literature-based Brazilian average for bivalves (2.06 particles g-1), indicating comparatively elevated contamination levels in Todos os Santos Bay. Microplastic contamination was widespread across Todos os Santos Bay despite all sampling sites being located within a multiple-use protected area. No consistent overall differences in microplastic concentrations were detected among species; however, a significant Species × Site interaction indicated that interspecific differences varied across sampling sites. Fibers, small and transparent particles predominated, whereas anthropogenic cellulose accounted for 56.8% of the spectroscopically characterized subset. Population density received the strongest statistical support among the evaluated socio-environmental predictors and was positively associated with microplastic concentrations in oysters. This spatial association highlights the importance of reducing land-based microplastic inputs in densely populated coastal areas through improved wastewater treatment, urban drainage, and solid waste management.

title: Exogenous granular activated carbon (GAC) promotes the biogenic oxidative dissolution of rhodochrosite and the degradation of pollutants: Insights from extracellular superoxide radical generation, key enzyme activities and transcriptomic analysis
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Huawei Wang, Fei Wang, Xinlei Duan, Yingjie Sun, Lei Gao, Ya-nan Wang
abstract: The oxidative dissolution of rhodochrosite (MnCO3) affects the availability of divalent Mn(II) ions and regulates the content of manganese oxides in aquatic environments; however, the effects of exogenous particles on the bacterial oxidation of rhodochrosite and the degradation of pollutants have not been elucidated. In this study, the underlying molecular mechanisms of the bacterial oxidative dissolution of rhodochrosite in the presence of granular active carbon (GAC) were investigated. After 120 h of reaction, the concentration of biogenic MnO2 in situ-generated reached 24.76 mg/L in the MnCO3@GAC system, which was significantly greater than the concentrations observed in the treatments with pure MnCO3 (18.43 mg/L) and dissolved Mn(II) (10.50 mg/L) (p < 0.05). GAC promoted the formation of organic acids and significantly upregulated the expression levels of genes associated with Mn ion transmembrane transport activity, biofilm formation, electron-transferring and oxidoreductases, facilitating the oxidative dissolution of rhodochrosite. Extracellular superoxide radicals served as the dominant reactive oxygen species (ROS) for the biogenic oxidation of rhodochrosite in the MnCO3@GAC system. The biogenic oxidation of MnCO3@GAC resulted in excellent degradation efficiency for phenylarsonic acid (PAA). The degradation efficiency of PAA was significantly greater than those of the MnCO3 and MnB1 treatments, which could efficiently remove 92.5% PAA. These findings provide new insights into the biogeochemical cycles of rhodochrosite.

title: Molecular insight of U-As-Cd synergistic mineralization and metabolic responses mediated by Brevundimonas spp.
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Aishu Li, Lin Yu, Shuyan Mi, Zhongqiang Hu, Qi Liao, Weichun Yang, Qingzhu Li, Mengying Si, Nan Hu, Guangyue Li, Zhihui Yang
abstract: A novel promising environmentally friendly remediation method by As(III)-oxidizing bacteria has been demonstrated to facilitate the synergistic biomineralization for Uranium (U), Arsenic (As) and Cadmium (Cd). However, the underlying remediation mechanism remains unclear. Herein, the process of synergistic mineralization of U, As, and Cd and the metabolic response of Brevundimonas spp. were revealed. Brevundimonas spp. enhanced the synergistic removal efficiencies of 27.54, 18.17 and 19.93 times for U, As and Cd comparing with the chemical methods, respectively. Precipitates were formed initially on the bacterial cell surface, and gradually released into the extracellular matrix concomitant with a transformation from low-crystallinity phase to crystalline phases. The protein-protein interaction (PPI) results revealed that the proteins involved in the As(III) oxidation phase primarily mediated the interactions among electron transfer-related proteins. The addition of U and Cd further strengthened the link of electron transfer with the Na+/H+ transporter, ATPase, and superoxide dismutase (SOD). The expression differences in oxidative phosphorylation reflect the self-regulatory capacity of Brevundimonas spp. in response to heavy metal oxidation and synergistic mineralization. Our study provides a molecular insight by which As(III)-oxidizing bacteria enhance to simultaneously remove U, As and Cd in the mining wastewater.

title: Multimodal deep learning for species-aware prediction of chemical toxicity to aquatic plants
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Zhixuan Yin, Jieming Li
abstract: Ecological hazard assessment relies on toxicity data spanning multiple species, yet experimental toxicity testing for aquatic plants remains costly, labor-intensive, and time-consuming. Computational approaches offer an efficient alternative, but existing models are typically tailored to a small number of individual species or a single taxonomic group, limiting their utility for multispecies ecological risk assessment. Here we present Aquatic Multimodal Toxicity predictor Learning (AMTox-L), a multimodal deep learning model for predicting acute chemical toxicity in aquatic plants. By jointly encoding molecular graph structure, physicochemical descriptors, taxonomic information, and exposure duration, the model integrates toxicity-relevant features across both chemical and biological dimensions. AMTox-L performed consistently on the independent test set and achieved lower prediction error than both ECOSAR and TRIDENT on the common-coverage external benchmark. The model also captured taxonomic differences in sensitivity using biological context resolved to the genus level. When integrated with field phytoplankton community data, AMTox-L enabled reconstruction of community-weighted species sensitivity distributions and estimation of community-informed hazardous concentration for 5% of species (HC5)/predicted no effect concentration (PNEC) values with propagated uncertainty. Together, these results suggest that multimodal deep learning could advance aquatic plant toxicity prediction and support more refined, context-aware ecological risk assessment.

title: Interfacial charge filtering sustains photocatalytic antibiotic transformation in irrigation return waters and attenuates residual biological effects
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Yaohua Yu, Quanquan Shi, Xueke Deng, Yushuai Jia, Yanpeng Gao, Yang-Guang Gu
abstract: Antibiotic transformation in irrigation return waters is constrained by matrix interference, while parent-compound disappearance does not ensure attenuation of residual biological effects. Here, “interfacial charge filtering” describes the treatment-relevant outcome of an S-scheme-like interface—preferential recombination of weak-redox-capacity carriers and retention of strongly reductive electrons and oxidative holes—rather than a distinct charge-transfer mechanism. This concept was evaluated using a tubular Na2Ti3O7/CuInS2 photocatalyst. T/CIS-8 achieved 81.9% apparent ciprofloxacin (CIP) removal and 49.5% total organic carbon (TOC) removal within 60 min. In situ X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy and femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy supported interfacial electron redistribution and heterointerface-modified carrier-relaxation dynamics. Quenching and electron paramagnetic resonance measurements identified holes and superoxide radicals (•O2 −) as the dominant reactive species, supporting multistep CIP transformation involving piperazine oxidation, defluorination, decarboxylation, ring cleavage, and fragmentation. In antibiotic-spiked irrigation return waters, CIP removal remained at 63–72%, while tetracycline (TC) and sulfamethoxazole (SMZ) removal reached 82.8% and 79.3%, respectively. Treatment partially attenuated residual biological effects, increasing 48 h Daphnia magna survival from 70.67% for untreated CIP to 89.33%. After membrane immobilization, approximately 80% apparent CIP removal was maintained during 20 h continuous-flow operation. These findings connect interfacial carrier regulation with antibiotic transformation and partial attenuation of residual biological effects in complex agricultural waters.

title: Viral potential to modulate antibiotic resistance gene succession through host interactions during food waste composting
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Liangmao Zhang, Dewei Luo, Jing Yang, Meng Yang, Ying Yang, Rui Yao, Min Zhan, Yuchen Zhang, Yinglong Su, Binghan Wang, Bing Xie
abstract: Composting can mitigate antibiotic resistance gene (ARG) risks, yet viral contributions to their dynamics remain unclear. Using time-series metagenomics, we investigated viral roles in ARG succession during composting of two food waste types. In both composts, ARGs followed an enrichment–decline–rebound trajectory accompanied by substrate-specific ARG-host turnover. Particularly, the maturation rebound involved the re-enrichment of high-risk ARGs, including tet(L) and lnu(G). Procrustes analysis showed significant associations of viral communities with bacterial and ARG profiles. Meanwhile, virus–host networks were organized predominantly around Firmicutes, with both temperate and lytic viral abundances correlated with ARG-host dynamics during the heating-to-thermophilic transition. Viral auxiliary metabolic genes (AMGs), annotated for central carbon metabolism, nutrient acquisition, and stress responses, may aid environmental adaptation in key ARG hosts, including Bacillus spp. Although mobile genetic elements (MGEs) provided important genetic contexts for ARG mobility, only four putative virus-mediated ARG horizontal transfer records were detected. Structural equation modelling suggested potential viral involvement through host interactions, while highlighting the importance of ARG hosts and MGEs in resistome succession. Further viral perturbation experiments are needed to clarify causal contributions in future. Overall, this study provides new insights into viral roles in resistome succession, informing resistance risk management during composting.

title: Deriving benchmark doses for nano- and microplastic-induced neurotoxicity: A systematic tiered framework for fragmented toxicological evidence
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Andrew Stiven Ortiz-Balsero, Jaber Ghorbani Kahrizsangi, Yusong Li, George M. Gray, Changmin Yan, Svetlana Romanova, Lucia Fernandez-Ballester, Mohammad Rashedul Hasan, Joseph Baumert, Bing Wang
abstract: The rapid proliferation of micro- and nanoplastics (MNPs) has intensified concerns about their potential neurotoxicity, yet heterogeneous, fragmented toxicological evidence limits quantitative human health risk assessment. Here, a structured, two-phase framework is presented that integrates systematic evidence synthesis with Bayesian benchmark dose (BMD) modeling to derive defensible toxicological benchmarks from mammalian oral exposure studies. Neurotoxicity is used as a proof-of-concept case study within a broader, scalable approach. A PRISMA-guided review across six databases (45,402 records, including an updated February 2026 search) combined large language model–assisted screening with manual evaluation, yielding 28 relevant neurotoxicity studies and 186 endpoints. After quality screening, 102 endpoints were identified with well-constrained dose–response relationships and further prioritized using a multi-criteria decision-making approach that integrated potency, uncertainty, study quality, and exposure duration. This process established a transparent, tiered evidence hierarchy (Tiers 1–3) and identified 30 high-priority (Tier 1) endpoints for hazard characterization. Across studies, MNP exposure was consistently associated with neurobehavioral, neurochemical, and neuropathological alterations, with effects varying by particle size, polymer type, and exposure duration. The framework is designed to support the synthesis of heterogeneous toxicological evidence, although its applicability to other biological systems, exposure routes, and contaminant classes remains to be demonstrated.

title: Fate and risk of natural and synthetic estrogens in a feed-manure-soil-vegetable system
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Lishan Zhang, Qingping Wang, Shiyao Chen, Bingzhu Guo, Bingqian Zhang, Yaowen Tian, Qian Zhang, Xuan Ru, Pin Gao, Zongchen Li, Shan Zhong
abstract: Steroidal estrogens and xenoestrogens from livestock production are emerging contaminants in agroecosystems, yet their transfer from feed to manure, soil, and crops remains poorly constrained. Here, six representative estrogens (estrone (E1), 17β-estradiol (E2), estriol (E3), bisphenol A (BPA), 17α-ethinylestradiol (EE2), and diethylstilbestrol (DES)) were quantified across an operational feed-manure-fertilizer-soil-vegetable system in Guangxi, China, using Liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS). Feed was an important upstream source, with substantial levels of several target compounds detected in feed, while all six compounds remained detectable in manure-derived fertilizers, with considerable variation among the investigated farms. After land application, all six compounds were detected in amended soils and edible vegetable tissues. EE2 showed the highest mean soil concentration (70.4 ± 6.5 μg·kg−1), DES accumulated most strongly in stems (58.4 ± 3.5 μg·kg−1), and EE2 was highest in leaves (40.4 ± 2.4 μg·kg−1), indicating tissue-specific partitioning. Risk assessment indicated high ecological risk in soil (the Risk Quotient, RQ ≥ 1) but low average noncarcinogenic human health risk (the combined hazard index, HI = 0.042), although hotspot scenarios under heavy manure application could yield the hazard quotient (HQ) > 1. These results identify manure recycling as a significant farm-to-food transport pathway for estrogenic contaminants and support improved manure treatment and routine residue monitoring.

title: Enhanced removal of sulfamethoxazole by tourmaline-modified iron‑carbon substrate in constructed wetlands and underlying microbial metabolic mechanisms
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Junchi Si, Yahui Li, Junyong He, Yulian Li, Peidong Hong, Chao Xie, Zijian Wu, Jiandong Lu, Dandan Yang, Lei Meng, Lingtao Kong
abstract: Tourmaline-modified iron‑carbon (Fe‑C) composite fillers were fabricated via high-temperature sintering, and their structural, electrochemical, pollutant removal and microbial response characteristics were systematically investigated. The optimal formulation was 15 wt% tourmaline with a 3:1 Fe‑C mass ratio. The optimal filler features a hierarchical porous structure, and tourmaline's spontaneous polarization mitigates iron passivation and enhances interfacial electron transfer. Static adsorption experiments demonstrated that sulfamethoxazole (SMX) adsorption onto the filler is dominated by monolayer chemisorption, with a maximum capacity of 2.91 mg/g. In a 21-day high-load static simulation system, the optimal filler achieved removal efficiencies of 84.2% for chemical oxygen demand (COD), 72.3% for total nitrogen (TN), 68.7% for total phosphorus (TP) and 84.8% for SMX, significantly outperforming pure Fe‑C, commercial Fe‑C and gravel controls. Metagenomic analysis revealed that tourmaline modification was associated with enrichment of denitrifying functional genera and key genes related to electron transport, denitrification, and SMX biodegradation. The synergistic mechanism enabled efficient pollutant removal, and continuous-flow verification over 77 days further confirmed the long-term stability of the modified filler (COD 90.8%, TN 93.3%, TP 83.3%, SMX 90.8%), demonstrating its practical potential for treating antibiotic-containing agricultural wastewater with low C/N ratios (approximately 3:1 in this study).

title: Evaluation and genomic characterization of endosulfan-degrading Streptomyces spp. isolated from a tropical environment
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Amirah Alias, Chiho Suzuki-Minakuchi, Kar Mun Mok, Nurul Syahirah Shamsol Anuar, Felipe Vejarano, Nurul Syazwani Ahmad Sabri, Nurtasbiyah Yusof, Kazunori Okada, Hirofumi Hara, Hideaki Nojiri
abstract: Endosulfan was banned worldwide under the Stockholm Convention in 2011, generating large amounts of waste to be disposed of and sporadic reports on its illegal usage. Microorganism-assisted treatment can be a cost-effective and environmentally friendly strategy to remove this chemical. Screening of bacteria from tropical agricultural sources heavily treated with endosulfan enabled us to isolate two Streptomyces spp. with ability to degrade α- and β-endosulfan isomers via hydrolytic pathway within 20 days of incubation in both sulfur-free medium (SFM) and carbon-free medium (CFM), producing endosulfan diol as metabolite. During the 20-day incubation in SFM, strain S12 degraded 99% (α) and 93% (β) of the isomers, while 68% (α) and 80% (β) were degraded in CFM. A similar tendency was observed for strain S9, with 96% (α) and 92% (β) degradation in SFM, compared to 40% (α) and 70% (β) degradation in CFM. Liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) analysis identified endosulfan diol as a single metabolite in both strains. Based on genome and RNA-Seq analyses, homologous genes of known endosulfan degradative genes, esd and ese, were found in both genomes; however, their expression levels were negligible or not induced in SFM supplemented with endosulfan, suggesting that these genes are not involved in endosulfan degradation. In contrast, other genes that were highly expressed and showed different expressions in SFM- and CFM-containing endosulfan were discovered, implying that novel genes may be involved in endosulfan metabolism. This report provides evidence of newly isolated Streptomyces species and their potential to transform endosulfan into endosulfan diol.

title: Econazole prevents the conjugative transfer of plasmid-borne last-line antibiotic resistance genes
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Hongye Hu, Ning Dong, Chunli Li, Guangfen Zhang, Yuanyuan Li, Yunbing Li, Xiaofan Li, Xiangkun Zeng, Jiayi You, Lili Huang, Ruichao Li, Mi Zhou, Sheng Chen, Shuyan Wu, Chen Xu
abstract: The global dissemination of antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs) via plasmid-mediated conjugative transfer severely compromises the efficacy of last-resort antibiotics. Inhibiting this horizontal gene transfer represents a promising strategy to treat multidrug-resistant infections. In this study, we identified the FDA-approved antifungal agent Econazole (Econ) as a potent conjugation inhibitor. Conjugation assays with clinically relevant plasmids carrying mcr, bla NDM, bla KPC-2, tet(X4), or tmexCD1-toprJ1 showed that Econ inhibited transfer at 4–128 μg/ml without affecting bacterial growth, reducing mcr-1 plasmid conjugation by approximately 33-fold at 128 μg/ml. Mechanistically, membrane potential, ATP, and qRT-PCR analyses revealed that Econ dissipates the proton motive force and depletes ATP levels, impairing the energy-dependent type IV secretion system, with virB11 downregulated by 3- to 25-fold in the donor. Concurrently, Econ interferes with plasmid processing and attenuates the accumulation of single-stranded DNA, which consequently suppresses the SOS response in the recipient strain. Collectively, these findings elucidate the molecular mechanisms underlying the broad-spectrum inhibitory effect of Econ on conjugation, highlighting its translational potential for combating the dissemination of ARGs.

title: Mechanical and thermal controls on brake-wear particle emissions and physicochemical properties in a plug-in hybrid vehicle: A comparison of two brake-pad formulations
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Jiawei Yin, Zhou Xu, Liuyang Guo, Yi Zhang, Zhenyu Jia, Xin Gong, Hao Qin, Xiao Liu, Yan Liu, Lin Wu, Lei Yang, Qijun Zhang, Lishan Zhou, Hongjun Mao
abstract: Vehicle electrification alters friction-brake use, but how mechanical engagement and thermal history shape brake-wear aerosol remains unresolved. We tested a plug-in hybrid vehicle sequentially equipped with low-metallic and non-asbestos organic pads using source-isolated wheel-end sampling during whole-vehicle testing. Event-resolved hydraulic pressure was combined with measurements of particulate matter (PM) mass, number–size distributions, 630 nm optical properties, composition, and morphology. Events with effective or high mechanical input comprised 36% of decelerations but contributed 80.3–92.7% of the PM10 mass response. Sustained heating increased ultrafine particle (<100 nm) number concentrations by 48.3–98.1-fold; emissions remained elevated during cooling while the micrometer-scale mass mode persisted, revealing number–mass decoupling and thermal-history dependence. Single-scattering albedo and mass absorption efficiency ranged from 0.606 to 0.766 and from 0.364 to 0.747 m2 g−1, respectively, and evolved differently between the two tested pad materials. High-temperature carbonaceous enrichment did not increase mass-normalized absorption. Thus, for the two tested formulations, mechanical engagement governed event-scale PM mass release, whereas thermal history and pad material shaped ultrafine-particle formation and optical and physicochemical properties. Evaluating electrified braking therefore requires resolving friction-brake engagement and thermal history and complementing PM mass with particle number, size, and physicochemical metrics.

title: Multi-scale soil heavy metal risk zoning in a typical industrial agglomeration area based on atmosphere–soil coupled risk assessment framework: Integrating pollutant discharge permit data and soil monitoring data
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Yusi Liu, Shanshan Li, Chengyi Sun, Yuhang Zhang, Yue Zhang, Qi Han, Ting Ma, Tianxiang Xia
abstract: Soil heavy metal pollution in industrial agglomeration areas exhibits characteristics of concealment, accumulation, and resistance to degradation. Traditional risk zoning methods based solely on soil monitoring data are constrained by limited spatial representativeness, high costs, and insufficient consideration of pollution source–receptor relationships. Taking a typical petrochemical industrial agglomeration zone in the Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei region as the study area, this study proposes a multi-scale atmosphere–soil coupled risk assessment framework that integrates permitted emission limit data from atmospheric emission outlets in Pollutant Discharge Permits with soil monitoring data. Through multi-scale correlation analysis, global and bivariate local spatial autocorrelation analysis, and a “source–spatial probability–receptor” three-dimensional risk identification matrix, the framework effectively achieves refined risk zoning of soil heavy metals. The results indicate that atmospheric emission intensity has significant positive correlations with As, Cd, Hg, and Sb concentrations across 50–500 m scales, with stable H-H spatial association pattern. Compared with single-medium soil risk zoning, the coupled framework substantially increases the proportion of high-risk zones from 6.98%–9.08% to 26.74%–29.16%, effectively identifying potential risks in regions with dense atmospheric emission outlets but sparse soil sampling points, and significantly improving the rationality and spatial representativeness of risk zoning. The strong consistency observed across the 50 m, 200 m, and 450 m scales demonstrates the reliability of the proposed framework. These findings indicate that incorporating data from Pollutant Discharge Permits effectively addresses the limitations of traditional soil monitoring, providing a low-cost, efficient, and scalable approach for precise soil pollution control and refined management in industrial agglomeration areas.

title: Environmental constraints reveal condition-dependent advantages of a defined benzene-degrading consortium
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Bo Zhang, Yongbin Li, Chenghang Du, Yiqun Xiong
abstract: Benzene-contaminated soils remain difficult to remediate because bioaugmentation strategies often rely on selecting individual strains with high degradation activity, while their long-term performance under environmental constraints is uncertain. Here, we show that a defined three-member consortium sustained benzene removal more effectively than the strongest degrader alone under environmental constraints. By integrating field microbiome analysis, 13C-benzene DNA stable isotope probing, genome-resolved metagenomics, cultivation, defined consortia, isotope labeling, and long-term soil incubation, we identified and reconstructed a functional benzene-degrading consortium. Field profiling identified a limited set of taxa associated with benzene contamination. DNA-SIP, genome-resolved metagenomics, and isolate assays further differentiated the roles of the focal lineages. Stutzerimonas showed the strongest benzene degradation, Rhodococcus encoded additional aromatic-catabolic potential, and Rhizobium exhibited nitrogenase activity. Although Stutzerimonas showed the highest degradation efficiency in monoculture (approximately 78%), the three-member consortium displayed a stronger advantage under environmental constraints. When the exogenous nitrogen source was omitted, corrected degradation reached approximately 73% in the three-member consortium, compared with approximately 38% in the Stutzerimonas–Rhodococcus consortium. At 700 mg L−1 benzene, the three-member consortium retained approximately 86% corrected degradation, whereas Stutzerimonas alone declined to approximately 44%. During 6 months of repeated benzene amendment in soil, the consortium maintained rapid benzene removal together with continued detection of all three focal bacterial lineages. These findings show that the benefit of the consortium depended on environmental context and provide a basis for evaluating candidate inocula for benzene remediation.

title: Characterization of physical and chemical properties controlling the transport of 129 I and 99 Tc in ultra-high-performance grout
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Ralph L. Nichols, Kenneth L. Dixon, Ronald W. Falta, David DiPrete, Peng Lin, Daniel I. Kaplan
abstract: Ultra-high-performance grout (UHPG) was evaluated as an engineered barrier for encapsulating solid waste generated during nuclear waste processing. The objective of this study was to measure geochemical, hydrological, and physical properties related to 129I and 99Tc transport through UHPG. 99Tc and 129I are key health-risk drivers associated with near-subsurface nuclear disposal facilities. To provide context, a second flowable Baseline grout currently used in nuclear waste disposal facilities was also characterized. Compressive strength and bulk density were appreciably greater in the UHPG (120.5 MPa and 2.2 g/cm3, respectively) than the Baseline grout (8.4 MPa and 1.5 g/cm3). UHPG had appreciably lower porosity (0.15 cm3/cm3) and hydraulic conductivity (K = 5.8 ×10−14 cm/sec) than the Baseline grout (porosity = 0.32 cm3/cm3; K = 9.4 ×10−7 cm/sec). Desorption partitioning experiments indicated that both grouts had similar 129I partitioning coefficients (CSolid/CLiquid; K d ), of ∼100 (moles/g)/(moles/mL) and had similar aqueous iodine speciation: I- > > IO3 - > organo-I. 99Tc aqueous concentrations appeared to be controlled by solubility (7 ×10−8 mol/L) in the UHPG, likely because slag in the UHPG formulation produced a reducing environment that converted the highly mobile aqueous TcO4 - to a much less mobile Tc(IV) solid species, TcO4·nH2O. 129I and 99Tc observed diffusivity (D obs ) were 6 and 7 orders of magnitude less, respectively, in the UHPG than in the Baseline grout. These tests provide multiple lines of evidence indicating that UHPG possesses excellent characteristics for encapsulating 99Tc and 129I waste.

title: Sixteen-year changes in hazardous metal(loid)s in urban topsoils: Land-use-specific enrichment and PM₁₀-based human health risk
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Antonio Peña-Fernández, Tomás Cámara-Pastor, M. Carmen Lobo-Bedmar
abstract: Urban topsoils are persistent reservoirs of hazardous metal(loid)s, yet reassessments rarely integrate censoring-aware statistics, geochemical enrichment and updated exposure modelling. We reassessed 137 topsoils collected in 2001 and 94 in 2017 across Urban, Industrial and Garden land uses in Alcalá de Henares, Spain. Eleven elements were compared temporally using left-censored methods with false-discovery-rate correction; Hg was retained as a 2017 descriptive endpoint because of poor historical comparability and high censoring. Urban Pb declined by 43.3%, whereas Be, Cr, Mn, Tl and V showed FDR-robust shifts towards higher 2017 acid-recoverable concentrations; because the digestion workflows differed between campaigns, the magnitude of these increases cannot be attributed exclusively to environmental accumulation. Sn showed a significant distributional shift, while the apparent 16.4% Cd decline was not robust to conservative analytical-threshold sensitivity. Industrial soils likewise showed higher 2017 acid-recoverable concentrations of As, Cr, Mn, Tl, V and Zn. Integrated enrichment was lowest in Urban soils and highest at the four sampled Garden locations; because the 2017 Garden subset comprised only n = 4, these metrics are interpreted as site-specific screening indicators rather than municipality-wide Garden estimates. Using updated U.S. EPA toxicity parameters and the historical-comparability assumption Cr(VI) = total Cr/6, 2017 hazard indices were 1.214 for Urban children, 0.156 for Urban adults, 0.0997 for Industrial workers, 2.173 for children at the sampled Garden locations and 0.278 for Garden adults. Cancer risks ranged from 4.13 × 10⁻⁵ to 2.16 × 10⁻⁴, with As dominating both non-cancer and cancer risk. From 2001–2017, Urban-child HI increased from 0.949 to 1.214, crossing the screening benchmark of 1. Excluding inferred Cr(VI) did not change this or any other qualitative receptor-level interpretation. Alcalá topsoils therefore show divergent contaminant trajectories, with declining legacy Urban Pb coexisting with higher 2017 acid-recoverable multi-element signatures and persistent child-exposure screening priorities.

title: From PN23 to PN10: Unraveling the operating-condition dependence of particle number emissions from heavy-duty diesel vehicles
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Hongfei Chen, Gang Li, Rencheng Zhu, Liqiang He, Xinping Yang, Liang Ji, Junfang Wang, Zhenhua Li, Xianglin Zhong, Tengteng Li, Zhihua Lv, Hang Yin, Yan Ding
abstract: Current particle number (PN) regulations for heavy-duty diesel vehicles (HDDVs) count particles above 23 nm, potentially missing sub-23 nm emissions. Euro VII lowers this boundary to 10 nm, and China VII development considers this transition. One China VI HDDV and three China VII prototypes were tested under start, temperature, and payload conditions. The analysis combined second-by-second high-emission episodes (HEEs), size distributions, and explainable machine learning. At 25 °C, cold-start PN10 emission factors (EFs) were 3.97 × 1010–8.79 × 1011 #/kWh, or 1.15–15.4 times hot-start values. Sub-23 nm particles represented 64%–76% of hot-start PN10 versus 16%–54% under cold starts; the 10–23 nm spectral fraction increased from 26.7% to 50.7%. Low temperature increased the relative sub-23 nm contribution, whereas full payload increased total PN, demonstrating that relative and absolute PN10–23 changes were asynchronous. HEE#3 required a sub-23 nm contribution above 50% and PN10 above the test 75th percentile. It occupied 19.1%–22.5% of cycle duration but contributed 85.9%–89.3% of PN10–23.
