RF and LightGBM achieved receiver operating characteristic area-under-the-curve values of 0.833–0.924. Fuel rate (FR), engine speed (ES), exhaust temperature (ET), and vehicle speed (VS) were principal predictors. Overall, PN10 provides condition-dependent sub-23 nm information that cannot be derived from PN23 using a fixed conversion factor.

title: Fe(III)-mediated sulfide mineralization preserves and reactivates sulfur-derived reductive capacity in autotrophic Cr(VI) bioremediation
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Yongheng Zhan, Nan Chen, Yuan Yuan, Penglu Li, Weiwu Hu, Tong Liu, Chuanping Feng
abstract: Sulfur-based autotrophic bioreduction is effective for Cr(VI)-contaminated groundwater remediation, yet the fate of sulfur-derived reducing equivalents after Cr(VI) depletion remains unclear. Continued sulfur disproportionation generates biogenic sulfide that constitutes a secondary pollutant and an irreversible loss of reductive capacity. Here we show that Fe2O3 supplementation (0.2–0.8 g/L) intercepts this loss pathway by sequestering post-reduction sulfide as reactive Fe-S minerals. After Cr(VI) exhaustion, sulfide produced from sulfur disproportionation was immobilized predominantly as FeS, with minor FeS2, as confirmed by XANES and EXAFS analyses. Electron-balance calculations showed that the otherwise mobile sulfide-derived reducing equivalents were largely retained in these reactive solids, and the resulting FeS reduced Cr(VI) more efficiently than elemental sulfur, indicating that mineral-preserved reductive capacity remains accessible for subsequent contaminant removal. Also, Fe2O3 accelerated autotrophic Cr(VI) bioreduction, with the pseudo-first-order rate constant 5.3 times that of the Fe-free control. This acceleration was driven by enhanced cell viability, electron transport activity, and cytochrome c, rather than by community restructuring or redirected electron allocation between Cr(VI) reduction and carbon metabolism. These results recast Fe(III) from a kinetic enhancer of electron transfer into a mineralogical sink that preserves reduction potential across the full cycle, coupling sulfide control with electron conservation in sulfur-driven remediation.

title: Multi-scale analysis of the selective depression mechanism of lactobionic acid on albite and its flotation separation from quartz
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Shanlong Yang, Yunfan Wang, Xingchen Leng, Bozhao Jiang, Jianing Lv, Yuqiao Feng, Shuangrong Deng, Ximei Luo
abstract: In this study, lactobionic acid (C12H22O12, LA) was employed as a depressant to investigate its performance and underlying mechanism in the flotation separation of albite from quartz using the Fe3 +/sodium oleate (NaOL) system. Flotation tests indicate that under the optimal conditions (pH=5, Fe3+/NaOL (1:10, 165 mg/L, and LA=7.5 mg/L), the recovery difference between albite and quartz reaches as high as 76.03 %age points, and a high-quality concentrate with an Al2O3 grade of 10.10% and recovery of 95.57% is obtained from a 1:1 mixed ore. A comprehensive suite of multi-dimensional characterization techniques, including surface wettability, zeta potential, Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), scanning electron microscopy–energy dispersive spectroscopy (SEM-EDS), time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectrometry (ToF-SIMS), and density functional theory (DFT) calculations, was employed to gain in-depth insights into the selective depression mechanism of LA. Mechanistic studies reveal that the polyhydroxyl structure of LA plays a pivotal role in its selectivity: the oxygen atoms of the hydroxyl groups preferentially form stable chemical bonds with the Al3+ sites on the albite surface via metal complexation, while a portion of the hydroxyl groups concurrently engage in hydrogen bonding with siloxane bonds. This dual interaction, dominated by chemical coordination and supplemented by hydrogen bonding, constructs a hydrophilic barrier on the albite surface, effectively hindering the adsorption of the collector sodium oleate.

title: Zearalenone hepatotoxicity in an agro-environmental context: Proteomics-anchored systems toxicology and hyperoside-associated stabilization
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Zuopeng Xing, Juan Xu, Jingwen Wang, Xu Shi, Shuting Cao, Guangliang Shi, Shiwen Xu
abstract: Zearalenone (ZEA), a thermally stable Fusarium mycotoxin, is frequently detected in cereals and feed-related matrices. In agricultural systems, contaminated feed exposes livestock directly, while mycotoxins or metabolites may re-enter the environment via manure handling and land application. However, how ZEA perturbs hepatic systems at the network level remains unclear. We combined network toxicology, label-free porcine liver proteomics, porcine-to-human orthology mapping, and molecular docking with molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. The analysis used a stage-oriented disease-module framework encompassing DILI-like injury, MAFLD, fibrosis, and HCC-related contexts. ADMETlab 3.0 predicted hepatotoxic liability for ZEA and its major metabolites. Across modules, enrichment implicated lipid and xenobiotic metabolism, redox regulation, inflammatory signaling, and cellular stress. Proteomics revealed broad remodeling of metabolic and antioxidant networks after ZEA exposure, while hyperoside (HYP) co-exposure shifted part of these alterations toward the control pattern. After orthology mapping, HYP-attenuated proteins converged on candidate hubs within human disease modules. Docking and 100 ns MD simulations suggested more stable HYP binding than ZEA at representative hubs, including glutathione reductase (GSR), mitogen-activated protein kinase 3 (MAPK3), and sequestosome 1 (SQSTM1). These findings provide a systems-level basis for interpreting ZEA-associated hepatotoxicity in feed-linked agricultural settings and identify candidate signatures for monitoring and mitigation.

title: Human-relevant hexafluoropropylene oxide dimer acid exposure drives neuronal senescence via KDM6A-mediated CDC42 K27 demethylation
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Qixue Zheng, Yang Yang, Ping Deng, Huihui Hong, Sicheng Liu, Jinxian Lin, Zhulin Du, Jiayi Li, Lingling Yang, Kun Luo, Haiyan Yu, Zhengwei Liang, Zhengping Yu, Wei Yuan, Huifeng Pi, Zhou Zhou
abstract: Hexafluoropropylene oxide dimer acid (HFPO-DA, also known as GenX) is an emerging per- and polyfluoroalkyl substance (PFAS) alternative increasingly detected in the environment, raising concerns about its potential long-term health effects. Neuronal senescence is a critical hallmark of brain aging and has been implicated in age-related neurodegeneration. However, whether chronic exposure to HFPO-DA promotes neuronal senescence and underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. In this study, single-cell transcriptomic analysis demonstrates that HFPO-DA exposure robustly induces neuronal senescence with subtype specificity (Camk2d⁺ and Sgcz⁺ subpopulations expansion, Dock10⁺ subpopulation depletion), convergently disrupting neuronal homeostasis and accelerating neurodegeneration. KDM6A is identified as a key protein activated by HFPO-DA exposure, whereas Kdm6a deletion (Kdm6a fl/fl , Emx1-Cre) significantly alleviates HFPO-DA-induced neuronal senescence. Mechanistically, KDM6A-mediated demethylation of CDC42 constitutes a critical event driving neuronal senescence. Kdm6a deficiency increase CDC42 K27 dimethylation, reduces CDC42 activation, and alleviates neuronal senescence. Taken together, these findings identify KDM6A-mediated CDC42 demethylation as a critical mechanism that drives neuronal senescence in response to environmental stress. Inhibition of KDM6A emerges as a potential strategy to counteract age-related neurodegeneration.

title: Unraveling the influence of Fe 2 O 3 and CaO on phase transformation of perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances during sewage sludge pyrolysis
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Thet Lei Yee, Phichanan Duchda, Jenyuk Lohwacharin
abstract: Understanding the phase transformation behavior of perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFASs) during the thermal treatment of lime-conditioned or iron-treated sludge is crucial for environmental risk evaluation. However, to date, no studies have explicitly evaluated PFAS degradation during the pyrolysis of sewage sludge. Herein, we report the investigation of the roles of CaO and Fe2O3 in promoting PFAS degradation in sewage sludge during low-temperature pyrolysis at 300°C and 500°C. Analyses via X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy and Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy indicated physical interactions between Fe-containing surface sites and perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA). Fe2O3 facilitates PFAS volatilization and/or transformation into fluorinated intermediates rather than mineralization, whereas PFAS undergo mineralization in the presence of CaO. Nontarget liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry analyses of leachates from Fe2O3-treated sludge biochar and gas-trapped samples revealed the presence of PFOA and fluorinated intermediates, such as 1-hydro-pentadecafluoroheptane, indicating partial degradation rather than mineralization. In contrast, no newly enriched intermediate compounds were observed in CaO-treated samples, probably owing to the increased stabilization of fluorinated species within the solid matrix. Leaching tests of the resulting biochar demonstrated that acidic conditions highly promote the release of PFOA and perfluorobutanesulfonic acid (PFBS) compared with neutral and alkaline conditions. PFBS leaching was strongly influenced by pH, whereas PFOA release was highly time dependent, highlighting compound-specific leaching behavior and potential environmental risks associated with post-pyrolysis biochar application. This study provides key insights for future research for optimizing pyrolysis conditions and additive selection to minimize secondary PFAS release.

title: Cross-media partitioning, sources, and health risks of phthalate esters in campus indoor air and PM 2.5
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Ran Wang, Xiaoyuan Cao, Guanwang You, Bo Yao, Shuwen Yan, Jiansheng Cui, Weihua Song
abstract: Campus environments present functionally heterogeneous indoor settings for multiphase phthalate esters (PAEs) exposure. Here, paired gas-phase and PM2.5 samples were collected from classrooms, dormitories, canteens, and courier stations at a university campus in Hebei Province, China, during spring and summer 2025. Fifteen PAEs were quantitatively analyzed to identify how microenvironmental functions and cross-medium distributions jointly regulate PAEs source characteristics, gas-particle partitioning, source contributions, and health-risk prioritization. Total PAE concentrations ranged from 1.11 × 102 to 1.53 × 103 ng m−3 in air and from 3.14 × 101 to 2.94 × 102 ng m−3 in PM2.5. Seasonal variation was characterized by a summer shift of lower-molecular-weight PAEs toward the gas phase, accompanied by compound- and microenvironment-specific changes in particle-bound PAEs. Gas-particle partitioning varied with K O A with low- K O A PAEs preferentially occurring in the gas phase and high- K O A PAEs showing greater particle association, while the dynamic partitioning framework better described the measured behavior than the instantaneous-equilibrium model. Source apportionment indicated phase- and season-dependent potential source patterns associated mainly with plasticized products, building/decorative materials, and daily-use products. The health risk assessment indicated that ingestion of PM2.5-bound PAEs was the dominant exposure pathway, and bis(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate was the main contributor to carcinogenic risk. Toxicological Priority Index ranking further identified dibutyl phthalate and diisobutyl phthalate as priority compounds for cross-media control. This study demonstrates that paired measurements of the gas phase and PM2.5 enable more precise identification of phase-specific pollution sources, exposure pathways, and priority control pollutants across distinct indoor scenarios on campus.

title: Ammonia emissions from range-extended electric vehicles under coupled temperature-HVAC conditions
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Yi Wen, Yunshan Ge, Jianwei Tan, Nan Yang, Chongyao Wang, Xin Wang
abstract: Ambient temperature and cabin heating or cooling jointly affect engine operation and ammonia (NH3) emissions from range-extended electric vehicles (EREVs). Two China 6 EREVs were tested in a climatic chamber over an RDE-derived aggressive chassis-dynamometer profile under three coupled temperature-HVAC conditions: 0 °C with heating on, 23 °C with HVAC off, and 40 °C with cooling on. Each condition was repeated three times. Reported trip-level NH3 emission factors ranged from 15.31 to 17.98 mg/km for SHEV 1 and from 2.65 to 4.69 mg/km for SHEV 2. The coupled conditions affected emission timing and phase distribution more strongly than trip-level factors. Both vehicles had higher urban NH3 factors at 0 and 40 °C than at 23 °C, coinciding with earlier or prolonged engine operation. Later engine intervention at 23 °C shifted emissions toward rural or motorway operation. SHEV 1 showed large NH3 peaks during rich motorway operation at 40 °C; SHEV 2 emitted less NH3 but exhibited isolated pollutant events and high catalyst-temperature signals. These observations support coordinated energy-management and aftertreatment control for the tested vehicles.

title: Hazard evolution in liquid dinitrogen tetroxide-isopropanol cleaning systems: thermal runaway and gas release
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Shichun Weng, Jing ye Li, Jinyao Hu, Yuqi Zhou, Zichao Guo, Guoning Rao, Liping Chen, Wanghua Chen
abstract: Liquid dinitrogen tetroxide (N₂O₄, NTO) can pose severe hazards when contacting incompatible cleaning agents. A vessel rupture accident involving NTO and an isopropanol-containing cleaning agent was investigated using accident reconstruction, chemical analysis, online Raman monitoring, calorimetry and field validation. Temperature-pressure records supported chemically driven thermal runaway. Blank tests showed vigorous gas evolution but limited heat accumulation during NTO hydrolysis and neutralization. HPLC/HPLC-MS supported acetone formation and tentative assignments to isonitrosoacetone, nitrolic-acid- and isoxazoline-type products. Raman monitoring revealed attenuation of NTO-related bands and transient spectral features tentatively associated with oxime/N-OH and cyano-containing species, while quantum-chemical calculations assessed the proposed nitrile-oxide-mediated pathway. Gas analysis tentatively indicated N₂O and carbon oxides without establishing their formation pathways. DSC revealed exothermic decomposition at approximately 60–90°C under the tested conditions, while ARC demonstrated rapid self-heating and pressure rise. Comparative experiments showed greater runaway severity at lower initial temperatures, consistent with liquid NTO retention and enhanced liquid–liquid contact. Higher temperatures reduced heat accumulation under the tested conditions but promoted volatilization, while toxic-gas release remained a concern. These findings highlight thermal runaway and gas-release hazards, with secondary decomposition of unstable intermediates as a possible contributor, and inform safer residual oxidizer cleaning and off-gas management.

title: Microplastics amplify Cr(VI)-mediated RP4 plasmid conjugative transfer through coupled interfacial, oxidative, and metabolic regulation
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Lijuan Zhang, Jiajia Zhang, Haizhu Pan, Hu Li, He Guo, Tiecheng Wang
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) can accumulate heavy metals and influence plasmid-mediated antibiotic resistance gene (ARGs) transfer, yet the regulatory mechanisms under metal-associated MP exposure remain poorly understood. Here, a polystyrene microplastic–Cr(VI) composite (PSMPs@Cr) was established to investigate RP4 plasmid conjugative transfer by integrating physicochemical characterization, physiological measurements, transcriptomic analysis, and multivariable modeling. PSMPs@Cr exhibited a non-monotonic effect on conjugative transfer, with the highest conjugative transfer frequency (9.4 × 10−2) observed at 20 ppm Cr loading, representing a 4.75-fold increase compared with the control. Cr adsorption reconstructed the MP interface by modifying surface charge, wettability, morphology, and colloidal stability, which was accompanied by altered bacterial adhesion behavior. Meanwhile, PSMPs@Cr exposure induced coordinated changes in ROS accumulation, antioxidant responses, ATP production, membrane-associated functions, and energy metabolism. Transcriptomic analysis further revealed treatment-dependent regulation of oxidative stress, membrane transport, cellular communication, and metabolic pathways. Random forest–SHAP analysis identified zeta potential, CAT activity, ATP, and ROS as relatively important variables associated with CTF variation. Overall, PSMPs@Cr-associated ARGs transfer was linked to coupled interfacial, redox, and energetic processes rather than a single regulatory pathway, providing new insights into how microplastic–metal interactions influence plasmid-mediated horizontal gene transfer under complex contaminant exposure scenarios.

title: Humic acid and related natural-organic-matter interfaces as sinks, carriers and mediators for persistent and recalcitrant organic contaminants: Mechanisms and endpoint-specific evidence
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Jinhang Song, Panting Zhang, Jianguo Zheng, Kunlong Hui
abstract: Humic acid (HA) is commonly viewed as an immobilizing sorbent, yet HA-associated organic matter can also mobilize contaminants or alter their transformation. This critical review evaluates when HA functions as a sink, carrier, or mediator for PAHs, pesticides and phenols, PFAS, and halogenated persistent organic pollutants. Evidence is distinguished among isolated HA/FA, operational natural humic fractions, bulk dissolved organic matter, native or mineral-associated organic matter, and model/comparator systems. We link hydrophobic partitioning, π–π interactions, hydrogen bonding, electrostatic forces, cation bridging, and quinone-mediated electron transfer to measurable fate endpoints. pH, ions, hydrodynamics, redox conditions, light, and biological activity can shift HA conformation, aggregation, mineral association, transport, and reactivity. Consequently, lower freely dissolved concentrations may coexist with greater colloid-associated flux, while parent loss may occur without mineralization or lower toxicity. We define sink, carrier, and mediator behavior from retention, transport, and product-resolved transformation, respectively, with exposure evaluated downstream. Event-scale evidence indicates contaminant redistribution during rainfall, freeze–thaw, and resuspension, although direct HA-specific data remain limited. An endpoint-specific assessment should integrate freely dissolved concentration, phase-resolved mass flux, products, mineralization, NER stability, and biological exposure within defined materials, media, comparators, and timescales, rather than a single removal metric.

title: Alteration of simulant UK nuclear waste glass in a low temperature natural environment: the Ballidon glass burial field experiment
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): G. Manifold, R.J. Hand, C. Littler, L.T. Haigh, E.A. Rencz, M.C. Stennett, A.H. Mir, S. Creasey-Gray, S. Nehzati, J. Qi, S.E. Pepper, O. Stagg, M.T. Harrison, C.L. Thorpe
abstract: Non-active UK nuclear waste glass surrogates, representative of vitrified highly active liquor (HAL) from Magnox and oxide fuel reprocessing, were buried in a mildly alkaline, undersaturated, near-surface environment at Ballidon, UK. Following 16–18 years, alteration layers were large (40–55 µm) on simulant ‘Blend’ glasses, made from a mixture of Magnox and oxide HAL, but smaller (10 µm) on glasses made from simulated Magnox HAL. Short term laboratory experiments showed that Magnox glass had a lower initial dissolution rate in deionised water when compared to Blend glasses. Analysis of alteration layers revealed distinct zones of varying composition and morphology; silicon rich nearest the glass, layered Fe, Al, Si and Zr in the centre, and a Ca/P/lanthanide rich layer nearest the surface. Outer layers were mostly amorphous and comprised glass-derived lanthanides, environment-derived calcium, and phosphate derived from both the glass and environment. Availability of P may have been enhanced through exchange of sorbed phosphate with dissolved silicic acid from the glass. Nanocrystals, tentatively identified as the hydrated lanthanide phosphate phase churchite, were detected at the silica-phosphate interface. Results provide insight into alteration layer evolution in a natural open system and how radioactive fission products and actinides may be retained within alteration layers.

title: Influence of material properties and environmental factors on VOC emission characteristics from automotive paint sludge
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Zewei Liu, Fuhang Huo, Ruihao Yang, Hongbo Liu
abstract: Automotive paint sludge is a hazardous waste with significant volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions. Effective source control requires understanding how material properties and environmental factors govern key mass-transfer parameters: initial emittable concentration (C m,0), diffusion coefficient (D m), and partition coefficient (K m). This study couples a finite diffusion model and nonlinear optimization with chamber experiments on oil-based paint sludge to evaluate effects of temperature, humidity, air exchange rate, VOC type, porosity, moisture, and solid matrix. Temperature dominates: increasing temperature raises C m,0 and D m but lowers K m, and correlating K m with temperature yields apparent desorption activation energies (E d). Although relative humidity induces minor non-monotonic fluctuations via competitive water adsorption and air exchange rate slightly alters surface convection, their standardized sensitivities are two orders of magnitude below temperature's, rendering their net impacts engineering-wise negligible. Low-molecular-weight, nonpolar VOCs have low E d and desorb rapidly, whereas hydrogen bonding hinders polar alcohols. D m increases with porosity via a power law, suggesting compaction for mitigation. Moisture forms water films that reduce C m,0 and D m but increase K m, and inorganic scaffolds exhibit higher adsorption potentials than organic matrices. These findings provide strategies for predicting and mitigating VOC emissions from hazardous wastes.

title: National-scale evaluation of groundwater fluoride in Ethiopia using spatially buffered machine learning
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Usman Sunusi Usman, Jianmei Cheng, Bing Yan, Kuiyuan Ding, Qiang Lv, Wen Zhao
abstract: Excess groundwater fluoride (F⁻) is a public health concern in the East African Rift, yet sparse, clustered observations limit reliable national inference. This study developed a leakage-controlled framework to classify groundwater fluoride exceedance above the WHO guideline of 1.5 mg/L, separating well-level prediction from national spatial transferability. A dataset of 1567 observations, including 567 exceedances, was evaluated using five-fold buffered spatial cross-validation with a 75-km train–test exclusion radius. The hydrochemical Extra Trees model (HYD_ET) achieved the strongest well-level performance, with Macro-F1 = 0.830, balanced accuracy = 0.817, MCC = 0.671, ROC-AUC = 0.910, PR-AUC = 0.859, and Brier score = 0.116. In contrast, the environmental-only Random Forest showed negligible geographic transferability (Macro-F1 = 0.495; balanced accuracy = 0.501), while Gaussian indicator kriging achieved Macro-F1 = 0.594. Applicability-domain analysis identified 8.23% of observations outside the model domain. Because no continuous model demonstrated adequate transferability, no wall-to-wall national F⁻-risk surface was retained. Instead, 48.43%, 18.84%, and 32.73% of 10-km grid cells had stronger, moderate, and weaker monitoring support, respectively. This evaluation spans heterogeneous hydrogeological and environmental settings under uneven monitoring across Ethiopia. The results show that strong well-level prediction does not imply reliable national extrapolation and supports groundwater monitoring and data collection.

title: The C-terminal fragment of COL1A1 protects mammalian testicular BTB integrity by competitively inhibiting Cd-induced activation of the TGFβ-SMAD2/3-MMP9 pathway
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Hao Xiong, Jialian Li, Anna Wu, Xinpeng Yang, Wenning Xu, Shang Wu, Shiqin Zhou, Gaogui Chen, Dake Chen, Jinhua Tang, Fenge Li
abstract: Cadmium (Cd), a heavy metal pollutant, impairs male reproductive health by disrupting the blood-testis barrier (BTB) and inducing testicular injury in mammals. Collagen type I alpha 1 chain (COL1A1) and its bioactive fragments are essential for maintaining BTB integrity and seminiferous tubule structure. However, whether COL1A1 and its bioactive fragments can modulate Cd-induced BTB injury remains largely unknown. In this study, proteomic analysis showed that downregulated proteins including COL1A1 were mainly enriched in collagen-containing extracellular matrix pathway in boars with low quality semen. COL1A1 generates an approximately 25 kDa bioactive fragment termed C1158/59. Overexpression of C1158/59 in primary mouse Sertoli cells and testes mitigated Cd-induced BTB damage by restoring the expression and localization of BTB-associated proteins, as well as the organization of F-actin and α-tubulin cytoskeletons in Sertoli cells. Mechanistically, C1158/59 competitively inhibited the binding of latent TGFβ to ITGB1, suppressing Cd-induced activation of the TGFβ-SMAD2/3 signaling pathway and subsequent MMP9 upregulation, ultimately preventing BTB structural degradation. Collectively, these findings demonstrate a critical protective role of the COL1A1-derived fragment C1158/59 against Cd-induced structural and functional impairment of the testicular BTB, providing new insights into the regulatory functions of bioactive fragments in preserving BTB structural integrity against environmental toxicant-induced testicular injury.

title: Combined salicylic and jasmonic acids enhance cd tolerance and accumulation in Sedum alfredii
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): An Shi, Wenhao Yang, Dongming Zhang, Zhijun Zhang, Xuehao Zhu, Wen Zhang, Beibei Wang
abstract: Salicylic acid (SA) and jasmonic acid (JA) individually improve Cd responses in the hyperaccumulator Sedum alfredii, but whether their combined application provides additional benefits and how these relate to Cd accumulation remain unclear. We compared SA, JA and their combination in an independent hydroponic experiment integrating physiological, hormonal, transcriptomic, metabolomic, thiol and subcellular Cd analyses. Compared with Cd alone, co-treatment increased fresh biomass by 62.9%, total chlorophyll by 99.3%, net photosynthetic rate by 75.0% and shoot Cd concentration by 80.0%, while reducing malondialdehyde by 27.5%. Among Cd-containing treatments, SA × JA interactions were significant for photosynthetic parameters and selected antioxidant and hormone indicators. Although net photosynthetic rate exceeded that under either hormone alone, its increase was smaller than the sum of the single-hormone increases. Glutathione and phytochelatins increased without a detectable interaction. Co-treatment increased Cd concentrations in cell-wall and soluble fractions, alongside changes in signaling, redox metabolism, lipid-related metabolites and metal transport-related gene expression. At the tested concentrations, combined SA and JA improved growth and photosynthesis despite higher shoot Cd concentration, without uniformly greater-than-additive responses. Increased thiols and Cd recovery in cell-wall and soluble fractions suggest that Cd binding and partitioning may contribute to reduced injury.

title: Stepwise sulfation roasting for co-recovery of Li and F/Al as AlF 3 from spent aluminum electrolyte: in-situ phase evolution and atomic-scale migration
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Zexun Han, Xuan Tan, Xingtong Sun, Xiaojun Lv, Yanqing Lai
abstract: Spent aluminum electrolyte (SAE) from aluminum smelting is both a hazardous fluoride waste and a valuable Li/F resource. The current Al2(SO4)3 roasting process of recycling SAE focuses solely on either AlF3 recovery or Li extraction, leading to incomplete F/Li/Al resource utilization. Mechanistic understandings of roasting reaction remain at the static thermodynamics and macroscopic level. Herein, we propose a stepwise roasting-leaching closed-loop recovery process. Primary sulfation roasting-water leaching converts SAE into AlF3 with 98.5% Li leached, and the crude AlF3 is purified to 95.20% purity via Na2CO3 conversion. The F and Al in the leachate were recovered as aluminum hydroxyfluoride, followed by NH4HF2 roasting to recycle AlF3 and entrained Li, boosting the overall Li and F recovery to 97.09% and 98.23% respectively. In-situ thermal behavior indicated that the melting point of the system decreased initially and then increased during roasting due to stepwise phase-evolution, and local melting occurred at 477 ℃, rather than the reported pure solid-solid reaction. First-principles calculation further revealed the atomic migration priority of the roasting reaction (F > Na > O > Al > S). Techno-economic and environmental analysis shows a profit of CNY 8382.1 /t-SAE and a net abatement of 0.92 t CO2 eq/t-SAE.

title: Removal and stabilization of PFAS and As(V) co-contamination in soils by fluorine-functionalized biochar
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Wei Zhang, Xueqi Zhang, Yajing Wang, Bingyue Guo, Xayida Subi, Yuting Wang, Dongmei Zhou, Qiming Xian
abstract: The prevalent PFAS and heavy metals (such as arsenic) co-contaminated soils, resulting from industrial activities, present a considerable remediation challenge as conventional single-function materials are often ineffective. In this study, a fluorine-iron dual-functionalized biochar (FMBC) was prepared via a magnetite impregnation-fluorosilane grafting strategy, which integrates multiple binding modes: grafted perfluoroalkyl chains provide hydrophobic and F-F interaction zones for capturing PFAS tails; loaded Fe oxides offer positively charged electrostatic and coordinative sites to attract the anionic headgroups of PFAS, while simultaneously capturing As(V) through electrostatic attraction, coprecipitation, and complexation. 1:10FMBC exhibited a higher PFOS sorption (75.91 mg/g) compared to raw biochar (0.63 mg/g), achieving 99.9%, 95.3%, and 65.7% removal for PFOS, PFOA, and PFHxS, showing notable chemical stability, and maintaining efficient PFAS-As(V) removal across various water matrices. DFT calculations reveal that synergy of F-F interactions and electrostatic attraction governs the chain-length-dependent sorption of PFAS. In column tests with co-contaminated soils, 1.0 wt% 1:10FMBC was estimated to reduce the cumulative release of PFAS and As(V) over 20 years by 75.8–99.4% and 31.8–82.9%, suggesting competitive performance among reported amendments. This work validates that the design of multifunctional biochar is an effective pathway for stabilizing PFAS-As(V) co-contaminated soils, offering a technological option for field-scale remediation.

title: Arsenite-associated attenuation of daptomycin-induced inhibition in Clostridium butyricum under co-exposure conditions
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Xiangfeng Zeng, Renzong Liu, Wenyue Chen, Xuejie Li, Yaqi Li, Can Jin, Shaofeng Wang, Weiming Li, Yongfeng Jia
abstract: The metalloid arsenic may co-occur with antibiotics in anaerobic environments, yet microbial responses to their combined stress remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated how arsenite (As(III)) alters the response of Clostridium butyricum CXL-1 using phenotypic, physiological, and transcriptomic analyses. Individually, As(III) and daptomycin inhibited bacterial growth and fermentative metabolism in a dose-dependent manner, with an As(III) IC50 of 120 mg/L and complete growth inhibition at 5 mg/L daptomycin. Under co-exposure, increasing daptomycin concentrations at fixed As(III) progressively inhibited fermentative metabolism, whereas increasing As(III) concentrations at fixed daptomycin increased final biomass despite slower substrate utilization. Relative to daptomycin alone, As(III) co-exposure produced a higher ATP index, lowered reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation and the NADH/NAD+ ratio, and reduced lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) leakage. Transcriptomic analysis under co-exposure revealed upregulation of the arsenic resistance operon (ars), mepA_6, and genes for thiamine biosynthesis, sulfur transport, and glutathione biosynthesis, and downregulation of phosphotransferase system and pentose phosphate pathway genes. At the relatively high laboratory As(III) concentrations tested, co-exposure was associated with attenuated daptomycin-induced inhibition, slower carbon utilization, a higher ATP index, improved redox balance, and membrane integrity. This study reveals a previously underexplored influence of arsenic exposure on bacterial responses to antibiotics under anaerobic conditions.

title: Pyrite-promoted hydrothermal upcycling of polyvinyl chloride waste: Deep dechlorination, enhanced graphitization, and heterogeneous Fenton catalysis
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Ziyi Ding, Shoushu Wei, Qingze Chen, Fangxin Deng, Ruixi Wang, Yunfei Xi, Runliang Zhu
abstract: Green dechlorination and high-value conversion of polyvinyl chloride (PVC) waste are critical challenges in plastic pollution control and resource recycling. This work presents a pyrite (Py)-enhanced one-step hydrothermal strategy that utilizes the reducing ability and Lewis acidity of Py to synergistically promote deep dechlorination and catalytic carbonization of PVC, thereby preparing an efficient heterogeneous Fenton catalyst. The Py-PVC system achieved a dechlorination efficiency of 99.90% at 240°C for 6 h, 15.72% higher than that of the control system without Py. Fe2+ donated electrons to facilitate C-Cl bond cleavage, thereby forming the C=C bond; while lattice sulfur contributed to Fe2+ regeneration. Subsequently, driven by Fe2+ / 3+ catalysis, the dechlorinated polyene intermediates formed highly graphitized hydrochar. The resulting composite showed excellent heterogeneous Fenton activity, removing 99.2% of bisphenol A within 10 min and facilitating the activation leaching of 84.75% of uranium within 180 min. As an electron shuttle, the graphite-carbon structure not only facilitated the transfer of electrons from Py to recalcitrant organochlorines during the hydrothermal process but also promoted the Fe(III)/Fe(II) cycle during the advanced oxidation process. This work elucidates the synergistic mechanism of Py-assisted PVC hydrothermal dechlorination and catalytic carbonization, offering perspectives on the green upgrading of chlorinated plastics.

title: Spatial distribution and microbial degradation potential of microplastics and nanoplastics along a 134-year proglacial chronosequence
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Qingyan Liu, Ruxin Yang, Cheng Yang, Yu Xiang, Ziwei Chen, Jingfang Cui, Yuanxiang Mao, Han Zhang, Mengli Chen
abstract: Glacier retreat increasingly exposes proglacial soils to micro- and nanoplastic (MNP) pollution, yet long-term MNP dynamics and associated microbial plastic-degradation potential remain unclear. Along a 134-year chronosequence at Hailuogou Glacier, we combined µ-FTIR, Py-GC/MS, and metagenomics to characterize MNP pollution, ecological risk, and microbial degradation potential. MP abundance followed a non-linear trajectory, peaking at 270 items kg⁻¹ at 66 yr, whereas NP abundance increased from 1.54 to 4.17 mg kg⁻¹ . MPs were dominated by PA, PE, PET, and Rayon, while NPs shifted from PMMA to PE dominance (>78%) in mature soils. Ecological risk was non-monotonic and polymer-dependent: MP-associated PERI reached Level IV at 66 yr, whereas NP-associated PERI peaked at 94 yr despite increasing NP mass. This decoupling suggested that risk was strongly influenced by polymer-composition turnover rather than abundance or mass alone. Gene-based microbial plastic-degradation potential increased during succession through enrichment of plastic-degradation-related genes. PLS-PM identified a sequence of positive associations linking glacier retreat age, soil development, MNP pollution, and microbial plastic-degradation potential. Random Forest analysis further highlighted retreat age and Ca among the leading predictors of degradation-gene abundance. These findings provide insights into MNP risk and gene-based microbial plastic-degradation potential in rapidly deglaciating high-altitude ecosystems.

title: From dense packing to porous layered POMOFs for ultra-efficient seawater uranium extraction
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Yanjie Lv, Xinyu Zhao, Jing Sun, Huiying Sun, Wenxi Zhang, Xiao Li, Xinlong Wang, Zhongran Dai, Zhongmin Su
abstract: Efficient and selective uranium extraction from seawater (UES) is crucial for nuclear fuel sustainability but is challenged by low concentration, complex matrix, and biofouling. Here, we construct two POMOFs with distinct architectures: a dense D-W10-MOF and a porous layered P-W10-MOF. Taking advantage of the precise O···O distance (4.17 Å) matching uranyl bidentate coordination, open porous framework, and enhanced mass transfer, P-W10-MOF achieves a record-breaking Langmuir-fitted theoretical maximum uranium adsorption capacity (qmax) of 3197.5 mg·g⁻¹ in simulated seawater adsorption tests, along with outstanding selectivity (U/V ≈ 103) and cycling stability. By contrast, D-W10-MOF delivers a substantially lower qmax of 961.5 mg·g⁻¹ due to hindered access to coordination sites. XAFS, XPS and DFT results confirm an equatorial U-O coordination number of 5.0 ± 0.4, consisting of three O donors from the W10 cluster and two bidentate carbonate O donors. P-W10-MOF also exhibits strong antibacterial activity, and a preliminary life cycle assessment guides green synthesis. This work provides a paradigm for designing high-performance uranium adsorbents by clarifying the geometric structure and framework structure of the components.

title: Dynamic changes of chicken gut microbiota and resistome during enrofloxacin treatment against multidrug-resistant Salmonella based on metagenomics
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Yang Chen, Jinhua Chu, Yali Guo, Muhammad Haris Raza Farhan, Xinru Lu, Hanqi Wei, Changqing Xie, Xu Wang, Lingli Huang, Guyue Cheng
abstract: Antibiotics are widely used to treat and prevent bacterial infections in human and animals. However, the impact of antibiotic dose on bacterial burden and diachronic changes and transfer of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in gut bacterial infections remains unclear. Here, we used enrofloxacin (ENR) at sub-inhibitory (1 mg/kg b.w.), prophylactic (3.03 mg/kg b.w.), and therapeutic (10 mg/kg b.w.) doses to treat infections with Salmonella harboring plasmid pJX-4, with infected but untreated groups as controls. We found that subtherapeutic ENR may pose potential risks to the gut ecosystem. Specifically, sub-inhibitory ENR led to persistently high Salmonella and its carried resistance gene qnrS1 levels; under this dose condition, preliminary evidence suggested that intestinal Escherichia coli was a potential host for in vivo transfer of plasmid pJX-4. The prophylactic dose group showed significantly higher relative abundances of human bacterial pathogens and ARGs, especially during treatment. Furthermore, this group was enriched in genes related to oxidative stress, cellular signaling, and secretion systems, and these functional genes were primarily associated with ARGs. Overall, different ENR doses shaped distinct evolutionary trajectories of the gut microbiome and resistome. This study provides a theoretical basis for the rational use of antibiotics in treating bacterial infections.

title: Co-inoculation of indigenous cyanobacteria and fungi effectively immobilizes heavy metals in molybdenum tailings by forming biocrusts: Exploration of potential immobilization mechanisms
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Chao Zhang, Yingzhi Liu, Min Wang, Feng He, Yin Li, Yanbo Wang, Yan Li, Yinping Bai, Junkang Guo
abstract: Nutrient deficiency and heavy metal (HM) toxicity represent major obstacles to the ecological restoration of tailings ponds. However, as “ecological engineers” in extreme environments, biological crusts (BCs) play a significant role in the restoration of degraded habitats. In this study, the molybdenum tailings were inoculated with the indigenous cyanobacteria and fungi isolated from a tailings pond to construct BCs in a pot experiment. Both single cyanobacteria inoculation and co-inoculation of cyanobacteria and fungi formed moss BCs after an 80-day cultivation. Compared with single inoculation, co-inoculation significantly increased the BCs thickness and chlorophyll a content by 16.16∼17.47% and 10.17∼26.29%, respectively. BCs effectively reduced the bioavailability of Cd, Cu, Mo, and Zn in tailings, while substantially enriching these HMs. EPS chelation, biosorption by moss and microorganisms, and clay mineral adsorption in BCs were synergistically involved in HM immobilization. Additionally, BCs significantly improved tailings properties, and BCs growth, organic carbon, exopolysaccharide, microbial biomass carbon, and available potassium were key influencing factors in reducing HM bioavailability. These results demonstrated the feasibility of rapidly constructing BCs via co-inoculation of functional microorganisms onto tailings and provided a low-cost, eco-friendly, and sustainable new strategy for ecological restoration and HM pollution mitigation of tailings ponds.

title: Synthesis, characterisation, and chemical durability of UK uranium Butex high-level waste glasses
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Adam J. Fisher, Hao Ding, Lewis R. Blackburn, Daniel J. Bailey, Martin C. Stennett, Mike T. Harrison, Claire L. Corkhill
abstract: Two inactive simulant glass wasteforms were developed to incorporate a unique blend of high-level waste calcine from Butex, Magnox, and ThORP fuel reprocessing at a ratio of 50: 37.5: 12.5, with a total waste loading of 32 wt%. The glasses differed compositionally: one used the traditional Mixed Windscale (MW) borosilicate base glass (Butex MW), the other a CaZn-modified borosilicate base glass (Butex CaZn). Glasses were characterised by Energy Dispersive Spectroscopy, X-ray Diffraction, and X-ray Absorption Near Edge Spectroscopy, the latter confirming that U is incorporated as the uranyl (U⁶⁺) moiety in both glasses. Dissolution kinetics were evaluated using the Product Consistency Test-B (PCT-B) in UHQ water at 40 °C for 110 d, under both oxic and anoxic conditions. No significant differences were observed in the dissolution behaviour of the main glass elements (B, Si, Na, Li) between either glass composition or atmosphere. Both glasses followed typical borosilicate dissolution behaviour: a rapid initial rate (∼10⁻³ g m⁻² d⁻¹, 1–35 d), transitioning to a slower residual rate (∼10⁻⁵ g m⁻² d⁻¹, 35–110 d) – up to 16 times lower than Magnox/ThORP-only blends, attributed to reduced Mg content from the Butex component. Uranium release rates were similarly low (∼10⁻⁵ g m⁻² d⁻¹), indicating that Butex calcine addition improves durability in short-term accelerated testing. Minor differences between oxic and anoxic experiments were attributed to CO₂-driven pH changes, which affected Al solubility. Enhanced U release under oxic conditions was linked to U⁶⁺ complexation with bicarbonate ions, offering novel preliminary insight into Butex glass behaviour in (bi)carbonate-rich groundwater.

title: Tracing sediment organic matter sources in a tributary of the Three Gorges Reservoir via stable isotopes (δ¹³C and δ¹⁵N) under anthropogenic influences
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Xiaoxia Bai, Cheng Cheng, Chenhui Yu, Jin Zhang, Jujiao Zhao
abstract: As major reservoirs of organic matter (OM), sediments are substantially influenced by anthropogenic activities, yet their effects on OM sources remain unclear. Surface sediments from the Yulin River, a tributary of the Three Gorges Reservoir (TGR), were analyzed for δ13C, δ15N, TOC, TN and C/N in 2019 and 2023 during stable impounding (SIP) and discharge (SDP) periods of TGR. Across the sampled sites, TOC and TN tended to be higher at the upstream sites than at the downstream site, indicating dam-induced sediment trapping and enhanced autochthonous production. From 2019–2023, δ13C shifted from −26.54‰ to −21.41‰, and δ15N increased from 2.51‰ to 6.15‰, reflecting a transition from soil dominance toward increased sewage and C4 plant contributions. MixSIAR showed soil contribution decreased (66.11%→58.70%), while sewage (2.83%→5.51%), phytoplankton (5.21%→6.65%), and C4 plants (18.93%→24.51%) increased over the four-year. Hydrological regulation further modulated source dynamics: SIP favored ¹ ³C-depleted algal OM, whereas SDP enhanced terrestrial and 15N-enriched sewage inputs. These findings indicate that dam operation, urbanization and sewage discharge substantially altered sedimentary OM composition, with stable isotope signatures proving effective in tracing anthropogenic impacts on riverine carbon and nitrogen dynamics.

title: The tolerance differences and response mechanisms of the main submerged plants in Erhai Lake to the environmental concentration of atrazine stress
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Yinuo Liu, Jian Shen, Jimeng Feng, Xinze Wang
abstract: To investigate whether pesticide residues in the area near farmlands of Erhai Lake affect the growth of submerged plants in Erhai Lake, this study combined field investigations with 56-day outdoor simulation experiments to assess the differences in the effects and tolerance mechanisms of atrazine at environmental concentrations in Erhai Lake on four submerged plants: Ottelia acuminata, Potamogeton wrightii, Hydrilla verticillata, and Ceratophyllum demersum. The results showed that: ①Exposuring to atrazine at level of ≤ 35 ng/L caused no visible injury under the tested conditions. Under the stress of 75 and 125 ng/L atrazine, the plants Ottelia acuminata and Hydrilla verticillata showed observable growth differences. The metabolic level of Potamogeton wrightii had shown latent damage. The Ceratophyllum demersum had the best growth. ②The Fv/Fm values of the four plants were all inhibited, which are the most sensitive physiological indicators. ③Combining the weighting of photosynthetic factors with the metabolic results, the comprehensive tolerance of the four plants to atrazine was ranked as follows: Ceratophyllum demersum > Potamogeton wrightii > Hydrilla verticillata > Ottelia acuminata. Long-term exposure to high concentrations of atrazine may selectively inhibits the growth of submerged plants of sensitive species, thereby affecting the community structure of submerged plants in the lake.

title: Glyphosate exposure alters the faecal corticosterone metabolite profile in a lizard: Validation and application of an enzyme immunoassay in Podarcis bocagei
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Anastasios Limnios, Rupert Palme, Sabine Macho-Maschler, Sarah A. Heleno, Effimia Tzaneti, Miguel A. Carretero
abstract: Glyphosate, the active ingredient of world’s most widely used herbicide Roundup™, has attracted attention due to its impact on non-target organisms. Studies highlight the effects of glyphosate and glyphosate-based herbicides on the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis of vertebrates. Nevertheless, they utilised dosages higher than toxicological reference values (TRVs) suggested by the European Food Safety Authority (EFSA), formulations of glyphosate, not allowing for clear distinctions of glyphosate’s effect itself, and blood samples, a technique inappropriate for small animals and for assessing long-term chronic effects. Here we tackled those caveats by analyzing faecal corticosterone metabolites (FCMs) of the wall lizard Podarcis bocagei to detect glyphosate-induced effects on the HPA axis. This species provides a promising animal model as reptiles are prevalent in agricultural fields treated with herbicides, reptile-specific TRVs are lacking, and only five studies have validated immunoassays for measuring FCMs in reptiles. We validated the 5α-pregnane-3ß,11ß,21-triol-20-one enzyme immunoassay. We detected a moderate increase in FCM levels during the exposure phase, while exposed animals of both sexes displayed an altered mass-depended FCM profile. Our results indicate that glyphosate likely impacts the energy mobilization and management of lizards and support the need for reptile-specific TRVs and the consideration of reptiles in EFSA's risk assessment.

title: Layer cellulose-based sandwich sponge with directionally aligned channels for rapid removal of polystyrene nanoplastics and TBBPA
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Mengyi Guo, Ruijing Liu, Yuqi Zhang, Yulin Shen, Ziyang Zhang, Zhe Li, Xiaoxin Wang, Zishuai Jiang, Lihong Yao
abstract: Nanoplastics can adsorb organic pollutants and facilitate their transport in water environments, thereby increasing potential risks to ecosystems and human health. However, most porous adsorbents have an even structure, making it difficult to combine rapid pollutant capture with stable retention. Herein, a layer cellulose-based sandwich (PCP) sponge with directionally aligned channels was fabricated through directional freezing and chemical cross-linking of cellulose fibers with chitosan and polyvinyl alcohol. The aligned porous channels promote solution transport, while chitosan provides positively charged sites favorable for capturing polystyrene (PS) nanoplastics. The layered architecture integrates macropore-mediated transport, interfacial adsorption, and physical interception within a single material. PCP sponge removed up to 99.88% of 100 nm PS nanoplastics within 10 min at room temperature. In coexistence experiments, an apparent tetrabromobisphenol A (TBBPA) removal efficiency of more than 80% was also observed. After 10 adsorption–desorption cycles, the removal efficiency of PS still remains above 94.85%, and the pore structure remains intact under acidic, saline, and repeated cycling conditions. This study proposes a sustainable strategy for raw materials, which convert biomass resources into high-performance multifunctional adsorbents, providing a promising solution for the simultaneous removal of nanoplastics and coexisting organic pollutants from complex water environments.

title: Biodegradable polylactic acid microplastics pose greater field nitrous oxide emission risks than conventional polyethylene by reshaping microbial production-reduction pathways in a wheat-maize rotation system
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Chuan Wang, Rui He, Lisha Wang, Yuan Li, Rui Li, Yiting Dai, Xiaoli He, Binghan Wang, Meng Yang, Xubo Wang
abstract: Microplastic contamination in agroecosystems is increasing, yet the field-scale effects of biodegradable microplastics on soil nitrous oxide (N2O) emissions remain unclear. We conducted a wheat–maize rotation field experiment to compare conventional polyethylene microplastics (PE-MPs) and biodegradable polylactic acid microplastics (PLA-MPs) at three application levels. Measurements included N2O fluxes, soil physicochemical properties, N-transformation enzyme activities, potential nitrification and denitrification rates, functional gene abundances, N2O/(N2O+N2) product ratios, 15N-18O-based N2O production pathways. Two-way ANOVA showed that microplastic type was the most consistent determinant of key responses, whereas concentration and interaction effects varied among indicators and seasons. PE-MPs caused weak and variable changes in soil N cycling and cumulative N2O emissions. In contrast, PLA-MPs increased cumulative N2O emissions by 38.9–61.1%, increased dissolved organic carbon, lowered pH, suppressed ammonia monooxygenase activity and nitrification, and stimulated nitrite reductase activity, potential denitrification, and nirK/nirS abundances. Increased N2O/(N2O+N2) and (nirK+nirS)/nosZ ratios indicated a stronger imbalance between N2O production and nosZ-mediated reduction. Dual-isotope tracing further showed that microplastics reduced nitrifier nitrification and shifted N2O production toward nitrifier denitrification, coupled nitrification–denitrification, and heterotrophic denitrification, with the strongest shift under PLA-MPs. These results demonstrate PLA-MPs pose greater N2O emission risks than PE-MPs, biodegradability does not necessarily imply environmental safety.

title: Construction and application of a mouth level exposure assessment system for harmful constituents in cigarette and heated tobacco products
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Minhui Cui, Ge Zhao, Sheng Wang, Bing Wang, Kejian Liu, Jingjing Yu, Chengjie Ma, Yu Liu, Yaqiong Qin, Junwei Guo, Hongbo Wang, Junlan Cai, Quanping Yan, Fuwei Xie
abstract: Smokers' actual exposure to harmful constituents is critical for assessing tobacco product health risks. This study established a mouth level exposure (MLE) method using nicotine and solanesol as filter markers to evaluate constituent exposure among Chinese users of regular cigarettes (RC), slim cigarettes (SC), and heated tobacco products (HTP). Twenty-eight constituents, including HTP-specific propylene glycol, glycerol, chloropropanols, and glycidol, were selected. In RC and SC, nicotine and solanesol perform differently across constituents, requiring constituent-specific marker selection. Filter nicotine is superior for HTPs, predicting all constituents (R² ≥ 0.86). The equations differ among product types (P < 0.0001) and are not interchangeable. Relative to RC users, SC users show 20%–50% lower daily MLE for most constituents. HTP users exhibite the lowest constituent exposure, with formaldehyde, crotonaldehyde, acrolein, phenol, and HCN daily MLE reduced by over 90% relative to RC. This reduction primarily reflects lower constituent release from HTPs. HTP-specific constituents are first quantified, with daily exposures of propylene glycol 20.9 ± 12.7 mg, 3-MCPD 93.9 ± 57.0 μg, and glycidol 46.3 ± 28.0 μg, warranting attention to potential health risks. The developed MLE equations provide a tool for comparative risk assessment and regulatory evaluation based on actual exposure.

title: Detoxification-associated polyvinyl chloride micro- and nanoplastics clearance and liver metabolomic responses in mice
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Hongying Gao, Zehua Xu, Jing Li, Yu Gao, Jierong Zheng, Miaomiao Ren, Yiyang Duan, Jiarui Li, Hao Chang, Guiying Liu, Heng Wang, Liangpo Liu, Heqing Shen
abstract: Aged PVC (A-PVC) exhibits distinct surface chemistry from original PVC that may result in different toxicokinetic and toxicodynamic behaviors, yet relevant evidence remains limited. This study investigated the tissue distribution, excretion kinetics and liver metabolic responses of PVC and its debris A-PVC in C57BL/6J mice following acute oral exposure. Py-GC/QTOF measurement revealed that both particles rapidly accumulated in major organs of liver, spleen, heart and lung, and that the particle burdens in the measured organs declined substantially by 72 h, which was further verified by the multiple imaging analysis. Although histopathological and biochemical alterations gradually attenuated during recovery, small A-PVC elicited more severe acute biological responses, whereas large original PVC produced relatively sustained toxic effects characterized by oxidative stress, inflammation and endocrine disruption. These findings highlight aging-associated alterations in the kinetic behavior of PVC MNPs. Notably, the organ specific clearance patterns of 300–1300 nm aged PVC are consistent with a hypothesized non-biliary intestinal excretion pathway, which warrants further verification.

title: Widespread antibiotic resistance and multidrug resistance in Escherichia coli from surface waters near dairies and a calf ranch in Wisconsin: Implications for hotspot screening and multi-method monitoring
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): K.P. Osborn, Y. Zhang, S. Ray, Y. Kong, S. Levy, S. Jun, M. Chang, J. Lin, J. Vuong, C. Ives, A. Jones, L. Henning, C. Dickerson, S. Mahendra, W. Bodeau, A. Casillas, R. Chowdhry, J. Chung, N. Curristan, A. Espinoza
abstract: Although concentrated animal feeding operations (CAFOs) are known sources of antimicrobial resistance (AMR), gaps remain regarding AMR dissemination to environments and monitoring methods. Impacts of large dairies and a calf ranch in Wisconsin on the environmental resistome were assessed at nine surface water sites near CAFOs and two nearby unimpaired sites. 1297 Escherichia coli (EC) isolates were tested against a suite of antibiotics by Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion. Up to 68% of EC isolates at dairy-impacted sites and 70% downstream of the calf ranch exhibited multidrug resistance (MDR), versus up to 8% at the unimpaired sites. Fecal indicator bacteria kits modified with antibiotics detected elevated extended-spectrum beta-lactamase-producing (ESBL) EC at the site exhibiting highest MDR, suggesting use as a screening tool. Metagenomic analysis showed elevated antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs), abundance, diversity, and human health risk scores at the calf ranch-impacted site. Follow-up sampling just upstream and downstream of the calf ranch showed dramatic increases in multiple measures, indicating calf ranches may warrant additional monitoring and elucidate more complex processes such horizontal gene transfer. Culture-based results revealed pronounced AMR hotspots and differences among sampling events only partially reflected by metagenomic analysis and a limited quantitative PCR (qPCR) panel, underscoring the importance of monitoring through complementary methods.

title: Tire-derived 6PPD-quinone promotes conjugative gene transfer through respiratory bioenergetic perturbation
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Biao Yang, Chuang Tan, Yuquan Peng, Qiurong Zhang
abstract: Tire-derived N-(1,3-dimethylbutyl)-N′-phenyl-p-phenylenediamine quinone (6PPD-Q) is transported by roadway runoff into urban waters, yet its sublethal effects on microbial gene exchange remain poorly resolved. Here, 5 μg/L 6PPD-Q increased the transconjugant fraction from 0.25% to 0.65% in a lake-water enriched biofilm community and enhanced plasmid transfer in a defined donor–recipient system. Relative to its parent compound 6PPD, 6PPD-Q more strongly altered oxidative phosphorylation, ATP/ADP ratios, and NAD+/NADH balance. Molecular simulations indicated membrane partitioning and predicted quinone-site interactions resembling those of ubiquinone analogues, while cyclic voltammetry and partial growth rescue of a ubiB-deficient strain supported quinone-associated redox activity. 6PPD-Q also increased succinate dehydrogenase activity, oxygen consumption, membrane potential, and ATP/ADP ratios. Respiratory-chain and bioenergetic inhibitors attenuated both these responses and the transfer enhancement, linking the phenotype to cellular energy metabolism. Extracellular filament-like structures, migration responses, and appendage-related transcription changed concurrently, although the structures could not be assigned to a specific pilus system. These results support respiratory bioenergetic perturbation as an upstream contributor to 6PPD-Q-enhanced conjugation and identify microbial gene exchange as a water-quality endpoint relevant to tire-contaminated runoff and receiving waters.

title: Abundance and characterization of microplastics in milk and dairy milk products with a special emphasis on possible health risk assessment: A global systematic review
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Dimple Dimple, Ruby Ruby, Arup Giri
abstract: The presence of microplastics (MPs) in food products has attracted widespread global attention because of concerns about their potential adverse effects on human health. This study synthesises published data on MPs in milk and dairy products, incorporates a comparative analysis across multiple countries and assesses potential health risks from MPs exposure through dairy consumption. In addition, methodological heterogeneity among the included studies was quantitatively evaluated by examining the effects of analytical techniques, minimum particle-size detection thresholds, and digestion protocols on the reported MP concentrations. The findings demonstrated that MPs concentrations in milk and dairy products ranged from 6 particles/L to approximately 20,200 particles/L. Methodological heterogeneity analysis demonstrated that analytical sensitivity and digestion protocols significantly contributed to inter-study variability, whereas differences among the principal analytical techniques were not statistically significant. Morphological characterisation revealed that fibers and fragments were the dominant forms in the milk matrices. An exposure assessment indicated that children are the most vulnerable population group for infant milk powder (827.75 particles/kg) and human breast milk (1828.92 particles/L) exposure. The MPs contamination factor (MCF) values across all countries and milk and dairy milk matrices predominantly fell within Category IV, corresponding to a very high contamination level classification. However, in packaged milk, countries such as Mexico and Ecuador were categorised within a comparatively lower, yet still significant contamination level. Notably, the microplastic load index (MPLI) values were highest in infant milk powder, followed by those in breast milk and packaged milk. This study provides a comprehensive evaluation of MPs occurrence, methodological heterogeneity, contamination severity, and dietary exposure through milk and dairy products, thereby providing evidence to support policymakers, food safety authorities, and public health initiatives aimed at reducing MPs contamination. Furthermore, the findings align with global sustainability goals, particularly SDG 2 (Zero hunger), SDG 3 (Good health and well-being), SDG 12 (Responsible consumption and production), and SDG 15 (Life on Land).

title: Engineering FAST-PETase with enhanced catalytic efficiency and acidic adaptability for sustainable PET waste recycling
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Haiquan Yang, Yiru Liu, Zhixing Shen, Yu Cao, Wei Shen, Yuanyuan Xia, Li Zhou, Xianzhong Chen
abstract: This study presented a comprehensive protein engineering strategy to enhance the catalytic efficiency and environmental adaptability of FAST-PETase for PET plastic degradation. Through systematic site-directed mutagenesis of key basic residues (Arg84, Arg117, and Lys227) surrounding the active site, we identified R84D as the optimal single mutant, exhibiting 2.1-fold higher activity than FAST-PETase. Iterative saturation mutagenesis at 19 targeted positions yielded the quadruple mutant R84D/A203T/S230K/E198Q, demonstrating superior kinetic parameters: 3.3-fold higher catalytic efficiency (k cat/K m = 10.8 L·mmol−1·min−1) and significantly improved substrate affinity (K m = 72.6 mM) at acidic conditions. Structural characterization revealed this mutant’s optimized active site geometry, featuring enhanced hydrogen bonding and hydrophobic interactions. It exhibited broad pH adaptability (maintaining >80% activity at pH 7.59.0) with a 0.5-unit acidic shift in optimal pH (7.5 vs wild-type’s 8.0), while retaining thermal stability up to 50°C. Molecular dynamics simulations confirmed the mutant’s enhanced structural rigidity, with 3050% lower RMSD values compared to FAST-PETase. When tested in a two-module reactor system, the quintuple mutant R84D/A203T/S230K/E198Q/S239V enabled efficient PET conversion to TPA, achieving a space-time conversion rate of 3.51 g·(L·h)−1. These results demonstrated its practical potential for industrial application. It established an effective framework for engineering plastic-degrading enzymes with enhanced performance under industrially relevant conditions.

title: Abnormal electron-donation-dependent sulfite activation in the Mn(II)-nitrilotriacetic acid system: QSAR and mechanistic insights
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Yanchanjuan Yang, Xinglian Qin, Pengli Zhang, Jiayu Wu, Shuaiqi Zhao, Xiuying Liu, Aihua Xu, Xiaoxia Li
abstract: In advanced oxidation processes (AOPs), electron-rich contaminants are generally susceptible to oxidation by reactive species. Herein, an unusual substrate-selective degradation was observed in sulfite (Na2SO3) based AOPs with the Mn(II)-nitrilotriacetic acid (NTA) complex. The strong electron-rich phenolics were hardly degraded, whereas electron-deficient phenols were efficiently removed. An asymmetric volcano-shaped correlation between the degradation rates and Hammett constants σ+ was established via quantitative structure-activity relationship analysis and can be expanded to antibiotics and dyes with anodic peak potential as a descriptor. Mechanistic investigations demonstrate that electron-rich phenolics complex with Mn(II)-NTA, suppressing O2-driven Mn(III)-NTA formation and thus limiting Mn(V)-NTA accumulation, with a slow radical chain reaction for Na2SO3 oxidation. In contrast, electron-deficient substrates promote Mn(III)-NTA generation, fast Na2SO3 oxidation and transformation to peroxymonosulfate (PMS), and subsequent Mn(V)-NTA formation. Consequently, radical pathways participate in the degradation of electron-rich pollutants, whereas Mn(V)-NTA governs the oxidation of electron-deficient ones. The low-cost Na2SO3 system shows comparable or superior performance to PMS-based systems for electron-deficient pollutants, highlighting its economic viability. These findings underscore the importance of pollutant-catalyst interactions in AOPs and provide mechanistic insights for targeted contaminant remediation.

title: Ultrasensitive and selective rGO QDs modified flower-like Bi 2 S 3 /Bi 2 O 3 heterostructures for room-temperature trace NO 2 detection
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Yongjiao Sun, Wenchang Zhao, Xiaohong Wu, Zhenting Zhao, Wenda Wang, Wendong Zhang, Koichi Suematsu, Jie Hu
abstract: Nitrogen dioxide (NO2) is a ubiquitous ambient pollutant, and chronic exposure to NO2, even at relatively low concentrations, has been associated with sustained adverse effects on multiple organ systems. Bismuth sulfide offers a promising platform for room-temperature gas sensing, yet its practical use is curtailed by poor charge-transfer efficiency and sparse interfacial active sites. In this study, reduced graphene oxide quantum dots (rGO QDs) modified Bi2S3/Bi2O3 composites with abundant p-n heterojunctions were fabricated and used for NO2 detection. The effects of annealing temperature and the amount of rGO on sensor performance were investigated, revealing optimal results for 0.5 wt% rGO modified Bi2S3 annealed at 150℃ (rGO0.5-Bi2S3/Bi2O3-2). The rGO0.5-Bi2S3/Bi2O3-2 sensor exhibited a high response of 36.95 toward 500 ppb NO2 at room temperature (RT). Experimental results demonstrated theoretical and experimental detection limits (LODs) of 0.6 ppb and 50 ppb for NO2 respectively, as well as excellent selectivity, anti-interference ability, good repeatability, and long-term stability. By combining band structure alignments analysis with density functional theory (DFT) calculations, the mechanism underlying the enhanced NO2 detection performance was elucidated, revealing a synergistic effect of the heterojunction interface modulation between components and rGO-promoted charge transfer.

title: From manure to fertilizer in minutes: Radical induced humification and decontamination
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Tao Zhang, Yanping Zhu, Pengjin Zhu, Junxiang Yang, Kaili Li, Yajuan Li, Yongle Yu, Cun Jiang, Guangpeng Wang, Xiuping Zhan, Chunhuo Zhou, Xin Yin, Guorong Ni, Naiqin Zhong, Pan Zhao, Shihu Shu, Dongfang Wang, Dongqing Cai
abstract: Global livestock/poultry manure output (approximately 13 billion tons/year) poses a major sustainability challenge. Conventional recycling via composting and anaerobic digestion after solid-liquid separation is slow (20–60 d) and inefficient at removing pollutants (i.e. pathogens, antibiotics, and heavy metals). This study develops a minute-scale, one-step process using microwave and FeSO₄ to activate persulfate, generating radicals that rapidly convert chicken manure into a fertilizer rich in fulvic-like acids (41.7 wt% on a dry-product basis) and nutrients, including K (a primary nutrient) and Fe (a micronutrient). It simultaneously inactivates culturable bacteria, achieves approximately 99% removal of the parent antibiotics, reduces the combined acid-extractable and reducible fractions of Cd, Cu, and As by approximately 90%, and reduces odors (>97%). Carbon and nitrogen losses, calculated on an absolute-mass basis, were 15.6% and 12.6%, respectively. In a 21-day pot experiment, the fertilizer increased the fresh biomass of pak choi seedlings by 214.3% compared with the unamended soil control (Blank), while increasing soil total potassium and available nitrogen and potassium. This process shows cost (201 RMB/t wet CMPFM) advantage compared with composting, offering an efficient green alternative for manure recycling and circular agriculture.

title: Associations of particulate matter-associated microbial profiles with lung and intestinal microbiomes in healthy mice
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Abubakar Zakari, Yu-Hsiang Chen, Po-Jui Chen, Syue-Wei Peng, Shu-Chi Lan, Yu-Syuan Shih, Ta-Chih Hsiao, Kian Fan Chung, Kai-Jen Chuang, Jer-Hwa Chang, Kai Hsien Chi, Hsiao-Chi Chuang
abstract: Ambient air pollution has detrimental effects on human health. We investigated exposure-related differences and microbial overlap among PM₁, lung, and gut microbiomes in mice exposed to PM₁, high-efficiency particulate air (HEPA)-filtered air, or clean air. PM₁ was characterized for soluble ions, metals, carbonaceous fractions, and oxidative potential, while gaseous pollutants data were obtained from air-quality monitoring stations. PM₁, lung, and gut microbiomes were analyzed using 16S rRNA sequencing, and short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) were quantified by gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (GC-MS). Proteobacteria was the dominant phylum in PM₁. PM₁ contained diverse chemical constituents, including soluble ions, metals, and oxidative species. Lung microbial diversity remained largely unchanged, whereas the gut microbiome was significantly altered. Compared with control, the PM₁ group showed reduced Actinobacteriota and Bacteroidota, while Campylobacterota and Patescibacteria decreased in both HEPA and PM₁ groups. Verrucomicrobiota increased in the HEPA group, and Proteobacteria increased in the PM₁ group compared with both HEPA and control groups. Correlation analyses identified associations between lung and gut microbiomes, environmental variables, PM₁ characteristics, gaseous pollutants, and SCFAs. Eleven bacterial families and six genera overlapped among PM₁, lung, and gut microbiomes in the PM₁ group. Overall, ambient air pollution was associated with gut dysbiosis in mice.

title: Distribution patterns of PFASs in intertidal sediments and the effects on reductive dehalogenating bacteria: A nationwide study in China
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Xingyu Zhu, Heng Wang, Shuo Li, Lingfang Ni, Yuan Li, Dongdong Zhang
abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFASs) are of great concern because of their environmental persistence. The intertidal zone sequesters various halogenated organic pollutants (HOPs) in sediments. Microbial reductive dehalogenation is crucial for HOPs detoxification. However, the nationwide distribution characteristics of PFASs in intertidal sediments and their impact on reductive dehalogenators (RDGs) remain poorly understood. We investigated PFAS distribution profiles in 128 intertidal sediments across China and analyzed their impact on potential RDGs. Sedimentary PFAS concentrations ranged 0.049–2.58 ng/g, with legacy PFASs being dominant. Amplicon sequencing and Spearman rank correlation analysis revealed positive correlation between total organic halogens and relative abundance and/or α-diversity of Anaerolineae and Desulfobacterota (p < 0.05), whereas no correlation was observed for Dehalococcoidia. Despite low ecological risks, Cl-PFESAs showed significant negative correlations with their relative abundance and α-diversity. Cl-PFESAs negatively correlated with abundance of the module associated with elemental cycles (p < 0.05), rather than those linked to organohalide utilization in the co-occurrence network. Microbial cultivation and metagenomic analysis reinforced the crucial role of Desulfobacterota and Anaerolineae in intertidal microbial dehalogenation and the negligible effect of 6:2 Cl-PFESA (0.1 mg/L) on reductive dehalogenating activity. This study provides critical insights into bioremediation strategies for HOPs in intertidal zones co-contaminated with PFASs.

title: Simultaneous nutrient and PAH removal from municipal secondary effluent in pilot-scale open algal raceway ponds: Effects of hydraulic retention time and multi-trophic microbial succession
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Yanyan Yang, Ronghao Qiao, Chao Chang, Songqi Yang, Ming Li
abstract: Algal raceway ponds (ARPs) are considered one of the most promising technologies for the advanced treatment of wastewater treatment plant (WWTP) effluents. In this study, three parallel pilot-scale open ARPs, each assigned to one hydraulic retention time (HRT, 2, 3, or 4 d), were continuously operated for 52 d to assess nutrient and PAH removal, PAH partitioning, and microbial community succession. The 3-d system provided the most favorable observed balance between pond biomass accumulation and pollutant removal, with the highest mean pond biomass concentration (704 mg L−1 (dw)) and mean removal efficiencies of 86.52%, 95.18%, 67.74%, 91.81%, and 73.68% for TN, TP, NH4 +-N, NO3 −-N, and Σ16PAH, respectively. Daily biomass harvesting was highest at 2 d (14.9 g m−2 d−1 (dw)). At the 3-d HRT, the mean removal efficiencies of low-molecular-weight (LMW) and high-molecular-weight (HMW) PAHs were 74.39% and 69.61%, respectively. Distinct microbial assemblages developed in the ARPs, with Golenkinia predominating among microalgal genera, Pseudomonadota among bacterial phyla, and Cercozoa among protozoan phyla. Exploratory association analyses revealed that LMW-PAH removal showed positive directional relationships with OD680 and microalgal diversity, whereas HMW-PAH removal showed predominantly negative relationships with physiological, nutrient-removal, and community indicators. Phase-distribution analysis further showed that HMW-PAHs were enriched in harvested biomass and that logKd increased with logKow. Aqueous BaP-equivalent concentrations were lower in the effluents than in the influent, and incremental lifetime cancer risk estimates for harvested biomass were below 10−6 under the specified adult incidental-ingestion scenario. These findings support the engineering application of open ARP systems for advanced treatment of WWTP effluent.

title: Agricultural impacts reshape the distribution and future potential health risks of soil heavy metals across global wheat-growing regions under interactive climate–socioeconomic influences
description: Publication date: 1 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 518 Author(s): Feng Zhang, Fasih Ullah Haider, Peng Mu, Bingxue Zhu, Yuan Gao, Tong Lin, Fulai Liu, Miao Jiang, Muhammad Farooq, Marian Brestic, Franciszek Janowiak, Kadambot H.M. Siddique, Xiangnan Li
abstract: Soil heavy metal(loid) pollution poses a critical threat to ecosystem health and sustainability. However, it remains unclear whether agricultural activities have systematically altered their distribution across global wheat-growing regions. Here, we collected paired soil samples from cropland and adjacent non-cropland sites across global wheat-growing regions on six continents to evaluate concentration differences and potential drivers for six heavy metal(loid)s—arsenic (As), nickel (Ni), cadmium (Cd), lead (Pb), antimony (Sb), and chromium (Cr).
